<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->
In the recent study one participant started a local workspace session. Once they were done with that they started working on a cloud repo but reused the session. As a result, while the agent was able to read and write to the cloud repo, the file list was not updated with the new context. This meant that it was difficult for the participant to see new files that were created or browse the files that had been modified. Also, the agent committed directly to main, rather than creating a PR.

Description:
While using GitHub Copilot in VS Code, I encountered a RangeError: Invalid string length during session serialization. The error occurs when VS Code attempts to save the Copilot chat session, which prevents the session from being stored. If the VS Code window is closed, the chat session is lost.
Error Trace:
RangeError: Invalid string length
    at JSON.stringify (<anonymous>)
    at i6.write (vscode-file://vscode-app/resources/app/out/vs/workbench/workbench.desktop.main.js:3003:914)
    at Xoe.writeSession (vscode-file://vscode-app/resources/app/out/vs/workbench/workbench.desktop.main.js:3005:12241)
    at vscode-file://vscode-app/resources/app/out/vs/workbench/workbench.desktop.main.js:3005:9202
    at Array.map (<anonymous>)
    at vscode-file://vscode-app/resources/app/out/vs/workbench/workbench.desktop.main.js:3005:9190

Steps to Reproduce:

Open VS Code with the GitHub Copilot extension installed.
Start a Copilot chat session and interact with it, potentially generating a large or long conversation.
Observe that closing or saving the session triggers the Invalid string length error.

Expected Behavior:
Copilot chat sessions should be serialized and stored without errors, regardless of session size.

Actual Behavior:
Large chat sessions cause a serialization error and cannot be saved.

Additional Notes:

The issue appears specific to Copilot; disabling other extensions does not prevent it.
Restarting VS Code or clearing session cache temporarily resolves the issue.
Likely related to JSON.stringify failing on very large session data.

VS Code Version: [1.119.0]
OS Version: [Windows_NT x64 10.0.26200]
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled? No

Type: Bug Background: - VS Code has a feature called 'Sticky Scroll' which pins the current code scope (function names etc.) to the top of the editor pane while scrolled, giving users the ability to quickly see which section of code they're in even when scrolled deep into a function. - VS Code has a Find Bar feature (opened on Windows via CTRL+F). When the UI is maximized, the Find Bar, when open, appears at the top-right of the editor pane, offset a half-row height below the Sticky Scroll function name. The Issue: When the VS Code window is resized horizontally, such as for a split-screen layout, depending on the width of the resized interface and the editing pane's zoom setting, the Find Bar may encroach and partially obscure the Sticky Scroll function name. (Screenshots to follow) Suggested fix: Ensure that the Find Bar does not overlap the Sticky Scroll text. This could either be achieved by increasing the Find Bar's default distance from the top of the editing pane or by detecting an overlap condition and moving it below the Sticky Scroll text when needed. The Issue: When the VS Code window is resized horizontally, such as for a split-screen layout, depending on the width of the resized interface and the editing pane's zoom setting, the Find Bar may encroach and partially obscure the Sticky Scroll function name. (Screenshots to follow) Suggested fix: Ensure that the Find Bar does not overlap the Sticky Scroll text. This could either be achieved by increasing the Find Bar's default distance from the top of the editing pane or by detecting an overlap condition and moving it below the Sticky Scroll text when needed. ### Type of Issue

Bug

### Description

Until recently, switching sessions using the picker on the left side of the Agents Window updated the terminal to show the terminal associated with the newly selected session. This no longer happens: after switching sessions, the terminal continues to show the stale terminal from the previously selected session.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open the Agents Window with at least two sessions that have terminals.
2. Select one session using the picker on the left.
3. Switch to another session using the same picker.

### Expected Behavior

The terminal updates to show the terminal associated with the newly selected session.

### Actual Behavior

The terminal continues to show the stale terminal from the previously selected session.

### Regression

This worked until recently.

> [!NOTE]
> Planning follow-up. This issue tracks documentation architecture and generated-reference work; it does not propose changing the current design-token values.

## Problem

VS Code's `.github` instructions and skills intentionally provide different levels of context, but mutable facts are currently copied across several artifacts. Token values, allowed scales, role counts, snap rules, and examples can drift when one copy changes without all of the others.

Recent work in #335346 exposed the maintenance cost: changing the proposed icon-size vocabulary required updates in several documents and still left the auto-applied design-philosophy instruction describing the previous two-size model.

Existing examples show that this is broader than one PR:

- `.github/skills/ux-css-layout/SKILL.md` duplicates most of the detailed design-token tables while calling another file canonical and asking maintainers to keep the copy in sync.
- `.github/skills/ux-theming/SKILL.md` describes `padding: 8px 12px` as off-scale while the design-token instruction uses it as an on-scale example.
- The design-token instruction contains both "use the token variable wherever one exists" and "on-scale raw pixels are fine," leaving the intended review policy ambiguous.
- Runtime registrations, stylelint scales, known-variable lists, tests, instructions, and skills each contain overlapping representations of the same token families.

## Desired ownership

Use one source of truth for each kind of information:

| Information | Owner |
|---|---|
| Current token IDs, values, families, and concise descriptions | Machine-readable runtime data |
| Registration, emitted CSS names, validation, and generated references | Derived from the machine-readable data where layering permits |
| Design values and role-selection rationale | Design-philosophy guidance |
| Layout and composition techniques | CSS-layout guidance |
| Color, high-contrast, and focus behavior | Theming guidance |
| Always-loaded reminders | Short path-scoped instructions that route to the relevant source or skill |

Instructions and skills may repeat stable principles for routing and independent context, but should not manually enumerate mutable token tables or counts. If a complete human-readable token reference is useful, generate it from the machine-readable source and verify it in CI.

## Proposed investigation

1. Inventory duplicated mutable facts across `.github/instructions`, `.github/skills`, runtime registries, validators, tests, and known-variable data.
2. Decide whether `baseSizes.ts` can be the shared machine-readable source or whether a lower-level manifest is needed for build/runtime layering.
3. Derive registration, validation scales, known CSS variable names, and generated reference material where practical.
4. Reduce auto-applied instructions to stable guardrails and routing.
5. Remove detailed token-table mirrors from skills; retain decision logic and representative examples.
6. Add focused drift checks for any projections that must remain duplicated.
7. Clarify whether raw on-scale values are allowed or whether token variables are required.

## Non-goals

- Changing token values as part of the documentation cleanup.
- Requiring every skill to load every other skill.
- Eliminating all repetition; compact stable invariants can remain where independent context is important.
- Adding brittle full-prose snapshot tests.

## Acceptance criteria

- A documented ownership map exists for the affected instructions, skills, and runtime data.
- Current token IDs and values have one machine-readable source of truth.
- Exhaustive Markdown tables are removed or generated rather than manually synchronized.
- Auto-applied instructions do not snapshot mutable counts such as the number of icon-size roles.
- Known contradictions are resolved.
- CI detects drift for any generated or intentionally mirrored token data.

## Related

- #335354 - Predictable UI composition umbrella proposal
- #335346 - Candidate authoring-guidance PR that exposed the drift

The **Agent Customizations > Tools** page does not indicate which agent its tool configuration applies to. It is unclear whether the listed tools are for the default agent or for the partner agent currently selected in the chat picker.

The equivalent Harness customization reflects the selected harness, so I expected agent tool customization to behave the same way.

**Expected**

The page should clearly identify the agent whose tools are being configured and, if applicable, update when the selected agent changes.

body_text:
> [!NOTE]
> Planning follow-up. This proposes a lightweight authoring and review principle, not a requirement to copy existing UI, a broad migration, or an automatic lint rule.

## Problem

VS Code is built by many teams across old and new UI generations. When adding or changing a visual or interaction pattern, two opposite failure modes are possible:

1. **Unnecessary invention:** a new local treatment is slightly different from an equivalent existing experience. Each difference adds customer learning load and creates another implementation to maintain.
2. **Blind reuse:** an existing implementation is treated as authoritative even when it is legacy, accidental, inaccessible, inconsistent with current design direction, or simply wrong for the new user need.

Current guidance says to reuse components and follow shared design ramps, but it does not provide a repeatable way to evaluate prior art, distinguish stable conventions from historical accidents, or explain when divergence is justified.

Recent work on #335583 illustrates both sides. Reusing the existing GitHub hover components avoided a new card language, but a broader comparison still found inherited choices that should not be propagated unchanged: an outdated title hierarchy, duplicate boundary padding, an unnecessary divider, and submenu chrome that differed from the standard popup containing it.

## Proposed principle

> **Consistency by default, intentional divergence.** Before introducing or changing a visual or interaction pattern, identify the closest analogous experiences and canonical guidance. Reuse shared semantics, behavior, and component contracts when their roles match, because unnecessary variation increases customer learning load. Treat existing implementations as evidence, not authority: do not preserve known debt, deprecated patterns, accessibility problems, or accidental styling. Diverge when a clear user need, accessibility requirement, simplification, or current design direction calls for it; make the reason explicit and decide whether the shared owner should evolve.

The goal is familiarity without stagnation: like things should behave alike unless a difference does useful work.

## Suggested lightweight workflow

For UI work, proportionate to the size and risk of the change:

1. **Name the role and user task.** Compare surfaces that serve the same purpose, not merely elements that look similar.
2. **Inspect representative prior art and canonical guidance.** Prefer shared primitives, current design guidance, and actively maintained/recently accepted surfaces over an isolated historical example.
3. **Separate invariants from accidents.** Identify which semantics, interactions, accessibility behavior, ownership boundaries, and visual roles should stay consistent; do not copy incidental DOM or CSS.
4. **Classify the decision.** State what is reused, adapted, or new. For a small change this can be implicit in the diff or review description; larger explorations may benefit from a short provenance table.
5. **Justify divergence.** A new treatment should answer an unmet user need, remove complexity, improve accessibility, or advance an accepted design direction—not exist only because it was easy to implement locally.
6. **Choose the right owner.** If the improved behavior should apply to equivalent surfaces, evolve the shared component or contract when there is demonstrated production need. Otherwise keep a clearly scoped local exception.
7. **Validate equivalent scenarios.** Use production components and focused fixtures where useful; check the relevant density, theme, keyboard, and accessibility states rather than validating only the new happy path.

## Resolving conflicting prior art

Existing code will often disagree. Use this evidence order as a review heuristic, not a mechanical ranking:

1. Accepted canonical design/accessibility guidance and explicit component contracts.
2. Shared primitives and actively maintained, recently reviewed comparable surfaces.
3. Local conventions in the feature area, when they do not conflict with the above.
4. Isolated legacy implementations, which are useful evidence but not precedent by default.

When no direction is clearly established, preserve behavior for narrow maintenance work and surface the uncertainty. For a genuinely new pattern, seek product/design input rather than selecting whichever old example is easiest to copy.

## Guardrails

- Do not require exhaustive repository archaeology or a fixed number of examples.
- Do not make “most common” or “oldest” synonymous with correct.
- Do not force reuse, inheritance, or a shared abstraction when roles differ.
- Finding a related component does not imply it must be extended; a documented no-reuse conclusion is valid.
- Do not block experiments. Treat them as explicit experiments, keep them scoped, and use what is learned to decide whether a pattern should become shared.
- Do not require competitor research for routine UI changes.
- Do not duplicate mutable component inventories or token tables across instructions and skills.
- Keep automatic enforcement out of scope until repeated accepted work reveals a precise mechanically checkable rule.

## Guidance placement

Coordinate with #335370's source-of-truth model:

- Add a short stable principle/router to the auto-applied design instruction.
- Keep the detailed workflow, examples, and feedback language in the canonical design-philosophy skill.
- Let layout, theming, accessibility, and component-fixture skills retain their domain-specific techniques rather than repeating this full checklist.

This is broader than #335346's candidate **one relationship, one owner** composition heuristic. That guidance is one example of applying the principle; this issue covers visual and interaction pattern decisions generally.

## Acceptance criteria

- Canonical UI guidance states **consistency by default, intentional divergence** or an equivalent high-level principle.
- Guidance explicitly says existing code is evidence, not authority, and warns against copying legacy or accidental patterns.
- A lightweight, proportional prior-art workflow covers reuse, adaptation, new work, and justified exceptions.
- Guidance protects accessibility improvements, modernization, simplification, necessary product differences, and experimentation.
- The workflow discourages unnecessary local variants and customer learning load without requiring forced abstraction.
- The detailed workflow has one canonical owner and auto-applied instructions remain concise, consistent with #335370.

## Related

- #335354 — predictable UI composition umbrella and guardrails against over-engineering
- #335346 — candidate UI relationship-ownership guidance and prior-art audit example
- #335345 — shared composition-token foundation
- #335370 — instruction/skill source-of-truth and drift reduction
- #335583 — GitHub reference-hover exploration that motivated the broader guidance

body_text: Type: Bug ## Summary Copilot setup cannot be started in VS Code Insiders for the Web. There is no GitHub/Copilot sign-in action in the Accounts menu, and selecting **Use AI Features** from the Copilot status menu tries to execute a command that is not registered. This prevents users who are signed out from enabling AI features in the browser. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Open VS Code Insiders for the Web while signed out of GitHub/Copilot. 2. Open the Accounts menu and look for a GitHub/Copilot sign-in action. 3. Open the Copilot status menu from the Copilot icon in the bottom-right corner. 4. Select **Use AI Features**. ## Actual result The Accounts menu does not provide a way to sign in to GitHub/Copilot. Selecting **Use AI Features** has no visible effect and logs the following error: ```text ERR command 'workbench.action.chat.triggerSetup' not found: Error: command 'workbench.action.chat.triggerSetup' not found at rmt._tryExecuteCommand (workbench.web.main.internal.js:2017:4832) at rmt.executeCommand (workbench.web.main.internal.js:2017:4732) ``` ## Expected result The browser should offer a working GitHub/Copilot sign-in and setup flow. Selecting **Use AI Features** should start that flow instead of invoking an unregistered command. ## Version VS Code Insiders for the Web Commit: `7b7e49c83affacfac726040280da69b4999f3e01` ## Additional information The same `workbench.action.chat.triggerSetup not found` error was previously reported in #254160, but that issue concerned running Code OSS and Copilot Chat from source and was closed as not planned. This report concerns the published VS Code Insiders web build.

<!-- Please keep the environment and diagnostic details below; they are important to this report. -->

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Not applicable. This involves the built-in Agents web UI, VS Code CLI, and Microsoft Dev Tunnels service.

## Environment

- VS Code Insiders CLI: `1.137.0-insider`
- Commit: `b6234bd71943c8a5caf5eef03bc4a8e49aef2698`
- Architecture: `x64`
- Host OS: Bluefin 42 / Fedora Silverblue
- Host kernel: `6.17.4-200.fc42.x86_64`
- Web client: `https://insiders.vscode.dev/agents`
- Agent Host name: `hawks-desktop`
- Active tunnel ID during diagnosis: `jolly-horse-93hm33s.use`
- Active Agent Host protocol label: `protocolv6`

## Summary

An active and healthy Agent Host was omitted by the Agents web app when the associated Dev Tunnels account contained six VS Code launcher tunnels.

Five tunnel records were stale and had zero host connections. The sixth tunnel, `jolly-horse-93hm33s.use` (`hawks-desktop`), had an active host connection and the expected Agent Host labels and port. Despite that, `insiders.vscode.dev/agents` showed `hawks-desktop` as offline or omitted it, while repeatedly attempting WebSocket connections to the stale tunnels.

After permanently deleting the five stale Dev Tunnel records, `hawks-desktop` appeared online and connected immediately on the next page reload. No change to the Agent Host process or systemd service was required.

This suggests that the Agents web discovery path may only be consuming the first page/subset of tunnel records (five in this case), without pagination or without prioritizing tunnels that have active host connections.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Use a GitHub account that owns at least six VS Code Dev Tunnel records.
2. Leave five of those tunnels offline, with `hostConnections: 0`.
3. Start an Agent Host tunnel for the sixth record:

   ```bash
   code-insiders agent host \
     --tunnel \
     --name hawks-desktop \
     --new-instance \
     --foreground
   ```

4. Confirm that the CLI reports the Agent Host as ready:

   ```text
   Visual Studio Code Agent Host v1.137.0 ready
   Tunnel: https://insiders.vscode.dev/agents/tunnel/hawks-desktop
   Server ready
   ```

5. Confirm the active tunnel through the Microsoft `devtunnel` CLI:

   ```bash
   devtunnel show jolly-horse-93hm33s.use --json
   ```

   Relevant fields:

   ```json
   {
     "tunnelId": "jolly-horse-93hm33s.use",
     "labels": [
       "hawks-desktop",
       "protocolv6",
       "vscode-server-launcher",
       "_flag4"
     ],
     "hostConnections": 1,
     "clientConnections": 1,
     "ports": [
       {
   ```

**Summary:**
New regression detected: `timeToFirstToken` in the *long-prose* chat scenario is up ~26% vs baseline (493.32ms ±69.73ms vs 392.03ms ±15.15ms). This is the first run after a baseline reset, so the regression is clear and not previously tracked.

**Evidence:**
- Current: 493.32ms ±69.73ms
- Baseline: 392.03ms ±15.15ms
- Absolute delta: +101.3ms
- Relative delta: +25.8%
- p-value: 0.05 (statistically significant)
- No prior alerts or open issues cover this scenario/metric.
- No baseline window available, but the jump is well beyond typical noise (±15ms previously).
- Recent commits affecting chat/agentHost logic:
  - `d92b683` (merge: chat/agentHost/agentSessions changes)
  - `b2dd4c8` (chat draft input restoration)
  - `1271787` (chat tools/enablement refactor)
  - `33a3fa9` (plan widget/agentHost session handler)
  - `e719715` (agentHost: multiple active clients)
  - `185495a` (agentHostSessionHandler/model usage)
  - `309b5b5` (propagate model list to agent host)
  - `0cf80df` (agentHost: pull request info)

**Suggested action:**
- Investigate recent changes to chat/agentHost session handling and model propagation.
- Review the above SHAs for code affecting token streaming or session initialization.
- If regression confirmed, bisect to isolate culprit and revert/fix as needed.
- Monitor next nightly for persistence or resolution.

body_text:
## Summary

VS Code's Agent Host generates chat URIs by encoding the owning session URI into the path. This conflicts with AHP's documented chat identity model: a chat has a server-allocated identifier, and its relationship to a session is represented in protocol state rather than encoded in its address.

The shared parsing helpers also require this VS Code-specific encoding, so they reject chat URIs that follow the documented AHP form.

This report is based on public source inspection at VS Code commit [`e6bf68e3c8986a3e1c8cc5f36db28e780170793c`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/e6bf68e3c8986a3e1c8cc5f36db28e780170793c), not a new end-to-end runtime reproduction.

## AHP contract

The [Chat Channel specification, URI section](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-host-protocol/blob/296b25e7b698a4a84a0ee5a28d9573e70048a0bf/docs/specification/chat-channel.md#uri) documents `ahp-chat:/<uuid>` and states:

> The path is a server-unique identifier (typically a UUID) allocated by the server when the chat is created. The owning session URI is **not** encoded in the chat URI — the relationship is expressed via the session's `chats` catalog and each chat's `origin`.

The same specification describes `defaultChat` as an optional, advisory routing hint. It does not define a default chat address that clients can calculate from the session URI.

## Current implementation

### 1. Chat identity embeds session identity

[**sessionState.ts — `buildChatUri`**](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/e6bf68e3c8986a3e1c8cc5f36db28e780170793c/src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/state/sessionState.ts#L1171):

```ts
export function buildChatUri(sessionUri: ProtocolURI | ResourceURI, chatId: string): string {
	const session = typeof sessionUri === 'string' ? sessionUri : sessionUri.toString();
	const encoded = encodeBase64(VSBuffer.fromString(session), false, true);
	return `${AHP_CHAT_SCHEME}://${chatId}/${encoded}`;
}
```

This produces `ahp-chat://<chatId>/<base64url(sessionUri)>`. The chat ID is placed in the authority, while the path contains the encoded session URI.

[**sessionState.ts — `buildDefaultChatUri`**](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/e6bf68e3c8986a3e1c8cc5f36db28e780170793c/src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/state/sessionState.ts#L1186):

```ts
export function buildDefaultChatUri(sessionUri: ProtocolURI | ResourceURI): string {
	return buildChatUri(sessionUri, DEFAULT_CHAT_ID);
}
```

[**`AgentHostStateManager._ensureDefaultChat` in agentHostStateManager.ts**](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/e6bf68e3c8986a3e1c8cc5f36db28e780170793c/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostStateManager.ts#L1194) uses that builder, registers the chat, and publishes the resulting address in `SessionState.chats` and `SessionState.defaultChat`.

**Those discovery fields are already populated. The problem is the identity construction, not missing advertisement.**

### 2. Parsing treats the encoding as a requirement

[**`parseChatUri` in sessionState.ts**](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/e6bf68e3c8986a3e1c8cc5f36db28e780170793c/src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/state/sessionState.ts#L1208) requires a nonempty authority and decodes the path to recover the owning session. Consequently, an illustrative AHP-shaped URI such as `ahp-chat:/11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111` is rejected because it has no authority.

[**`parseRequiredSessionUriFromChatUri` in sessionState.ts**](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/e6bf68e3c8986a3e1c8cc5f36db28e780170793c/src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/state/sessionState.ts#L1247) then reports it as `Malformed AHP chat URI`.

## Why this matters

- Host and client code using the same builder can agree with each other while still relying on a convention that AHP explicitly does not define.
- Consumers that reconstruct chat addresses or decode them to discover ownership cannot handle independently allocated chat identities through those paths.
- Changing only the host's URI generator would leave those consumers and restoration paths dependent on the old encoding.

## Expected behavior / proposed scope

- Allocate server-unique chat identifiers without embedding the owning session URI. Apply the same identity model to default, additional, and subagent chats.

The shared parsing helpers also require this VS Code-specific encoding, so they reject chat URIs that follow the documented AHP form.

## AHP contract

The [Chat Channel specification, URI section](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-host-protocol/blob/296b25e7b698a4a84a0ee5a28d9573e70048a0bf/docs/specification/chat-channel.md#uri) documents `ahp-chat:/<uuid>` and states:

> The path is a server-unique identifier (typically a UUID) allocated by the server when the chat is created. The owning session URI is **not** encoded in the chat URI — the relationship is expressed via the session's `chats` catalog and each chat's `origin`.

```ts
export function buildChatUri(sessionUri: ProtocolURI | ResourceURI, chatId: string): string {
	const session = typeof sessionUri === 'string' ? sessionUri : sessionUri.toString();
	const encoded = encodeBase64(VSBuffer.fromString(session), false, true);
	return `${AHP_CHAT_SCHEME}://${chatId}/${encoded}`;
}
```

```ts
export function buildDefaultChatUri(sessionUri: ProtocolURI | ResourceURI): string {
	return buildChatUri(sessionUri, DEFAULT_CHAT_ID);
}
```

[**`AgentHostStateManager._ensureDefaultChat` in agentHostStateManager.ts**](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/e6bf68e3c8986a3e1c8cc5f36db28e780170793c/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostStateManager.ts#L1194) uses that builder, registers the chat, and publishes the resulting address in `SessionState.chats` and `SessionState.defaultChat`.

### Summary
*New regression detected*: Significant increases in `timeToFirstToken` (+29–45%) and `layoutDurationMs` (+21%) in the following chat scenarios: **large-codeblock, long-prose, file-links, thinking-response**. These are well outside the baseline window's normal noise and represent a clear step up from previous runs.

### Evidence
- **large-codeblock**: TTFT 507ms (was 373ms ±18), layoutDurationMs 207ms (was 171ms ±2.8)
- **long-prose**: TTFT 494ms (was 384ms ±13)
- **file-links**: TTFT 552ms (was 382ms ±5.6)
- **thinking-response**: TTFT 535ms (was 397ms ±17)

All are >100ms above the baseline mean and well outside baseline spread.

**Trend:**
- All four metrics show a sharp increase in the current run, after a long period of stability (see baseline window: no similar spikes, no prior regressions).
- The regression is not present in the last 6 baseline runs, all of which were stable.

**Suspect Commits:**
- The regression likely landed between the last baseline and this run. The most suspicious are recent changes touching chat/session/layout logic:
  - 4ccdb71 (sandy081): "sessions: Synchronize live last turn changes" — touches chat/session logic, landed just before this regression.
  - 1e3ed44 (sandy081): "agentHost: Scope server tools to exact chats" — also landed in this window, touches chat/agent logic.

### Suggested Action
- Bisect between the last good baseline and this run, focusing on 4ccdb71 and 1e3ed44 as likely culprits.
- Review changes in chat/session/layout code for performance impact on TTFT/layout.
- Roll back or optimize as needed.

---
**Please triage promptly: these are major regressions in core chat responsiveness.**

**Summary**
First run of chat-perf pipeline: Detected two clear regressions exceeding the 20% threshold, with no prior baseline or open tracking issues covering these metrics/scenarios.

**Evidence**
- *multi-turn-user*: `timeToFirstToken` increased from 196ms ±10.5ms to 296.2ms ±35.12ms (+51.1%, p=0.001)
- *many-small-chunks*: `layoutDurationMs` increased from 139.48ms ±7.98ms to 169.55ms ±7.74ms (+21.6%, p=0)
- Both metrics are well outside typical noise and above regression threshold.
- No prior baseline window available, but absolute jumps and p-values indicate real regressions.
- No open tracking issues or Slack threads cover these scenarios/metrics.

**Suspect Commits**
- Unable to attribute to a specific commit due to lack of baseline history (first run).
- Recent changes affecting chat/session/agentHost code:
  - cb39ed9 (agent host: fix subagent rendering and tools)
  - bcb76ec (populate turn timings for agent-host providers)
  - 6cde2e9 (scope model and agent selection per chat)
  - d2f679c (fix bugs related to setting the right Chat model)

**Suggested Action**
- Open tracking issue for these regressions.
- Monitor next few runs to confirm persistence and begin commit attribution as baseline builds.
- Investigate recent changes in chat/agentHost/session handling for root cause.

### Summary
:rotating_light: New regression detected: `layoutDurationMs` increased by 26.5% in the *text-only* scenario and 33.0% in the *tool-terminal* scenario, both well outside the baseline window's normal spread.

### Evidence
- *text-only*: Baseline 113.96ms ±4.4ms → Current 144.13ms ±3.15ms (+30.17ms, +26.5%)
- *tool-terminal*: Baseline 167.28ms ±1.96ms → Current 222.56ms ±10.84ms (+55.28ms, +33.0%)
- Both metrics were stable in the last 3 baselines (no prior runs near these values).
- No open tracking issue or prior Slack thread covers this regression in these scenarios.

#### Trend (last 3 runs):
- *text-only* layoutDurationMs: 166.3ms → 140.9ms → 144.1ms (current)
- *tool-terminal* layoutDurationMs: 230.8ms → 188.5ms → 222.6ms (current)

### Suspect Commits
- The regression appears after a large set of agent host and chat-related changes, especially `bf87d75` ("Merge pull request #330566 from microsoft/connor4312/agents-enablement-2"), which touched chat session, layout, and agent host logic.

### Suggested Action
- Investigate recent changes to chat layout/session/agent host logic, especially in `bf87d75` and related commits.
- Profile layoutDurationMs in the affected scenarios to identify the cause of the increased layout time.
- Consider reverting or optimizing the relevant changes if a root cause is confirmed.

**Summary:**
New regression detected: layoutDurationMs increased by 21–38% in text-only, tool-terminal, large-codeblock, file-links, thinking-response, and tool-read-file chat scenarios. This is the first run, so no prior baseline exists, but the magnitude and consistency across scenarios indicate a real regression.

**Evidence:**
- *text-only*: 126.34ms ±1.82ms → 166.63ms ±6.81ms (+31.9%)
- *tool-terminal*: 177.62ms ±3.32ms → 220.3ms ±9.02ms (+24.0%)
- *large-codeblock*: 167.31ms ±4.46ms → 216.57ms ±9.64ms (+29.4%)
- *file-links*: 211.82ms ±3.7ms → 261.71ms ±2.17ms (+23.6%)
- *thinking-response*: 154.67ms ±3.84ms → 212.82ms ±6.57ms (+37.6%)
- *tool-read-file*: 213.62ms ±7.18ms → 258.39ms ±4.69ms (+21.0%)

All p-values are 0, indicating high statistical significance.

**Suspect commits:**
- 3b1bd0b (justschen): "make sure layout accounts for agents window padding" — src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/chat.ts, src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatListRenderer.ts, src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatWidget.ts
- aaf5994 (justschen): "fix editor container overflow" — src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/media/chat.css
- 33a3fa9 (justschen): "use plan widget instead of questions carousel when exiting plan mode" — src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/agentHostSessionHandler.ts, src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatListRenderer.ts

**Suggested action:**
- Investigate recent changes to chat widget rendering/layout logic, especially those affecting chatListRenderer, chatWidget, and chat.css.
- Roll back or optimize the affected code to restore layoutDurationMs to prior levels.
- Monitor subsequent nightly runs for confirmation and further trend analysis.

### Summary
:rotating_light: New regression: `layoutDurationMs` increased by 21–47% in 6 chat scenarios (text-only, tool-terminal, many-small-chunks, tool-read-file, multi-turn-user, mixed-content). This is a clear, sudden step outside the prior window's noise, not seen in the last 6 baselines.

### Evidence
- *text-only*: 213.3ms (±2.5) vs baseline 169.4ms (±12.6) — +25.9%
- *tool-terminal*: 316.4ms (±12.1) vs baseline 260.8ms (±15.3) — +21.3%
- *many-small-chunks*: 182.9ms (±2.7) vs baseline 126.6ms (±12.3) — +44.5%
- *tool-read-file*: 208.1ms (±12.0) vs baseline 141.3ms (±10.2) — +47.2%
- *multi-turn-user*: 217.7ms (±15.9) vs baseline 167.0ms (±12.4) — +30.4%
- *mixed-content*: 183.9ms (±4.8) vs baseline 146.6ms (±8.4) — +25.4%

All affected metrics were stable in the previous 6 runs, with no sign of drift or prior outliers. The current values are well outside the baseline spread.

#### Trend
- All affected scenarios show a sudden jump in layoutDurationMs in this run, not a gradual drift.
- No similar regressions reported in prior Slack threads or open issues.

#### Suspect Commits
- The regression appeared in this run, after a long period of stability. The window contains a large batch of merges, but the following are most suspicious due to their direct relevance to chat layout, session, and chat rendering:
  - `5270ba6` (sessions: Stabilize docked side pane sizing, sandy081)
  - `1f3057f` (sessions: Preserve workbench-level pane sizing, sandy081)
  - `4ccdb71` (sessions: Synchronize live last turn changes, sandy081)
  - `38220ea` (Improve agent feedback workflows and persistence, benibenj)
  - `d9a8a27` (Share one model-selection policy between Workbench chat and the Agents Window, lramos15)

### Suggested Action
- Bisect or revert recent changes to chat/session layout and sizing logic, especially those in the above commits. Investigate for accidental extra layout passes or inefficient layout invalidations.
- If a root cause is found, file a PR to address the regression and link this issue.

---
*Please triage and assign to the chat/session layout owners for investigation. This regression is new and not covered by any open tracking issue or prior alert.*

:rotating_light: New regression: layoutDurationMs increased 20–33% in 10 chat scenarios (text-only, tool-terminal, large-codeblock, file-links, thinking-response, many-small-chunks, tool-read-file, multi-turn-user, mixed-content, tool-edit-file). This is a broad and sustained regression not present in the prior 6-night window, which was stable.

### Evidence
- *text-only*: 162.73ms ±8.85ms → 208.3ms ±5.44ms (+28.0%)
- *tool-terminal*: 243.36ms ±6.54ms → 303.7ms ±4.84ms (+24.8%)
- *large-codeblock*: 183.62ms ±9.23ms → 232.4ms ±10.75ms (+26.6%)
- *file-links*: 229.29ms ±3.75ms → 275.43ms ±8.01ms (+20.1%)
- *thinking-response*: 169.14ms ±5.4ms → 225.58ms ±9.06ms (+33.4%)
- *many-small-chunks*: 190.25ms ±12.15ms → 239.69ms ±7.01ms (+26.0%)
- *tool-read-file*: 206.96ms ±8.45ms → 263.85ms ±11.19ms (+27.5%)
- *multi-turn-user*: 220ms ±5.45ms → 277.1ms ±13.65ms (+26.0%)
- *mixed-content*: 134.57ms ±3.51ms → 177.78ms ±8.09ms (+32.1%)
- *tool-edit-file*: 167.21ms ±6.63ms → 201.39ms ±7.85ms (+20.4%)

All p-values = 0 (statistically significant). No similar regressions in the previous 6-night window; all layoutDurationMs changes were within noise or improved.

#### Trend
- The regression is abrupt and present in all scenarios above, not a gradual drift.
- All prior baselines (last 6 runs) show layoutDurationMs within ~10% of previous values; this run jumps 20–33% across the board.

#### Suspect Commits
- Regression window: b10961b (last good) → 64a666e (current)
- 64a666e is a version bump; the bulk of changes are in the preceding commits.
- Several large merges affecting chat/session/layout code landed: e.g., 5270ba6 ("sessions: Stabilize docked side pane sizing"), 1f3057f ("sessions: Preserve workbench-level pane sizing"), 4ccdb71 ("sessions: Synchronize live last turn changes").
- These touch layout/session infrastructure and could plausibly impact layout counts/duration.

### Suggested Action
- Bisect between b10961b and 64a666e, focusing on session/layout-related changes (esp. 5270ba6, 1f3057f, 4ccdb71).
- Review for any changes that could increase layout churn or trigger extra layout passes in chat scenarios.
- Consider reverting or optimizing the responsible change(s) to restore previous layout performance.

## Description

Running **Chat: Install Plugin from Source** from the Command Palette reveals the installed plugin in the legacy Extensions-based Agent Plugins view.

The plugin should instead open in the current Chat Customizations Plugins view, which provides the current plugin details experience.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run **Chat: Install Plugin from Source** from the Command Palette.
2. Install an agent plugin from a repository.
3. Select the installed plugin after VS Code reveals it.

VS Code opens the installed plugin in **Chat Customizations → Plugins**.

**Summary**
First run: layoutDurationMs regressed 23–46% in 7 chat scenarios (tool-terminal, large-codeblock, file-links, thinking-response, tool-read-file, multi-turn-user, mixed-content). No prior tracking issue or Slack thread covers this exact set.

**Evidence**
- tool-terminal: 181.32ms ±9.39ms → 255.08ms ±3.77ms (+40.7%)
- large-codeblock: 124.74ms ±1.31ms → 170.16ms ±14.43ms (+36.4%)
- file-links: 165.64ms ±5.58ms → 215.29ms ±6.26ms (+30.0%)
- thinking-response: 112.87ms ±13.61ms → 165.23ms ±8.63ms (+46.4%)
- tool-read-file: 227.25ms ±10.77ms → 294.2ms ±6.19ms (+29.5%)
- multi-turn-user: 248.12ms ±10.84ms → 306.31ms ±10.98ms (+23.5%)
- mixed-content: 169.68ms ±9.12ms → 224.24ms ±6.82ms (+32.2%)

All are well above the 20% regression threshold. No baseline window exists, so this is the initial reference.

**Suspect Commits**
- This is the first run, so all recent changes are suspect. Many recent merges touch chat widget rendering, agent host, and layout logic:
  - src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatListRenderer.ts
  - src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatWidget.ts
  - src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/agentHostSessionHandler.ts
  - src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/localAgentSessionsController.ts
  - src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/media/chat.css
  - src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/tools/languageModelToolsService.ts
  - src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/tools/toolSetsContribution.ts
  - src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/model/chatModel.ts
  - src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/chatService/chatServiceImpl.ts
  - src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/chatService/chatService.ts
  - src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgentSession.ts
  - src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotSessionLauncher.ts
  - src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/prompts/promptRegistry.ts
  - src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/prompts/toolInstructions.ts
  - src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/claude/claudeAgentSession.ts
  - src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/claude/customizations/claudeSessionCustomizationDiscovery.ts
  - src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/claude/customizations/claudeSessionCustomizationsProjector.ts

**Suggested Action**
- Bisect recent commits affecting chat widget/layout and agent host logic.
- Review changes in chat widget rendering and layout logic for performance regressions.

### Summary
:rotating_light: *New regression*: layoutDurationMs increased by 20–39% in 8 chat scenarios (text-only, tool-terminal, large-codeblock, thinking-response, many-small-chunks, tool-read-file, multi-turn-user, mixed-content) compared to the prior 6-run baseline window. This is a clear, sustained regression outside normal noise.

### Evidence
- *text-only*: 160ms ±9.2ms vs baseline 115.3ms ±4.7ms (+38.8%)
- *tool-terminal*: 221.5ms ±6.8ms vs baseline 163.5ms ±4.3ms (+35.5%)
- *large-codeblock*: 219.2ms ±6.8ms vs baseline 181.8ms ±5.1ms (+20.6%)
- *thinking-response*: 209.5ms ±7.1ms vs baseline 162.5ms ±5.3ms (+28.9%)
- *many-small-chunks*: 237.1ms ±3.7ms vs baseline 196.9ms ±10.2ms (+20.4%)
- *tool-read-file*: 269.7ms ±10.3ms vs baseline 201.8ms ±3.1ms (+33.6%)
- *multi-turn-user*: 286.6ms ±11.6ms vs baseline 225.4ms ±3.9ms (+27.2%)
- *mixed-content*: 212.6ms ±5.6ms vs baseline 172.4ms ±8.3ms (+23.3%)

All are well outside the baseline window's normal spread, and the regression is present in all recent runs (see raw data).

### Trend
- The baseline window (last 6 runs) showed stable layoutDurationMs values in these scenarios, with no prior regressions.
- The current run shows a sharp, consistent jump in all affected scenarios.

### Suspect Commits
- Regression appears in the first run after commit `b10961b` (2026-09-22), with no prior sign in the window. This commit is a large merge with many files, including chat widget and layout code.
- No prior Slack threads or open issues match this multi-scenario regression.

### Suggested Action
- Bisect and investigate changes in/around commit `b10961b` (and its merged PRs) that could impact chat layout performance, especially in chat widget/layout files.
- Consider reverting or optimizing the relevant changes.
- Tag chat perf owners for urgent attention.

## Summary

Follow-up to [#340223](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/340223): review and remove the remaining synchronous filesystem operations whose conversion needs initialization, ordering, or API-contract work.

The PR adds production ESLint enforcement, converts low-risk cases, and excludes designated bootstrap/startup/shutdown files and isolated CLI/askpass processes. Of the **55 covered, explicitly suppressed call sites across 27 files**, this issue tracks the **30 deferred runtime call sites across 16 files** marked with migration TODOs. The other suppressions are not automatically included in this conversion request.

These are source-level findings, not measured regressions. Sync filesystem operations can block unrelated work on the process event loop, especially for larger files or slow/network-backed paths. A suppression is a migration marker, not proof that synchronous I/O is permanently necessary.

## Review candidates and blame-based contacts

Contacts below are **likely reviewers based on Git blame of the actual filesystem-call lines**, not assigned or confirmed owners. Copy/move tracing was used where possible. ## Summary

Follow-up to [#340223](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/340223): review and remove the remaining synchronous filesystem operations whose conversion needs initialization, ordering, or API-contract work.

The PR adds production ESLint enforcement, converts low-risk cases, and excludes designated bootstrap/startup/shutdown files and isolated CLI/askpass processes. Of the **55 covered, explicitly suppressed call sites across 27 files**, this issue tracks the **30 deferred runtime call sites across 16 files** marked with migration TODOs. body_text:
The `copilotSdk/tool_call_executed` telemetry declaration and canvas measurement guidance advertise `invoke_outcome`, with success/error/cancelled/disabledByUser values. The current runtime instead emits the coarse `result_type` field (`SUCCESS` or `FAILURE`), without a fine-grained invocation outcome.

This causes consumers following `src/vs/platform/agentHost/PERFORMANCE.md` to classify recorded tool results as unknown. The unit-test fixtures also currently supply `invoke_outcome`, masking the contract mismatch.

Expected: document and test the emitted `result_type` field; preserve missing/unrecognized results without inventing a fine-grained classification. Remove the unsupported field from the telemetry declaration.

---

This repeats the core managed-plugin coverage from #340992 after the lifecycle moved into the shared standalone runtime.

## Prerequisite

Use a build whose bundled Copilot SDK contains github/copilot-agent-runtime#26059 (`596a4c312a5`). Leave `chat.agentHost.copilot.runtimePath` empty and unset `COPILOT_CLI_PATH` and `COPILOT_LEGACY_CLI_PATH`. Remove any existing device `managed-settings.json`.

## Setup

1. From a VS Code source checkout, run:

   ```sh
   COPILOT_CACHE_HOME="$PWD/.build/mock-policy-cache" npm run mock-policy-server
   ```

2. Open `http://127.0.0.1:3000` > **Setup** > **System proxy**. Apply the shown Map Remote rule, enable the OS proxy, add the shown `http.proxy`, and wait for **Connected**.
3. Launch the signed-in test build:

   ```sh
   COPILOT_E2E_TEST_HOOKS=1 \
   COPILOT_TEST_MANAGED_SETTINGS_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS=3000 \
   COPILOT_CACHE_HOME="$PWD/.build/mock-policy-cache" \
   code-insiders
   ```

4. Open **Chat: Open Customizations** > **Plugins**. If **context-engineering** is installed, uninstall it.

## Install

1. In **Managed Settings**, save:

   ```json
   {
     "extraKnownMarketplaces": {
       "awesome-copilot": {
         "source": { "source": "github", "repo": "github/awesome-copilot" }
       }
     },
     "enabledPlugins": {
       "context-engineering@awesome-copilot": true
     },
     "forceRemoteSettingsRefresh": true
   }
   ```

2. Run **Developer: Sync Account Policy** and confirm a managed-settings request appears under **Live Requests**.
3. Start a new Agents chat, select **Copilot**, and send `Reply with exactly MANAGED_OK.`.
4. Verify managed-plugin progress names `context-engineering@awesome-copilot`, then verify the response is `MANAGED_OK` with no warning.
5. Open **Customizations** > **Plugins**. Verify exactly one **context-engineering** row and a disabled switch indicating that the plugin is managed by the organization.

## Failure and recovery

1. Change `enabledPlugins` to `{ "missing-managed-plugin@awesome-copilot": true }`, sync policy, then send `Reply with exactly FAILURE_OK.` in a new Copilot chat.
2. Verify one warning names `missing-managed-plugin@awesome-copilot` and the response is `FAILURE_OK`.
3. Restore `{ "context-engineering@awesome-copilot": true }`, sync policy, then send `Reply with exactly RECOVERED_OK.` in a new Copilot chat.
4. Verify `RECOVERED_OK`, no new warning, and exactly one **context-engineering** row.

## Cleanup

Save an empty managed policy, sync it, uninstall **context-engineering**, stop the mock server, and disable the OS proxy/Map Remote rule.

New owner: @vritant24

[Create Issue](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/new?template=blank&body=Testing+%23341617%0A%0A&assignees=vritant24)

---

## Prerequisite

1. Use a build whose bundled Copilot SDK contains github/copilot-agent-runtime#26059 (`596a4c312a5`) and #26575 (`8e207264055`). Leave `chat.agentHost.copilot.runtimePath` empty and unset `COPILOT_CLI_PATH` and `COPILOT_LEGACY_CLI_PATH`.
2. Reach out to @digitarald for access to a GitHub test account whose Team assigns `awesome-copilot@awesome-copilot` with state `defaultEnabled`.

## Setup

1. Run **Profiles: New Window with Temporary Profile** and sign in with the assigned account.
2. Open **Chat: Open Customizations** > **Plugins**. If **awesome-copilot** is installed, uninstall it.
3. Open `~/.copilot/settings.json` and remove any `enabledPlugins` entry for `awesome-copilot@awesome-copilot`. Keep the rest of the file unchanged.

## Test

1. Open the Agents window, create a Copilot session, and send `Reply with exactly TEAM_OK.`.
2. Verify the response is `TEAM_OK`; Team preparation is best effort and must not block the response.
3. Within 60 seconds, open **Customizations** > **Plugins** and verify exactly one **awesome-copilot** row appeared without selecting **Install**.
4. Open **Skills**, search `suggest-awesome`, and verify these three skills are loaded:
   - **suggest-awesome-github-copilot-agents**
   - **suggest-awesome-github-copilot-instructions**
   - **suggest-awesome-github-copilot-skills**
5. Toggle **awesome-copilot** off, create another Copilot session, and verify the three skills are no longer loaded.
6. Run **Developer: Reload Window** and verify the plugin remains off; the Team default must not overwrite the explicit opt-out.

## Cleanup

Uninstall **awesome-copilot**, then remove its `enabledPlugins` entry from `~/.copilot/settings.json` so another test starts without an explicit choice.

---

## Prerequisite

Use a build whose bundled Copilot SDK contains github/copilot-agent-runtime#26059 (`596a4c312a5`). Leave `chat.agentHost.copilot.runtimePath` empty and unset `COPILOT_CLI_PATH` and `COPILOT_LEGACY_CLI_PATH`.

## Setup

1. Run **Profiles: New Window with Temporary Profile**.
2. Open **Chat: Open Customizations** > **Plugins**. If **context-engineering** is installed, uninstall it.
3. Create a temporary Git repository containing `.github/copilot/settings.json`:

   ```json
   {
     "extraKnownMarketplaces": {
       "awesome-copilot": {
         "source": { "source": "github", "repo": "github/awesome-copilot" }
       }
     },
     "enabledPlugins": {
       "context-engineering@awesome-copilot": true
     }
   }
   ```

4. Open that repository and choose **Don't Trust** when prompted.

## Test

1. Open **Chat: Open Customizations** > **Plugins**, wait 15 seconds, and verify **context-engineering** was not installed.
2. Run **Workspaces: Manage Workspace Trust**, trust the folder, and reload when prompted.
3. Open the Agents window, create a Copilot session in this repository, and send `Reply with exactly REPO_OK.`.
4. Verify the response is `REPO_OK`.
5. Within 60 seconds, reopen **Customizations** > **Plugins** and verify exactly one **context-engineering** row appeared without selecting **Install**.
6. Open **Skills**, search `context`, and verify **context-map**, **refactor-plan**, and **what-context-needed** are loaded.
7. Open a different empty folder in a new window, start a Copilot session there, and verify those three repository plugin skills are not loaded.

## Cleanup

Uninstall **context-engineering** and delete the temporary repository/profile.

3. Add these User Settings (JSON):

   ```json
   "chat.customizations.migration.enabled": true,
   "chat.plugins.marketplaces": [
     "microsoft/vscode-team-kit"
   ]
   ```

4. Run **Chat: Open Customizations** and open **Migrations**.

## Test

1. Verify a **Plugin Marketplaces** migration appears under the user scope with `vscode-team-kit` selected and `~/.copilot/settings.json` shown as the destination.
2. Select **Migrate...** and verify the confirmation explains that the marketplace will be added to Copilot while the Local agent keeps using the existing VS Code setting.
3. Confirm the migration and verify a success message is shown.
4. Verify the Plugin Marketplaces migration is no longer offered for `vscode-team-kit`.
5. Open the user Copilot settings file and verify `extraKnownMarketplaces` contains an entry for `microsoft/vscode-team-kit`.
6. Reopen User Settings (JSON) and verify `chat.plugins.marketplaces` still contains `microsoft/vscode-team-kit`.
7. Start a new Local agent session and verify the marketplace remains available there.
8. Start a new Copilot agent session and verify the migrated marketplace is available there as well.

## Cleanup

Remove the `vscode-team-kit` entry from both `chat.plugins.marketplaces` and `extraKnownMarketplaces`, then delete the temporary profile.

Explore the redesigned **Compare Models / bake off** workflow end to end: setup, attempts, Judge scorecard, and synthesis.

## Setup

- Use the latest build
- In the Agents window, enable `sessions.chat.compareAgents.enabled` ~and `chat.experimentalModelPicker`.~
- Open the Agents window with a disposable Git repository (with a commit and remote), a worktree-capable Agent Host agent, and multiple fixed models. Configure Copilot, Claude, and Codex where available.
- Runs consume tokens and create worktrees; use a small coding task.

## Areas to cover

- **Setup and picker:** Explore checkboxes, Details, effort variants, optional Judge/Synthesizer, and cancelling/reopening setup. The picker should stay anchored, preserve selections/focus/collapsed groups, and retain model badges and configuration details. Compare the same model at different efforts; configurations must remain distinct and launch correctly. Check composer icons and hover.
- **Execution:** Try small and larger comparisons, including mixed harnesses. Startup should remain responsive; each participant should use the selected harness, effort, and native permissions without inheriting incompatible modes. Empty/unsupported repositories should not offer comparison.
- **Results:** Review the redesigned Judge scorecard, winner, time/tokens, expandable rationale and validation evidence, and links to attempts. Try synthesis. Results and the instructions input should align with chat content and work at narrow widths; missing evidence/no-run states should be clear.
- **Sessions and grids:** Check workspace grouping/capping, long titles, and collapse/expand. Open an unrelated session, switch comparisons, and delete a comparison group: no stale tiles or broken destination. Ordinary multi-session layouts should remain unaffected.
- **Inactive inputs:** With `sessions.chat.compareAgents.hideInactiveInputs` enabled and 3+ comparison panes, only inactive inputs should hide. Keep the active input visible; do not hide inputs in screen-reader mode or unrelated layouts.

Use keyboard and pointer, and spot-check screen-reader behavior, themes, and compact layouts.

Explore **Worktree Cleanup**, focusing on the revised UI, measurement reuse, and responsiveness.

## Setup

- Use the latest 1.143.0 Insiders and the Agents window.
- Use **disposable** repositories/worktrees: cleanup marks sessions Done and removes their worktrees, committing uncommitted changes first.
- Prepare eligible inactive sessions plus some active, pinned, or recent sessions. Include a worktree with many small files if practical.
- Open **Open Worktree Cleanup** from the Command Palette.

## Areas to cover

- **UI and help:** Check the editor title, explanatory copy, compact-width table, empty state, info buttons/hovers, and Alt+F1 help. Eligibility details should open and receive focus from the keyboard. Settings copy should distinguish immediate persistence from background cleanup, and inactivity before Done from additional retention before deletion.
- **Measurement reuse:** Watch the **Measuring agent session worktrees...** progress notification (very fast scans may finish before it appears). Close/reopen during a scan: no duplicate notification. Reopen after completion within an hour, or change **Untouched For**: sizes should be reused without another measurement notification, while eligibility/totals update. Adding a session/worktree or reloading the window should allow fresh measurement. No need to wait an hour for expiry.
- **Cleanup:** Select and clean up disposable eligible worktrees. Newly Done sessions should disappear immediately without remeasuring unchanged remaining worktrees. Protected/unselected worktrees must remain intact.
- **Large scans and suggestions:** Check responsiveness and memory during a large scan; if it times out, the window should recover without continuing runaway background work. With `chat.agentSessions.sessionStorageCleanupSuggestion.enabled`, check automatic/manual scan sharing and suggestion updates after cleanup where observable; no need to manufacture a threshold-sized collection.

Use keyboard and pointer, and spot-check screen-reader descriptions, themes, and surfaced errors.

Refs: #339150, #338708

- [x] anyOS @chryw
- [x] anyOS @dbaeumer

Complexity: 5

Authors: @meganrogge

[Create Issue](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/new?template=blank&body=Testing+%23342070%0A%0A&assignees=meganrogge)

---

Verify the newly merged OpenAI GPT Live BYOK Voice Mode provider and the associated voice lifecycle fixes in regular Chat and the Agents window.

## Setup and cost

- Use the latest 1.143.0 Insiders build containing #339150, with the bundled Copilot extension.
- Enable `agents.voice.enabled`, allow microphone/audio access, and use an account/environment where client BYOK is permitted.
- Add your OpenAI API key through Models Management and set `agents.voice.useBYOKVoiceModel` to an available GPT Live model ID accessible to that key , `gpt-live-1`. Do not put credentials in settings screenshots, logs, or bug reports.
- BYOK sessions consume OpenAI credits. Use short, harmless requests and disposable workspaces. Never approve a destructive tool operation for testing.
- Cover both a regular Chat sidebar/editor and the Agents window, including its new-session welcome composer. Save settings for restoration.

## Connection and failure boundaries

1. Start Voice Mode. Verify it connects to the configured OpenAI model and identifies the configured provider/model in the UI.
2. Stop/disconnect during startup, then reconnect. Repeat a few times. There should be no stale connection reviving later, duplicate microphone use, stuck speaking state, or leaked audio after disconnect.
3. Temporarily configure an unavailable model ID, then an invalid test API key through Models Management. Each failure must terminate startup with an understandable sanitized error, never silently switch to hosted Voice Mode or another billing path. Restore the valid credentials after each case.
4. Clear `agents.voice.useBYOKVoiceModel`. With an eligible paid Copilot account, verify the existing hosted path still connects. Where practical, check that ineligible accounts still receive the appropriate hosted eligibility/onboarding behavior.
5. If a managed environment is available, verify a restriction on client BYOK is respected rather than bypassed by a configured voice-model ID.

## Input ownership and narration

1. Speak a small coding request. Verify its transcript goes through normal chat submission in the input/session that owned the turn. An acknowledgement may indicate acceptance, but must not imply the coding task has already completed.
2. Start from the Agents window welcome composer. Verify materializing the new session preserves the request and correct voice target.
3. While Voice Mode remains active, manually focus or create another chat/session. Old-target output should be suppressed. Speak a new request and verify it reaches the newly focused input, not the prior session.
4. Let a background session complete. It must not narrate through the active session's voice connection.
5. Say a phrase such as 'switch to the other session' or 'which session am I in?'. Verify it is submitted as ordinary chat text rather than silently moving focus or invoking special client-side session navigation.
6. Let GPT Live speak and interrupt with meaningful speech. Verify current output stops/suppresses and the new input turn is handled. Incidental noise should not cause repeated spurious interruptions; if bracket-only ASR annotations such as `[mouth noise]` occur, they must not count as meaningful barge-in.
7. Set `agents.voice.speakResponses` to false. Verify output is muted while voice input and the connection remain usable. Re-enable it and check output resumes normally. If autoplay is blocked, verify there is a usable recovery action.

## Approvals and question forms

Use only harmless actions requiring confirmation. Treat any incorrect approval or cross-session application as a bug.

1. With `agents.voice.language` set to English, answer a current approval with a complete supported response such as 'approve' or 'reject'. Verify it applies through the normal confirmation path to that exact pending action, with acknowledgement only after success.
2. Try tentative, qualified, or negated consent, such as 'maybe approve' or 'do not approve'. It must not authorize the action. Repeat a previously accepted reply and verify it cannot authorize a different pending occurrence.
3. Change/resolve the prompt or switch sessions while an answer is in flight. Verify a stale answer is rejected rather than applied to a new request.
4. For question forms, test exact displayed option labels and ASCII numeric choices. For multiple questions, verify answers accumulate and submit only once the current schema is complete. Exercise multi-select, supported custom answers, and permitted/forbidden skipping where available.
5. Set a supported non-English `agents.voice.language`. Verify exact displayed localized labels and numeric choices work, but unsupported free-form approval phrases are not guessed. English-only shortcuts such as number words, 'option N', 'and', 'other', or 'skip' must not be interpreted as locale-independent consent.
6. Check `auto` language behavior with the display/browser locale. GPT Live receives language instructions, but automatic transcription-language detection and model wording are not guaranteed verbatim.

Finally check keyboard access, Alt+F1 accessibility help, disconnect/cancel behavior, and that disabling AI/Voice Mode does not leave a usable voice entry point or active capture. Restore credentials/settings and stop Voice Mode. Report the surface, provider/model, locale, and exact routing/confirmation sequence without exposing secrets.

- Copilot Chat Extension Version: n/a, Agent Host with the Copilot provider (bundled `@github/copilot-win32-x64` 1.0.84-4)
- VS Code Version: 1.138.0 (7debcd0e2acdea1c52de81bf9ee1620444407dda)
- OS Version: Windows 11 (10.0.26200)
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Agent Host chat, `create_session` tool (`relationship: "currentSession"`)
- Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): Claude Opus 5.5, reasoning effort xhigh, 1M context (`long_context`)
- Logs: `session.start` events from `~/.copilot/session-state/<id>/events.jsonl`, quoted below

An agent that works through a list of tasks by starting one chat per task with `create_session` can choose each chat's model, but not its reasoning effort or context tier. The agent host already supports both per chat: `_createSession` reads them from `model.config.thinkingLevel` and `model.config.contextTier`, and users can set them in the model picker. The tool doesn't expose either.

Passing `model` also loses the caller's reasoning effort:

- Without `model`, `create_session` uses `getCreationDefaults(chat).model`, the calling chat's whole model selection, so the new chat gets the caller's effort and tier.
- With `model`, it sends only `{ id: model.id }`, so the new chat starts with no reasoning effort, which means the model's default.

`create_chat` goes through the same code, and `independent` sessions are also created with `model: { id }` only.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. In an Agent Host chat, select Claude Opus 5.5 with reasoning effort xhigh and the 1M context.
2. Have the agent call `create_session` with `relationship: "currentSession"` and no `model`. The new chat's `session.start` has `"selectedModel":"claude-opus-5.5","reasoningEffort":"xhigh","contextTier":"long_context"`.
3. Have it call `create_session` again with `model: "claude-opus-5.5"`. The new chat's `session.start` has `"selectedModel":"claude-opus-5.5","contextTier":"long_context"` and no `reasoningEffort`.

Expected: a way to set the reasoning effort and context tier of each new chat, and passing `model` shouldn't silently reset the effort.

Suggestion: optional `reasoningEffort` and `contextTier` inputs on `create_session` and `create_chat`, validated against the chosen model the way the model picker does. When they're omitted, keep the caller's values if the chosen model supports them.

>
- VS Code Version: 1.140.0 (07f806f999227108933c2e30515b26eecc1fda74, 2026-09-30T10:38:38+02:00, `stable`)
- OS Version: Windows 10 21H1 (19043.1466), x64

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Use a profile in which any extension persists data through `context.globalState` (any extension works — e.g. Zoo Code / Roo Code / Cline).
2. While VS Code is running, cut power to the machine or hard-reset it, so that the SQLite file ends up with a torn page. (In my case: Kernel-Power 41; EventLog 6008 reports that the previous shutdown at 22:10:11 was unexpected.)
3. Start VS Code again.

**Note — this is not an extension bug:** the failure happens during storage initialization (`[storage main] initialize(): Unable to init storage ...`), *before* any extension is activated, and it wipes the `globalState` of every extension that uses it at once. In my case the extension whose settings disappeared was `zoocodeorganization.zoo-code`, but the defect is in the core storage layer.

*Deterministic variant, in case a power cut is impractical (this mirrors the verification steps that were used for #93428):* replace `globalStorage/state.vscdb` with a copy of a healthy DB in which one page is damaged such that the file still *opens* but `SELECT * FROM ItemTable` fails.

---

## Summary

After an unexpected power loss, `globalStorage/state.vscdb` contained a torn page. VS Code then:

1. **opened the DB successfully** — a torn page does **not** prevent SQLite from opening the file; it only fails when a read or write lands on the damaged page. That is precisely why `doConnect()` — which never issues a `SELECT` — does not throw, and why the `connect()` catch branch that would restore `state.vscdb.backup` is unreachable. The fallback was never attempted;
2. failed **every** subsequent read and write with `SQLITE_CORRUPT: database disk image is malformed`;
3. reported `[shared storage] Fallback application storage initialized with **0 items**` — a "healthy" but empty storage — and then **silently rebuilt** the DB at shutdown from its in-memory cache, which never contained the old values because the initial `all()` read had already failed;
4. and on the **next clean shutdown** VS Code itself ran `backup()` again and **overwrote `state.vscdb.backup`** with that empty shell — removing the one file that, by construction, predated the power loss and could have restored everything.

Net result: all extension `globalState` (API keys, provider configuration, custom modes) was **permanently and silently destroyed**, and `state.vscdb.backup` — the file that exists precisely as the fallback for this situation — turned out to be **unusable**: it ended up with the *same byte size and the same mtime* as the freshly recreated, empty DB.

**No warning was shown to the user.** The data loss was discovered hours later, when the extension came up unconfigured.

The original corrupt file can no longer be attached, because **VS Code itself replaced it** during the sequence above.

## Actual behavior — log evidence

What this log shows, in order:

- `22:50:49.455` — `all()` fails and `[storage main] initialize()` gives up, **but VS Code keeps running**.
- `22:50:49.455` — the smoking gun: `Fallback application storage initialized with **0 items**`. Storage is reported as successfully initialized and *empty*, and the user is told nothing.
- `22:51:30.406` → `22:51:31.533` → `22:51:41.394` → `22:51:45.128` — writes keep being attempted and keep failing, with shrinking key sets: `__$__targetStorageMarker, ZooCodeOrganization.zoo-code, ms-vscode.cpptools` (1709 bytes) → `ms-vscode.cpptools, ZooCodeOrganization.zoo-code` (292) → `ZooCodeOrganization.zoo-code` (184) → `ZooCodeOrganization.zoo-code` (242). The extension is actively trying to persist its state and every attempt is rejected.
- **No line anywhere mentions `state.vscdb.backup`** — the backup path is never taken.

State of the files *after* that session ended:

| File | Size | mtime |
|---|---|---|
| `globalStorage\state.vscdb` | 204800 bytes (50 × 4096-byte pages, header self-consistent) | 2026-10-19 23:05:03 |
| `globalStorage\state.vscdb.backup` | 204800 bytes | **2026-10-19 23:05:03** |

The recreated DB holds only default values for `ZooCodeOrganization.zoo-code`, and **zero** `secret://` entries — every encrypted secret that extension had stored is gone as well.

## Why this happens (code analysis)

Verified against `src/vs/base/parts/storage/node/storage.ts` and `common/storage.ts`; identical in the shipped 1.140.0, in 1.142.0 (current stable) and in `main`.

| Location | Behavior | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| `SQLiteStorageDatabase.doConnect()` | runs only `PRAGMA user_version = 1;` and `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ItemTable (...)` — it **never issues a `SELECT`** | a torn page does **not** make `connect()` throw, so the `.backup` recovery branch inside `connect()`'s `catch` is **unreachable** for this class of corruption |
| `handleSQLiteError()` | only sets `connection.isErroneous = true` and logs | no recovery is attempted at the point of failure |
| `doClose()` | `if (!connection.isErroneous && !connection.isInMemory) { return this.backup() }` | because errors *were* seen, **no backup is written**; execution falls through to the recovery branch |
| recovery branch (`doClose()`) | `unlink(path)` → `doConnect(path)` fresh → insert `recovery()` | `recovery()` is `common/storage.ts`'s `database.close(() => this.cache)` — the **in-memory cache of the current session**. Because the initial `all()` failed, that cache never held the extension's state, so the rebuild writes only defaults |
| `Storage.init()` | `catch (e) { this.logService.error('Unable to init storage ...') } finally { whenInitPromise.complete() }` | VS Code keeps running on storage it knows is broken, and never tells the user |
| `checkIntegrity()` | defined, but has **no caller anywhere in the product** | no integrity check at startup |
| `backup()` | plain copy of `path` → `path + '.backup'`, without `-wal`/`-shm` | once the rebuilt DB is healthy, the next clean shutdown copies it over `.backup`, so **VS Code itself overwrites the only surviving pre-corruption copy with the empty rebuild** |

This is the trade-off that was accepted in #93428 ("VS Code does not warn about or try to recover a corrupt state.vscdb", closed 2020-03-26 as completed). But:

- #93428 concerned **workspace** storage, and its verification steps explicitly accept the outcome *"you should see all workspace state wiped out but things are still functional"*;
- the **"warn about"** half of that issue's title, and the usefulness of `.backup`, were never delivered for this path.

I checked the full commit history of `node/storage.ts`: after `93309f06` (2020-03-26, the fix for #93428) there is not a single corruption-recovery-related change.

## Expected behavior

VS Code should restore the database from `state.vscdb.backup` instead of discarding it.

What this log shows, in order:

- `22:50:49.455` — `all()` fails and `[storage main] initialize()` gives up, **but VS Code keeps running**.
- `22:50:49.455` — the smoking gun: `Fallback application storage initialized with **0 items**`. Storage is reported as successfully initialized and *empty*, and the user is told nothing.
- `22:51:30.406` → `22:51:31.533` → `22:51:41.394` → `22:51:45.128` — writes keep being attempted and keep failing, with shrinking key sets: `__$__targetStorageMarker, ZooCodeOrganization.zoo-code, ms-vscode.cpptools` (1709 bytes) → `ms-vscode.cpptools, ZooCodeOrganization.zoo-code` (292) → `ZooCodeOrganization.zoo-code` (184) → `ZooCodeOrganization.zoo-code` (242). The extension is actively trying to persist its state and every attempt is rejected.
- **No line anywhere mentions `state.vscdb.backup`** — the backup path is never taken.

State of the files *after* that session ended:

| File | Size | mtime |
|---|---|---|
| `globalStorage\state.vscdb` | 204800 bytes (50 × 4096-byte pages, header self-consistent) | 2026-10-19 23:05:03 |
| `globalStorage\state.vscdb.backup` | 204800 bytes | **2026-10-19 23:05:03** |

The recreated DB holds only default values for `ZooCodeOrganization.zoo-code`, and **zero** `secret://` entries — every encrypted secret that extension had stored is gone as well.

## Why this happens (code analysis)

Verified against `src/vs/base/parts/storage/node/storage.ts` and `common/storage.ts`; identical in the shipped 1.140.0, in 1.142.0 (current stable) and in `main`.

| Location | Behavior | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| `SQLiteStorageDatabase.doConnect()` | runs only `PRAGMA user_version = 1;` and `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ItemTable (...)` — it **never issues a `SELECT`** | a torn page does **not** make `connect()` throw, so the `.backup` recovery branch inside `connect()`'s `catch` is **unreachable** for this class of corruption |
| `handleSQLiteError()` | only sets `connection.isErroneous = true` and logs | no recovery is attempted at the point of failure |
| `doClose()` | `if (!connection.isErroneous && !connection.isInMemory) { return this.backup() }` | because errors *were* seen, **no backup is written**; execution falls through to the recovery branch |
| recovery branch (`doClose()`) | `unlink(path)` → `doConnect(path)` fresh → insert `recovery()` | `recovery()` is `common/storage.ts`'s `database.close(() => this.cache)` — the **in-memory cache of the current session**. Because the initial `all()` failed, that cache never held the extension's state, so the rebuild writes only defaults |
| `Storage.init()` | `catch (e) { this.logService.error('Unable to init storage ...') } finally { whenInitPromise.complete() }` | VS Code keeps running on storage it knows is broken, and never tells the user |
| `checkIntegrity()` | defined, but has **no caller anywhere in the product** | no integrity check at startup |
| `backup()` | plain copy of `path` → `path + '.backup'`, without `-wal`/`-shm` | once the rebuilt DB is healthy, the next clean shutdown copies it over `.backup`, so **VS Code itself overwrites the only surviving pre-corruption copy with the empty rebuild** |

This is the trade-off that was accepted in #93428 ("VS Code does not warn about or try to recover a corrupt state.vscdb", closed 2020-03-26 as completed). But:

- #93428 concerned **workspace** storage, and its verification steps explicitly accept the outcome *"you should see all workspace state wiped out but things are still functional"*;
- the **"warn about"** half of that issue's title, and the usefulness of `.backup`, were never delivered for this path.

I checked the full commit history of `node/storage.ts`: after `93309f06` (2020-03-26, the fix for #93428) there is not a single corruption-recovery-related change.

## Expected behavior

VS Code should restore the database from `state.vscdb.backup` instead of discarding it.


## Attachments

None — every log needed to understand this is pasted inline above.

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: `code --disable-extensions --version` fails with the same missing `cli.js` error before extension loading.

- VS Code: 1.141.2, stable, Windows x64 System setup.
- Installed commit: `16507d91be0dc1ce4f94c04d4d0430210b8685d9`.
- OS: Windows 11 26H2, build 26300.9711, x64.
- Install directory: `C:\Program Files\Microsoft VS Code`.
- Downloaded pending update: 1.143.0, commit `087f03b7b82a0c89753986603421c3d24a24cd41`.

## Impact and reproduction

The active installation's entire `16507d91be\resources\app\out` directory is missing.
Starting VS Code through the CLI fails.
Existing editor sessions also report missing editor/profiling worker scripts and repeated terminal-host exits.

On the affected installation:

1. Run `code .`, `code --version`, or `code --disable-extensions --version`.
2. Observe:

```text
Error: Cannot find module 'C:\Program Files\Microsoft VS Code\16507d91be\resources\app\out\cli.js'
    at Module._resolveFilename (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1571:15)
    ...
  code: 'MODULE_NOT_FOUND',
  requireStack: []
Node.js v24.21.0
```

3. Check the directory and files with PowerShell:

```powershell
Test-Path 'C:\Program Files\Microsoft VS Code\16507d91be\resources\app\out'
Test-Path 'C:\Program Files\Microsoft VS Code\16507d91be\resources\app\out\cli.js'
Test-Path 'C:\Program Files\Microsoft VS Code\16507d91be\resources\app\out\main.js'
```

All three return `False`.
`Code.exe`, `bin\code.cmd`, `resources\app\package.json`, and `resources\app\product.json` remain present.
The launcher references the same installed commit as the product metadata.
The transition that removed the directory has not been reproduced deliberately.

## Correlated evidence

Copilot inspected the local files, VS Code logs, and Windows Application event log.
All times below are local on October 20, 2026, UTC-07:00.

```text
07:27:47.037  update#readyStateCheck: newer update available, restarting update machinery
07:27:47.048  update#setState overwriting
07:27:47.087  update#setState downloading
07:27:55.651  update#setState downloaded
07:27:55.652  update#setState ready
```

The cached update metadata identifies 1.143.0.
The installed executable and product metadata still identify 1.141.2.

Windows Application log, provider `Microsoft-Windows-RestartManager`:

```text
07:32:05  Event 10000: Starting session 0
07:32:19-20  Event 10010, repeated for Code.exe processes:
  Application 'C:\Program Files\Microsoft VS Code\Code.exe' (...) cannot be restarted
  - Application SID does not match Conductor SID.
07:32:20  Event 10005: Machine restart is required.
07:32:26  Event 10001: Ending session 0
```

The surviving `16507d91be\resources\app` directory has `LastWriteTime` 07:32:21.
That timestamp establishes a directory change during the Restart Manager session; identifying the deleting process requires additional evidence.
At 13:27, VS Code logs `ERR_FILE_NOT_FOUND` for `profileAnalysisWorkerMain.js` and `editorWebWorkerMain.js` under the missing directory.
At 14:28, it repeatedly logs `ptyHost terminated unexpectedly with code 1`.
No matching update/setup process was running when inspected later that afternoon.
The inspected Defender detection/event records did not identify these files.

## Assessment

**Boundary proven:** required files in the active installation are absent, and Restart Manager encountered failures involving active VS Code processes in the same directory-change window.

**Hypothesis:** an installer/update cleanup or rollback left the active version incomplete.
