body_text:
### Description

With the containerd image store (`driver-type: io.containerd.snapshotter.v1`), **every `docker build` leaks containerd leases** in the `moby` namespace. The leaked leases are labeled `containerd.io/gc.flat=<timestamp>` (plus buildkit `<id>`, `<id>-variants`, `<id>-view` leases without expiry) and are never released — not when the build finishes, not when the built image is removed. Each lease pins the content blobs and snapshots written during that build, so containerd GC can never collect them. On hosts running many builds (CI), this accumulates into tens of GB of uncollectable snapshot/content data.

Only the `buildkit/lease.temporary=...` leases (which carry `containerd.io/gc.expire`) self-clean after ~5 minutes. The plain `gc.flat` leases have no expiry and stay forever.

The pull/export paths were fixed in #48910, but builds still leak on 29.1.3.

### Versions

- Docker Engine 29.1.3 (API 1.52), storage driver `overlayfs` / `io.containerd.snapshotter.v1` (containerd image store)
- containerd 2.2.2
- Ubuntu 26.04 LTS

### Reproduction

```console
$ before=$(ctr -n moby leases ls -q | wc -l); echo $before
753
$ printf 'FROM alpine:3.20\nRUN echo hi\n' > Dockerfile
$ docker build -q -t leaktest . && docker rmi leaktest
$ after=$(ctr -n moby leases ls -q | wc -l); echo $after
761          # +8, and they stay indefinitely
```

Leases added by a single successful build include, e.g.:

```
82sb42yb96nv9agmb9583lswo        containerd.io/gc.flat=2026-10-15T00:27:28.13Z
82sb42yb96nv9agmb9583lswo-variants  -
82sb42yb96nv9agmb9583lswo-view   buildkit/lease.temporary=...,containerd.io/gc.flat=...
o4qdyxk78oli5f8qyf72qydqu        containerd.io/gc.flat=...
o4qdyxk78oli5f8qyf72qydqu-variants -
b7w7uencfdjzbqfbh1tmoxqh1        containerd.io/gc.flat=...
0n6lr0llhnyahb1ksmo1bfop5        containerd.io/gc.flat=...
...
```

Killed/interrupted builds leak the same way (and unlike successful builds, their partial layers are *only* rooted by the lease, so they are pure garbage that GC can never reach).

`docker pull` + `docker rmi` alone does **not** leak (verified), consistent with #48910 having fixed the pull path.

### Production evidence

An internal CI host (many builds per day, some killed) accumulated over ~1 month:

- 660 leaked leases in `ctr -n moby leases ls`, all `gc.flat`, creation dates matching daily build activity (e.g. 121 on one day, 95 on another)
- `/var/lib/containerd` at 191G with **1236 snapshot directories**, while the 65 actual images + 22 containers accounted for only ~42G of unique layer data
- Removing the 444 leases older than 48h (`ctr -n moby leases rm`) immediately triggered containerd GC, which reclaimed **~41G** (114G → 73G; snapshots 1236 → 777) with zero impact on images or running containers — confirming the leases were the only thing keeping the objects alive

### Expected

Build-scoped leases (`gc.flat` and the buildkit session `-view`/`-variants` leases) are released when the build session ends, the same way `buildkit/lease.temporary` leases expire.

### Actual

They persist indefinitely. Symptom on the host: `df` usage of `/var/lib/containerd` far exceeding what `docker system df` / images can account for (very likely the same root cause as #52539).

### Related

- #48910 — fixed lease management for pull and export; build path still leaks
- #50509 — open PR adding leaked-lease cleanup at daemon startup (mitigation, not root cause)
- #52539 — ghost disk usage symptom, likely same root cause

### Workaround

Periodic sweep of stale `gc.flat` leases (safe in our runs; images/containers root their own content):

```bash
ctr -n moby leases ls | awk '{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) if ($i ~ /^containerd\.io\/gc\.flat=/) {d=substr($i,index($i,"=")+1,16); if (d < CUTOFF) print $1}}' \
  | xargs -r -n1 ctr -n moby leases rm
```

We run this from a daily maintenance job with a 48h cutoff.

The leaked leases are labeled `containerd.io/gc.flat=<timestamp>` (plus buildkit `<id>`, `<id>-variants`, `<id>-view` leases without expiry) and are never released — not when the build finishes, not when the built image is removed. Each lease pins the content blobs and snapshots written during that build, so containerd GC can never collect them. On hosts running many builds (CI), this accumulates into tens of GB of uncollectable snapshot/content data.

Only the `buildkit/lease.temporary=...` leases (which carry `containerd.io/gc.expire`) self-clean after ~5 minutes. The plain `gc.flat` leases have no expiry and stay forever.

The pull/export paths were fixed in #48910, but builds still leak on 29.1.3.

### Versions

- Docker Engine 29.1.3 (API 1.52), storage driver `overlayfs` / `io.containerd.snapshotter.v1` (containerd image store)
- containerd 2.2.2
- Ubuntu 26.04 LTS

### Reproduction

```console
$ before=$(ctr -n moby leases ls -q | wc -l); echo $before
753
$ printf 'FROM alpine:3.20\nRUN echo hi\n' > Dockerfile
$ docker build -q -t leaktest . && docker rmi leaktest
$ after=$(ctr -n moby leases ls -q | wc -l); echo $after
761          # +8, and they stay indefinitely
```

Leases added by a single successful build include, e.g.:

```
82sb42yb96nv9agmb9583lswo        containerd.io/gc.flat=2026-10-15T00:27:28.13Z
82sb42yb96nv9agmb9583lswo-variants  -
82sb42yb96nv9agmb9583lswo-view   buildkit/lease.temporary=...,containerd.io/gc.flat=...
o4qdyxk78oli5f8qyf72qydqu        containerd.io/gc.flat=...
o4qdyxk78oli5f8qyf72qydqu-variants -
b7w7uencfdjzbqfbh1tmoxqh1        containerd.io/gc.flat=...
0n6lr0llhnyahb1ksmo1bfop5        containerd.io/gc.flat=...
...
```

Killed/interrupted builds leak the same way (and unlike successful builds, their partial layers are *only* rooted by the lease, so they are pure garbage that GC can never reach).

`docker pull` + `docker rmi` alone does **not** leak (verified), consistent with #48910 having fixed the pull path.

### Production evidence

An internal CI host (many builds per day, some killed) accumulated over ~1 month:

- 660 leaked leases in `ctr -n moby leases ls`, all `gc.flat`, creation dates matching daily build activity (e.g. 121 on one day, 95 on another)
- `/var/lib/containerd` at 191G with **1236 snapshot directories**, while the 65 actual images + 22 containers accounted for only ~42G of unique layer data
- Removing the 444 leases older than 48h (`ctr -n moby leases rm`) immediately triggered containerd GC, which reclaimed **~41G** (114G → 73G; snapshots 1236 → 777) with zero impact on images or running containers — confirming the leases were the only thing keeping the objects alive

### Expected

Build-scoped leases (`gc.flat` and the buildkit session `-view`/`-variants` leases) are released when the build session ends, the same way `buildkit/lease.temporary` leases expire.

### Actual

They persist indefinitely. Symptom on the host: `df` usage of `/var/lib/containerd` far exceeding what `docker system df` / images can account for (very likely the same root cause as #52539).

### Related

- #48910 — fixed lease management for pull and export; build path still leaks
- #50509 — open PR adding leaked-lease cleanup at daemon startup (mitigation, not root cause)
- #52539 — ghost disk usage symptom, likely same root cause

### Workaround

Periodic sweep of stale `gc.flat` leases (safe in our runs; images/containers root their own content):

```bash
ctr -n moby leases ls | awk '{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) if ($i ~ /^containerd\.io\/gc\.flat=/) {d=substr($i,index($i,"=")+1,16); if (d < CUTOFF) print $1}}' \
  | xargs -r -n1 ctr -n moby leases rm
```

We run this from a daily maintenance job with a 48h cutoff.

body_text:
Two related silent failures on current versions, both verified on a clean install.

## Environment

- Docker 29.9.1 (daemon config default except log rotation and `default-address-pools`; reproduced with both the `nftables` default backend and `"firewall-backend": "iptables"`)
- Kernel `7.0.0-30-generic`, Ubuntu 26.04, x86_64 cloud VM (Hetzner)

## Failure mode 1: host-specific bindings

```sh
docker run -d --rm --name t -p <any-host-ip>:8080:80 nginx:alpine
ss -tlnp | grep 8080            # nothing; no docker-proxy, no DNAT
curl http://<that-ip>:8080/     # connection refused
```

`docker inspect` shows the binding in `HostConfig.PortBindings`, but nothing is ever wired. The same command with a wildcard bind (`-p 8080:80`) works.

## Failure mode 2: ports published on internal networks

```sh
docker network create --internal intnet
docker run -d --rm --name t --network intnet -p 8081:80 nginx:alpine
ss -tlnp | grep 8081            # nothing
```

Same container on a non-internal network works. (If rejecting published ports on internal networks is intentional in 29.x, it should error loudly at container start rather than silently record the binding.)

## Observed side-symptoms

- `nft list ruleset` prints `Warning: XT target DNAT not found` / `XT target MASQUERADE not found` (modules `nf_nat`, `nft_chain_nat`, `xt_nat` all loaded and in use).
- No Docker nftables tables exist (`nft list tables` shows only pre-existing tables; the `docker-bridges` table dockerd tries to clean up at startup never gets created).
- Nothing relevant in `journalctl -u docker` — the failure is completely silent; the container reports healthy.

## Expected

Ports functional, or an explicit error at container start.

## Actual

Binding recorded in the container config, never wired (no listener, no DNAT, no userland proxy), no error anywhere.

Note: cannot fully rule out the brand-new 7.0 kernel being the culprit rather than Docker itself — versions above are exact in case that helps bisecting.

body_text:
### Description

After upgrading our Swarm cluster (13 nodes, Ubuntu 24.04.5) from Docker Engine 29.7.2/29.8.0 to 29.9.0, containers attached to an overlay network can no longer establish new TCP connections to a port published through the ingress routing mesh when the service task runs on the same node as the connecting container. The connection attempt times out (ETIMEDOUT).

Connections from containers on any other node to the same published port work fine.
Connections from the host itself (host network namespace) to its own published port work fine. Only containers attached to overlay networks on the same node are affected.
Already-established TCP connections keep working; only new connects fail. This made the problem surface gradually (long-lived DB connections survived, restarted containers could not reconnect).

The problem affects every node in the cluster equally (verified on two different nodes with a minimal reproduction), so it is not corrupted state on a single node. It survives:

systemctl restart docker on the affected node
docker service update --force on the published service and on the client services
a full reboot of the affected node

Last known good version: 29.7.2 (the same workload ran for months with the client containers co-located with the published service). We did not bisect 29.8.x, so the regression is somewhere in 29.8.0–29.9.0.

Possibly related to the fixes that landed in 29.9.0 itself (moby/moby#53723 "published port unreachable from another container ... including Swarm services published through the routing mesh", moby/moby#53663 stale VXLAN FDB entries, moby/moby#53825 DOCKER-INGRESS chain cleanup) — the symptom matches the first one, but on 29.9.0 it is not fixed for the same-node case in our environment.

### Reproduce

Multi-node swarm, default ingress network. NODE_A is any worker, NODE_A_IP its address on the swarm data path. testnet is any attachable overlay network (the same happens with stack-created overlay networks).
`# on a manager
docker network create -d overlay --attachable testnet
docker service create --name lbtest \
  --constraint node.hostname==NODE_A \
  --publish 18080:80 nginx:alpine

# 1) SAME NODE — on NODE_A:
docker run --rm --network testnet alpine \
  sh -c 'wget -qO- --timeout=5 http://NODE_A_IP:18080 >/dev/null \
         && echo SAMEHOST_OK || echo SAMEHOST_FAIL'
# -> SAMEHOST_FAIL   (wget: download timed out)

# 2) OTHER NODE — on NODE_B:
docker run --rm --network testnet alpine \

### Description

Since #52892 ("daemon: Set umask to 0000", milestone 29.6.0), processes started with `docker exec` run with umask `0000`, so every file and directory they create without an explicit mode is world-writable.

`docker run` is unaffected: runc sets umask `0022` for the container's init process. An exec'd process does not get that default. It inherits the umask of the shim, which inherits it from `containerd`, which inherits it from `dockerd`, which is now `0000`. On this machine `dockerd`, `containerd` and every `containerd-shim-runc-v2` report `Umask: 0000`, while the process that launches `dockerd` has `0022`.

The PR's goal (honoring explicit modes such as `COPY --chmod=777`) makes sense, but the change in `docker exec` behavior looks unintended. It silently changes the permissions of anything created through `docker exec`. In my case, a DDEV add-on's post-start hook (run through `docker exec`) writes `~/.ssh` config include files. Those are now created as `0666`, and OpenSSH refuses to use them:

```
Bad owner or permissions on /home/<user>/.ssh/config.platformsh-lite.pre.d/config
```

Anything else that writes files from an exec session (setup scripts, CI steps, `sudoers.d` drop-ins, etc.) is affected the same way. Other projects have run into the same thing and added `umask 022` wrappers around exec, for example chainguard-dev/melange#2705 and zackees/bosn#365.

### Reproduce

```console
$ docker run -d --name umask-repro alpine:3 sleep 300
$ docker exec umask-repro sh -c umask
0000
$ docker exec umask-repro sh -c 'grep Umask /proc/1/status'
Umask:	0022
$ docker exec umask-repro sh -c 'touch /tmp/f && mkdir /tmp/d && ls -ld /tmp/f /tmp/d'
drwxrwxrwx    1 root     root             0 Oct 20 02:39 /tmp/d
-rw-rw-rw-    1 root     root             0 Oct 20 02:39 /tmp/f
$ docker rm -f umask-repro
$ docker run --rm alpine:3 sh -c umask
0022
```

Daemon-side processes (inspected from a `--pid=host` container):

```
dockerd                  Umask: 0000
containerd               Umask: 0000
containerd-shim-runc-v2  Umask: 0000
```

### Expected behavior

`docker exec` processes get umask `0022` by default, the same as `docker run` and as before 29.6. For example, the daemon could set an explicit `User.Umask` in the exec process spec rather than letting it inherit the daemon's umask.

body_text:
### Description

With the graphdriver image store, `docker push` of an image that was pulled with zstd layers writes a
manifest that labels those layers `application/vnd.docker.image.rootfs.diff.tar.gzip`. The blobs are
reused unchanged, so they are still zstd. This happens both when the blob is already in the target repo
and when it is mounted from another repo. The containerd image store pushes the same image with the
correct `application/vnd.oci.image.layer.v1.tar+zstd`.

Reproduced on Docker 29.9.1 and 28.5.2. On Docker 29 it still matters, because daemons upgraded from 28
keep the graphdriver store ("using prior storage driver: overlay2").

Registries accept such manifests, since they check that blobs exist but not what they contain, so the wrong
label persists and spreads to images built on top. Pulls still work, because dockerd and containerd detect
the compression from the blob's magic bytes. Tools that trust the media type do not: for example,
BuildKit's `force-compression=true` fails on these layers (moby/buildkit#7308).

The media type appears to be hard-coded on both reuse paths in `daemon/internal/distribution/push_v2.go`:
[`layerAlreadyExists`](https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/docker-v29.9.1/daemon/internal/distribution/push_v2.go#L550) and [`Upload` on `ErrBlobMounted`](https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/docker-v29.9.1/daemon/internal/distribution/push_v2.go#L341), both
`desc.MediaType = c8dimages.MediaTypeDockerSchema2LayerGzip`.


### Reproduce

The reproducer is the two files below: save them in one directory and run `./repro.sh`
(`DOCKER_VERSION=28.5.2 ./repro.sh` for 28). It needs only Docker with Compose, and runs
`registry:3.1.2`, two `docker:29.9.1-dind` daemons (`containerd-snapshotter` false and true) and an
alpine container with curl, jq and zstd.

1. Push a one-layer image to `registry:5000/repro/app:zstd`: an OCI manifest with one
   `tar+zstd` layer (a tar compressed with the `zstd` CLI), built with curl. No BuildKit is involved.
2. On each daemon:
   ```
   docker pull registry:5000/repro/app:zstd
   docker tag registry:5000/repro/app:zstd registry:5000/repro/app:<store>
   docker tag registry:5000/repro/app:zstd registry:5000/repro/other-<store>:latest
   docker push registry:5000/repro/app:<store>
   docker push registry:5000/repro/other-<store>:latest
   ```
3. Compare each pushed manifest's layer media type with the blob's first bytes:

```
image                                  layer media type                                   blob content
repro/app:zstd (source)                application/vnd.oci.image.layer.v1.tar+zstd        zstd
repro/app:graphdriver                  application/vnd.docker.image.rootfs.diff.tar.gzip  zstd
repro/other-graphdriver:latest         application/vnd.docker.image.rootfs.diff.tar.gzip  zstd
repro/app:containerd                   application/vnd.oci.image.layer.v1.tar+zstd        zstd
repro/other-containerd:latest          application/vnd.oci.image.layer.v1.tar+zstd        zstd
```

All five reference the same blob digest.

<details>
<summary>compose.yaml</summary>

```yaml
# Image versions are set in repro.sh
name: moby-zstd-push-repro

x-dind: &dind
  image: docker:${DOCKER_VERSION:?set by repro.sh}-dind
  privileged: true
  depends_on:
    - registry

services:
  registry:
    image: registry:${REGISTRY_VERSION:?set by repro.sh}

  dockerd-graphdriver:
    <<: *dind
    command: ["dockerd", "--host=unix:///var/run/docker.sock", "--insecure-registry=registry:5000", "--debug"]
    configs:
      - source: graphdriver
        target: /etc/docker/daemon.json

  # For comparison
  dockerd-containerd:
    <<: *dind
    command: ["dockerd", "--host=unix:///var/run/docker.sock", "--insecure-registry=registry:5000"]
    configs:
      - source: containerd
        target: /etc/docker/daemon.json

  # curl, jq and zstd for inspecting and writing registry manifests
  tools:
    image: alpine:${ALPINE_VERSION:?set by repro.sh}
    command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache -q curl jq zstd && touch /ready && exec sleep infinity"]

configs:
  graphdriver:
    content: '{"features": {"containerd-snapshotter": false}}'
  containerd:
    content: '{"features": {"containerd-snapshotter": true}}'
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>repro.sh</summary>

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Reproduce dockerd (graphdriver image store) pushing a pulled zstd layer with
# a gzip media type. The containerd image store is run alongside for comparison.
#
# Usage: ./repro.sh                    (versions below)
#        DOCKER_VERSION=28.5.2 ./repro.sh
#        KEEP=1 ./repro.sh             (leave the stack running afterwards)
# Exits 0 if the bug reproduces, 1 if it doesn't.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"

export DOCKER_VERSION=${DOCKER_VERSION:-29.9.1}
export REGISTRY_VERSION=${REGISTRY_VERSION:-3.1.2}
export ALPINE_VERSION=${ALPINE_VERSION:-3.24.2}

R=registry:5000/repro

# Registry helpers, run with sh in the tools container
TOOLS=$(cat <<'EOF'
set -eu
R=http://registry:5000
ACCEPT='application/vnd.oci.image.manifest.v1+json,application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.v2+json'
OCI_MANIFEST=application/vnd.oci.image.manifest.v1+json

case $1 in
layers) # <repo> <tag>: each layer's media type, digest, and actual compression from its first bytes
  curl -fsS -H "Accept: $ACCEPT" "$R/v2/$2/manifests/$3" | jq -r '.layers[] | "\(.mediaType) \(.digest)"' |
    while read -r mt dg; do
      magic=$(curl -s "$R/v2/$2/blobs/$dg" | head -c4 | od -An -tx1 | tr -d ' \n')
      case $magic in 28b52ffd) c=zstd ;; 1f8b*) c=gzip ;; *) c="? ($magic)" ;; esac
      printf '  %-50s %.19s…  content: %s\n' "$mt" "$dg" "$c"
    done
  ;;
zstd-image) # <repo> <tag>: one-layer image compressed with the zstd CLI, labelled tar+zstd
  cd "$(mktemp -d)"
  mkdir root && echo hello >root/hello.txt && tar -C root -cf layer.tar . && zstd -3 -q layer.tar
  arch=$(uname -m | sed 's/x86_64/amd64/;s/aarch64/arm64/')
  jq -n --arg arch "$arch" --arg diff "sha256:$(sha256sum layer.tar | cut -d' ' -f1)" \
    '{architecture: $arch, os: "linux", rootfs: {type: "layers", diff_ids: [$diff]}}' >config.json
  for f in config.json layer.tar.zst; do # monolithic blob upload
    loc=$(curl -fsS -X POST -D - -o /dev/null "$R/v2/$2/blobs/uploads/" | tr -d '\r' | sed -n 's/^[Ll]ocation: //p')
    curl -fsS -X PUT -H 'Content-Type: application/octet-stream' --data-binary @"$f" \
      "$loc&digest=sha256:$(sha256sum "$f" | cut -d' ' -f1)"
  done
  jq -n \
    --arg cd "sha256:$(sha256sum config.json | cut -d' ' -f1)" --argjson cs "$(wc -c <config.json)" \
    --arg ld "sha256:$(sha256sum layer.tar.zst | cut -d' ' -f1)" --argjson ls "$(wc -c <layer.tar.zst)" \
    '{schemaVersion: 2, mediaType: "application/vnd.oci.image.manifest.v1+json",
      config: {mediaType: "application/vnd.oci.image.config.v1+json", digest: $cd, size: $cs},
      layers: [{mediaType: "application/vnd.oci.image.layer.v1.tar+zstd", digest: $ld, size: $ls}]}' |
    curl -fsS -X PUT -H "Content-Type: $OCI_MANIFEST" --data-binary @- "$R/v2/$2/manifests/$3"
  ;;
esac
EOF
)

dc() { docker compose "$@"; }
step() { printf '\n\033[1m== %s\033[0m\n' "$*"; }
tools() { dc exec -T tools sh -c "$TOOLS" tools "$@" </dev/null; }
trap '[ -n "${KEEP:-}" ] || dc down --volumes >/dev/null 2>&1' EXIT

repush() { # <daemon> <store name>: pull the zstd image and push it to the same repo and to another repo
  local docker="dc exec -T $1 docker"
  $docker pull -q "$R/app:zstd" >/dev/null
  $docker tag "$R/app:zstd" "$R/app:$2"
  $docker tag "$R/app:zstd" "$R/other-$2:latest"
  $docker push -q "$R/app:$2" >/dev/null
  $docker push -q "$R/other-$2:latest" >/dev/null
  echo "  $R/app:$2 (blob already in the repo):"
  tools layers repro/app "$2"
  echo "  $R/other-$2:latest (blob mounted from repro/app):"
  tools layers "repro/other-$2" latest
}

step "Starting registry and two dockerd $DOCKER_VERSION daemons"
dc down --volumes >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
dc --progress quiet up -d --quiet-pull
until dc exec -T tools test -f /ready 2>/dev/null; do sleep 1; done
for d in dockerd-graphdriver dockerd-containerd; do
  until dc exec -T "$d" docker info >/dev/null 2>&1; do sleep 1; done
  echo "  $d: $(dc exec -T "$d" docker info --format '{{.ServerVersion}}, storage driver {{.Driver}}')"
done
mkdir -p out
dc exec -T dockerd-graphdriver docker version >out/docker-version.txt
```

With the graphdriver image store, `docker push` of an image that was pulled with zstd layers writes a
manifest that labels those layers `application/vnd.docker.image.rootfs.diff.tar.gzip`. The blobs are
reused unchanged, so they are still zstd. This happens both when the blob is already in the target repo
and when it is mounted from another repo. The containerd image store pushes the same image with the
correct `application/vnd.oci.image.layer.v1.tar+zstd`.

Reproduced on Docker 29.9.1 and 28.5.2. On Docker 29 it still matters, because daemons upgraded from 28
keep the graphdriver store ("using prior storage driver: overlay2").

Registries accept such manifests, since they check that blobs exist but not what they contain, so the wrong
label persists and spreads to images built on top. Pulls still work, because dockerd and containerd detect
the compression from the blob's magic bytes. Tools that trust the media type do not: for example,
BuildKit's `force-compression=true` fails on these layers (moby/buildkit#7308).

The media type appears to be hard-coded on both reuse paths in `daemon/internal/distribution/push_v2.go`:
[`layerAlreadyExists`](https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/docker-v29.9.1/daemon/internal/distribution/push_v2.go#L550) and [`Upload` on `ErrBlobMounted`](https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/docker-v29.9.1/daemon/internal/distribution/push_v2.go#L341), both
`desc.MediaType = c8dimages.MediaTypeDockerSchema2LayerGzip`.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Reproduce dockerd (graphdriver image store) pushing a pulled zstd layer with
# a gzip media type. The containerd image store is run alongside for comparison.
#
# Usage: ./repro.sh                    (versions below)
#        DOCKER_VERSION=28.5.2 ./repro.sh
#        KEEP=1 ./repro.sh             (leave the stack running afterwards)
# Exits 0 if the bug reproduces, 1 if it doesn't.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"

export DOCKER_VERSION=${DOCKER_VERSION:-29.9.1}
export REGISTRY_VERSION=${REGISTRY_VERSION:-3.1.2}
export ALPINE_VERSION=${ALPINE_VERSION:-3.24.2}

R=registry:5000/repro

# Registry helpers, run with sh in the tools container
TOOLS=$(cat <<'EOF'
set -eu
R=http://registry:5000
ACCEPT='application/vnd.oci.image.manifest.v1+json,application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.v2+json'
OCI_MANIFEST=application/vnd.oci.image.manifest.v1+json

case $1 in
layers) # <repo> <tag>: each layer's media type, digest, and actual compression from its first bytes
  curl -fsS -H "Accept: $ACCEPT" "$R/v2/$2/manifests/$3" | jq -r '.layers[] | "\(.mediaType) \(.digest)"' |
    while read -r mt dg; do
      magic=$(curl -s "$R/v2/$2/blobs/$dg" | head -c4 | od -An -tx1 | tr -d ' \n')
      case $magic in 28b52ffd) c=zstd ;; 1f8b*) c=gzip ;; *) c="? ($magic)" ;; esac
      printf '  %-50s %.19s…  content: %s\n' "$mt" "$dg" "$c"
    done
  ;;
zstd-image) # <repo> <tag>: one-layer image compressed with the zstd CLI, labelled tar+zstd
  cd "$(mktemp -d)"
  mkdir root && echo hello >root/hello.txt && tar -C root -cf layer.tar . && zstd -3 -q layer.tar
  arch=$(uname -m | sed 's/x86_64/amd64/;s/aarch64/arm64/')
  jq -n --arg arch "$arch" --arg diff "sha256:$(sha256sum layer.tar | cut -d' ' -f1)" \
    '{architecture: $arch, os: "linux", rootfs: {type: "layers", diff_ids: [$diff]}}' >config.json
  for f in config.json layer.tar.zst; do # monolithic blob upload
    loc=$(curl -fsS -X POST -D - -o /dev/null "$R/v2/$2/blobs/uploads/" | tr -d '\r' | sed -n 's/^[Ll]ocation: //p')
    curl -fsS -X PUT -H 'Content-Type: application/octet-stream' --data-binary @"$f" \
      "$loc&digest=sha256:$(sha256sum "$f" | cut -d' ' -f1)"
  done
  jq -n \
    --arg cd "sha256:$(sha256sum config.json | cut -d' ' -f1)" --argjson cs "$(wc -c <config.json)" \
    --arg ld "sha256:$(sha256sum layer.tar.zst | cut -d' ' -f1)" --argjson ls "$(wc -c <layer.tar.zst)" \
    '{schemaVersion: 2, mediaType: "application/vnd.oci.image.manifest.v1+json",
      config: {mediaType: "application/vnd.oci.image.config.v1+json", digest: $cd, size: $cs},
      layers: [{mediaType: "application/vnd.oci.image.layer.v1.tar+zstd", digest: $ld, size: $ls}]}' |
    curl -fsS -X PUT -H "Content-Type: $OCI_MANIFEST" --data-binary @- "$R/v2/$2/manifests/$3"
  ;;
esac
EOF
)

dc() { docker compose "$@"; }
step() { printf '\n\033[1m== %s\033[0m\n' "$*"; }
tools() { dc exec -T tools sh -c "$TOOLS" tools "$@" </dev/null; }
trap '[ -n "${KEEP:-}" ] || dc down --volumes >/dev/null 2>&1' EXIT

repush() { # <daemon> <store name>: pull the zstd image and push it to the same repo and to another repo
  local docker="dc exec -T $1 docker"
  $docker pull -q "$R/app:zstd" >/dev/null
  $docker tag "$R/app:zstd" "$R/app:$2"
  $docker tag "$R/app:zstd" "$R/other-$2:latest"
  $docker push -q "$R/app:$2" >/dev/null
  $docker push -q "$R/other-$2:latest" >/dev/null
  echo "  $R/app:$2 (blob already in the repo):"
  tools layers repro/app "$2"
  echo "  $R/other-$2:latest (blob mounted from repro/app):"
  tools layers "repro/other-$2" latest
}

step "Starting registry and two dockerd $DOCKER_VERSION daemons"
dc down --volumes >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
dc --progress quiet up -d --quiet-pull
until dc exec -T tools test -f /ready 2>/dev/null; do sleep 1; done
for d in dockerd-graphdriver dockerd-containerd; do
  until dc exec -T "$d" docker info >/dev/null 2>&1; do sleep 1; done
  echo "  $d: $(dc exec -T "$d" docker info --format '{{.ServerVersion}}, storage driver {{.Driver}}')"
done
mkdir -p out
dc exec -T dockerd-graphdriver docker version >out/docker-version.txt
dc exec -T dockerd-graphdriver docker info >out/docker-info.txt 2>&1

step "1. Push a one-layer zstd image built with curl and the zstd CLI ($R/app:zstd)"
tools zstd-image repro/app zstd
tools layers repro/app zstd

step "2. Graphdriver store: pull it, then push it under new tags"
repush dockerd-graphdriver graphdriver

step "3. containerd store: the same, for comparison"
repush dockerd-containerd containerd

dc logs dockerd-graphdriver >out/dockerd-graphdriver.log 2>&1
echo
echo "  (docker version/info and the graphdriver daemon's --debug log are in out/)"

pushed=$(tools layers repro/app graphdriver; tools layers repro/other-graphdriver latest)
if grep -q 'gzip .*content: zstd' <<<"$pushed"; then
  printf '\n\033[1mREPRODUCED\033[0m with Docker %s\n' "$DOCKER_VERSION"
  exit 0
fi
echo "NOT REPRODUCED" >&2
exit 1
```

### Description

### Description

After upgrading rootless Docker on Debian 12 from 29.9.0 to 29.9.2, long-lived RTSP-over-TCP streams from LAN IP cameras into a container (Frigate NVR) stall intermittently. ffmpeg in the container logs `Failed reading RTSP data: Connection timed out`. The RTSP session sets up fine (the stream is identified as H.264), but then the video data stops arriving. The affected cameras are random and fail at random times, while the others keep streaming.

Rolling back to 29.9.0 / containerd.io 2.4.1 fixes it immediately. Nothing else changed: same kernel, same compose files, same rootless config.

Packages changed in the upgrade (`/var/log/apt/history.log`):

```
Upgrade: containerd.io:amd64 (2.4.1-2~debian.12~bookworm, 2.4.2-3~debian.12~bookworm),
docker-ce-cli:amd64 (5:29.9.0-1~debian.12~bookworm, 5:29.9.2-1~debian.12~bookworm),
docker-ce:amd64 (5:29.9.0-1~debian.12~bookworm, 5:29.9.2-1~debian.12~bookworm),
docker-ce-rootless-extras:amd64 (5:29.9.0-1~debian.12~bookworm, 5:29.9.2-1~debian.12~bookworm)
```

Component changes per the release notes:
- 29.9.1: RootlessKit 3.2.0 → 3.3.0, containerd 2.4.1 → 2.4.2
- 29.9.2: Go 1.26.10

Possibly related: rootless-containers/rootlesskit#648 / #649. RootlessKit 3.3.0 makes the builtin port driver's source-IP-transparent backend actually activate under `--detach-netns`. On 3.2.0 the probe failed with EPERM and the backend was silently disabled. That is a real behaviour change for builtin-port-driver users between 29.9.0 and 29.9.2. It's not confirmed as the cause yet: I'm testing containerd and RootlessKit separately and will update this issue.

### Reproduce

1. Debian 12 (Proxmox VM), rootless Docker as a systemd user service, with:
```
   DOCKERD_ROOTLESS_ROOTLESSKIT_NET=slirp4netns
   DOCKERD_ROOTLESS_ROOTLESSKIT_PORT_DRIVER=builtin
```
2. Run Frigate with 12 IP cameras pulled over RTSP/TCP from a different routed subnet.
3. On 29.9.0 / containerd.io 2.4.1, streams are stable.
4. Upgrade to 29.9.2 / containerd.io 2.4.2, then run `systemctl --user restart docker`.
5. Within ~5 minutes, random cameras start dropping with the log below. After downgrading, streams are stable again.

### Expected behavior

Streams stay as stable as they were on 29.9.0.


### Additional Info

ffmpeg log (Frigate, on 29.9.2):

```
[in#0/rtsp @ 0x560f02d4bec0] Failed reading RTSP data: Connection timed out
[in#0/rtsp @ 0x560f02d4bec0] Could not find codec parameters for stream 0 (Video: h264, none): unspecified size
Consider increasing the value for the 'analyzeduration' (0) and 'probesize' (5000000) options
```

### Bug Report Checklist

- [x] This is NOT a [security, `npm audit`, or GitHub Advisory issue](https://mochajs.org/explainers/security-vulnerability-reports).
- [x] I have read and agree to Mocha's [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/mochajs/mocha/blob/main/.github/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) and [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/mochajs/mocha/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] I have searched for [related issues](https://github.com/mochajs/mocha/issues?q=is%3Aissue) and [issues with the `faq` label](https://github.com/mochajs/mocha/issues?utf8=%E2%9C%93&q=is%3Aissue%20label%3Afaq%20), but none matched my issue.
- [x] I have 'smoke tested' the code to be tested by running it outside the real test suite to get a better sense of whether the problem is in the code under test, my usage of Mocha, or Mocha itself.
- [x] I want to provide a PR to resolve this

### Expected

When running with `--parallel` under a V8-coverage tool (`c8`, or `nyc` in V8 mode), each worker's collected coverage should be included in the report. At a minimum, the grace period a worker is given to exit before Mocha force-kills it should be configurable, so a worker whose exit/flush legitimately takes longer than 1 second is not killed mid-flush.

### Actual

Whole workers' coverage is **silently discarded**, so the parallel report is dramatically lower than the same suite run serially. The run still exits `0`; only the percentages look wrong, so it is easy to misread as a flaky/environment problem.

Root cause: Mocha creates the `workerpool` pool without setting `workerTerminateTimeout`, so workerpool uses its default of **1000 ms**. At end of run each worker is asked to terminate and then hard-killed (`SIGTERM`) once that timeout elapses. Node writes the `NODE_V8_COVERAGE` profile *as the process exits*; a worker still flushing when the 1 s grace period lapses is killed first, and that worker's coverage file is never written. There is currently no Mocha CLI/`.mocharc` option to change this timeout.

It is load-dependent: it appears on many-core machines (more workers flushing at once) and with large dependency graphs (bigger profiles, ~10–16 MB per worker here). Lowering `--jobs` hides it, which disguises the real cause.

Relevant code:

```js
// lib/nodejs/parallel-buffered-runner.js — pool created with only maxWorkers
pool = BufferedWorkerPool.create({maxWorkers: options.jobs});

// lib/nodejs/buffered-worker-pool.js — WORKER_POOL_DEFAULT_OPTS never sets it

// workerpool/src/Pool.js — hence the 1000ms fallback
this.workerTerminateTimeout = options.workerTerminateTimeout || 1000;
// workerpool/src/WorkerHandler.js — setTimeout(() => worker.kill(), workerTerminateTimeout)
```


### Minimal, Complete and Verifiable Example

The effect needs enough concurrent flush work to exceed 1 s, so it reproduces most reliably in a real project on a many-core machine:

```bash
# many-core machine; large-ish dependency graph
c8 --reporter=json-summary --temp-directory .cov-tmp \
  mocha --parallel --jobs 9 -- '**/*.test.ts'
```

Then inspect `.cov-tmp/*.json`: the per-worker V8 dumps that should contain each spec are missing, and they never appear after the run (so it is not the reporter reading too early — the dumps were never written).

Measured on a 10-core Linux devcontainer, same suite, only the grace period / `--jobs` varied (compare covered counts, not just %, since `c8 all:true` shifts denominators between runs):

| Run | Worker coverage dumps written | lines | functions | branches |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--parallel --jobs 9` (default 1000 ms) | 0 of 9 | 35.69% | 22.11% | 60.50% |
| `--parallel --jobs 2` (default 1000 ms) | 2 of 2 | 73.57% | 72.61% | 65.84% |
| `--parallel --jobs 9`, grace period 60000 ms | 9 of 9 | 73.59% | 72.61% | 69.96% |

Raising only the grace period (nothing else) restores all 9 workers' coverage.

I could not make a small, dependency-free repro fail: with tiny profiles the flush completes well within 1 s. It needs enough workers/profile size/disk latency to push the flush past the 1 s window. On constrained CI (e.g. 4 vCPU) it often "works" simply because fewer workers flush simultaneously. If a synthetic MCVE is required I can build one that pads each worker's exit flush, but I wanted to report the real-world trigger first.


### Versions

- `mocha`: 11.7.5 (the pool is still created without `workerTerminateTimeout` in 11.8.0 and the 12.0.0 RCs)
- `node_modules/.bin/mocha --version`: 11.7.5
- `node --version`: v20.20.2
- `workerpool`: 9.x (default `workerTerminateTimeout` 1000 ms; unchanged in v10)
- `c8`: 10.1.x
- OS: Linux x64, 10 logical cores
- Transpiler: `ts-node` (CommonJS)


### Additional Info

#### Proposed fix

Expose workerpool's `workerTerminateTimeout` as a first-class Mocha option so it can be raised without patching, keeping the current default unchanged:

- Add a `--worker-terminate-timeout <ms>` number option (Rules & Behavior group), documented as the grace period a `--parallel` worker is given to exit on its own before being force-killed; `defaultDescription: '1000'` (no behavior change unless set).
- Thread `options.workerTerminateTimeout` into `BufferedWorkerPool.create({maxWorkers, workerTerminateTimeout})`, forward it into the workerpool options, and add it to the parallel runner's `DENY_OPTIONS` (it is a pool-level option like `jobs`, not something to serialize to worker Mocha instances). When unset, leave workerpool's own default in place rather than pinning one in Mocha.

This is the smallest change that preserves current defaults. A stronger fix (awaiting a clean coverage flush before force-killing) would also be welcome but is more invasive; a configurable grace period unblocks users today and is a reasonable knob regardless. I'm running exactly this locally via `patch-package` and it resolves the loss (row 3 above); happy to open the PR.

#### Workarounds for others hitting this

- Lower `--jobs` until workers flush within 1 s (fragile; regresses as the suite grows).
- Collect coverage from a serial run (`--no-parallel`) — slower.
- Patch Mocha/workerpool to raise `workerTerminateTimeout`.

#### Related

- bcoe/c8#374 — "Code coverage breaks in parallel mode": same symptom; the workaround there was lowering `--jobs`, and the root cause was never identified as this timeout.

Measured on a 10-core Linux devcontainer, same suite, only the grace period / `--jobs` varied (compare covered counts, not just %, since `c8 all:true` shifts denominators between runs):

| Run | Worker coverage dumps written | lines | functions | branches |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--parallel --jobs 9` (default 1000 ms) | 0 of 9 | 35.69% | 22.11% | 60.50% |
| `--parallel --jobs 2` (default 1000 ms) | 2 of 2 | 73.57% | 72.61% | 65.84% |
| `--parallel --jobs 9`, grace period 60000 ms | 9 of 9 | 73.59% | 72.61% | 69.96% |

Raising only the grace period (nothing else) restores all 9 workers' coverage.

I could not make a small, dependency-free repro fail: with tiny profiles the flush completes well within 1 s. It needs enough workers/profile size/disk latency to push the flush past the 1 s window. On constrained CI (e.g. 4 vCPU) it often "works" simply because fewer workers flush simultaneously. If a synthetic MCVE is required I can build one that pads each worker's exit flush, but I wanted to report the real-world trigger first.


### Versions

- `mocha`: 11.7.5 (the pool is still created without `workerTerminateTimeout` in 11.8.0 and the 12.0.0 RCs)
- `node_modules/.bin/mocha --version`: 11.7.5
- `node --version`: v20.20.2
- `workerpool`: 9.x (default `workerTerminateTimeout` 1000 ms; unchanged in v10)
- `c8`: 10.1.x
- OS: Linux x64, 10 logical cores
- Transpiler: `ts-node` (CommonJS)


### Additional Info

#### Proposed fix

Expose workerpool's `workerTerminateTimeout` as a first-class Mocha option so it can be raised without patching, keeping the current default unchanged:

- Add a `--worker-terminate-timeout <ms>` number option (Rules & Behavior group), documented as the grace period a `--parallel` worker is given to exit on its own before being force-killed; `defaultDescription: '1000'` (no behavior change unless set).
- Thread `options.workerTerminateTimeout` into `BufferedWorkerPool.create({maxWorkers, workerTerminateTimeout})`, forward it into the workerpool options, and add it to the parallel runner's `DENY_OPTIONS` (it is a pool-level option like `jobs`, not something to serialize to worker Mocha instances). When unset, leave workerpool's own default in place rather than pinning one in Mocha.

This is the smallest change that preserves current defaults. A stronger fix (awaiting a clean coverage flush before force-killing) would also be welcome but is more invasive; a configurable grace period unblocks users today and is a reasonable knob regardless. I'm running exactly this locally via `patch-package` and it resolves the loss (row 3 above); happy to open the PR.

#### Workarounds for others hitting this

- Lower `--jobs` until workers flush within 1 s (fragile; regresses as the suite grows).
- Collect coverage from a serial run (`--no-parallel`) — slower.
- Patch Mocha/workerpool to raise `workerTerminateTimeout`.

#### Related

- bcoe/c8#374 — "Code coverage breaks in parallel mode": same symptom; the workaround there was lowering `--jobs`, and the root cause was never identified as this timeout.", "language": "JavaScript", "state": "open", "assignees": [], "locked": false, "verified_at": "2026-10-23T06:12:56.168Z", "expires_at": "2026-10-24T06:12:56.168000+00:00", "timeline_complete": true, "bucket": "historical_signal_only"}

### Bug Report Checklist

- [x] This is NOT a [security, `npm audit`, or GitHub Advisory issue](https://mochajs.org/explainers/security-vulnerability-reports).
- [x] I have read and agree to Mocha's [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/mochajs/mocha/blob/main/.github/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) and [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/mochajs/mocha/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] I have searched for [related issues](https://github.com/mochajs/mocha/issues?q=is%3Aissue) and [issues with the `faq` label](https://github.com/mochajs/mocha/issues?utf8=%E2%9C%93&q=is%3Aissue%20label%3Afaq%20), but none matched my issue.
- [x] I have 'smoke tested' the code to be tested by running it outside the real test suite to get a better sense of whether the problem is in the code under test, my usage of Mocha, or Mocha itself.
- [x] I want to provide a PR to resolve this

### Expected

A config file in the current working directory wins over any config in a parent directory. Filename priority (.mocharc.cjs before .mocharc.js, and so on) applies only among files in the same directory. That is what the [configuring docs](https://mochajs.org/running/configuring/) describe, and what find-up did when given the whole CONFIG_FILES list: check every name in the current directory, then walk up one level.

### Actual

Since 12.0.2, findConfig walks the entire tree for .mocharc.cjs before it looks for .mocharc.js in the current directory. A parent .mocharc.cjs is loaded even when the working directory has its own .mocharc.js.

lib/cli/config.cjs does this:

```
const findUpSyncAny = (files, options) => {
  for (const file of files) {
    const filepath = findUpSync(file, options);
    if (filepath) return filepath;
  }
  return undefined;
};
```
find-up-simple accepts one name, so each call walks to the filesystem root. The first name in CONFIG_FILES is .mocharc.cjs.

### Minimal, Complete and Verifiable Example
```
mkdir -p /tmp/mocha-rc/child
printf '%s\n' "module.exports = { grep: 'from-parent' };" > /tmp/mocha-rc/.mocharc.cjs
printf '%s\n' "module.exports = { grep: 'from-child' };" > /tmp/mocha-rc/child/.mocharc.js
printf '%s\n' "it('from-child', () => {});" "it('from-parent', () => {});" > /tmp/mocha-rc/child/test.js
cd /tmp/mocha-rc/child
npx --yes mocha@12.0.1 test.js   # runs "from-child"
npx --yes mocha@12.0.3 test.js   # runs "from-parent"
```
### Versions

Mocha 12.0.1 uses the local .mocharc.js.
Mocha 12.0.2 and 12.0.3 use the parent .mocharc.cjs.
Reproduced with Node.js v22.22.0.

### Additional Info

This came in with [#6342](https://github.com/mochajs/mocha/pull/6342) (a652ff5), the find-up-simple workaround for [#6319](https://github.com/mochajs/mocha/issues/6319). The PR says filename order matches find-up. find-up's multi-name search is per directory; this loop is per filename across the whole tree.

The tests added there stub findUpSync and assert call order. They never place a local .mocharc.js next to an ancestor .mocharc.cjs. [#6345](https://github.com/mochajs/mocha/issues/6345) asks for those same stub tests.

Parent lookup when the current directory has no config file is the older behavior from [#4774](https://github.com/mochajs/mocha/issues/4774). This report is only about a local config losing to a higher-priority filename farther up the tree.

```
mkdir -p /tmp/mocha-rc/child
printf '%s\n' "module.exports = { grep: 'from-parent' };" > /tmp/mocha-rc/.mocharc.cjs
printf '%s\n' "module.exports = { grep: 'from-child' };" > /tmp/mocha-rc/child/.mocharc.js
printf '%s\n' "it('from-child', () => {});" "it('from-parent', () => {});" > /tmp/mocha-rc/child/test.js
cd /tmp/mocha-rc/child
npx --yes mocha@12.0.1 test.js   # runs "from-child"
npx --yes mocha@12.0.3 test.js   # runs "from-parent"
```
### Versions

Mocha 12.0.1 uses the local .mocharc.js.
Mocha 12.0.2 and 12.0.3 use the parent .mocharc.cjs.
Reproduced with Node.js v22.22.0.

### Additional Info

This came in with [#6342](https://github.com/mochajs/mocha/pull/6342) (a652ff5), the find-up-simple workaround for [#6319](https://github.com/mochajs/mocha/issues/6319). The PR says filename order matches find-up. find-up's multi-name search is per directory; this loop is per filename across the whole tree.

The tests added there stub findUpSync and assert call order. They never place a local .mocharc.js next to an ancestor .mocharc.cjs. [#6345](https://github.com/mochajs/mocha/issues/6345) asks for those same stub tests.

Parent lookup when the current directory has no config file is the older behavior from [#4774](https://github.com/mochajs/mocha/issues/4774). ### Expected

I expected `--clear-screen` to fully clear previous output from the terminal so that only output from the latest run is available afterwards

### Actual

The rerun output gets positioned at the top of the terminal, but I can still scroll back to output from previous reruns.

### Minimal, Complete and Verifiable Example

`mocha --watch --clear-screen` with any tests

### Versions

mocha 12.0.3

### Additional Info

I don't really understand the point of what `--clear-screen` currently does.  To me the whole point of clearing the screen is that when the test output is large, it's hard to scroll back to where the current run started, unless you clear the screen AND kill scrollback to all previous output.

Even if large output begins at the top of the terminal with `--clear-screen`, once you scroll down, if you need to scroll back up to the start of the last run, it's easy to overshoot it and wind up in the middle of previous runs.

If you fully clear all previous output, then you can get to the start of the latest test output by just scrolling up.

### Overview

Three tests in `test/integration/plugins/root-hooks.spec.cjs` fail without nyc because #6078 changed two ESM fixtures to .js under `"type": "commonjs"`. nyc masks this by letting Node infer the module type from the syntax. same issue as #6214 and it needs fixing before dropping nyc (my #6351).

i would rename root-hook-defs-esm.fixture.js back to `.mjs` and move `root-hook-defs-esm-broken.fixture.js` to a folder without a `type` field. All 8 tests should then pass with and without nyc.

### Additional Info

Repro on main, Win. 11, node 24.17.0:

```sh
node bin/mocha.js test/integration/plugins/root-hooks.spec.cjs # 5 passing and 3 failing
npx nyc node bin/mocha.js test/integration/plugins/root-hooks.spec.cjs # 8 passing
```

A tiny require hook that only drops that module type makes them pass too and the same hook passing it along doesn't so it's exactly that part of nyc. With the fix every test-node script also passes without nyc for me. So these 3 are the only tests nyc was hiding.

A sample app depending on both `mockito-android:5.23.0` and `mockk-android:1.14.11` (latest version at the time of writing) leads to a build time failure. This:

- prevents any Android project that is depending on both frameworks from being able to upgrade to 5.23.0 
- prevents any mockito based Android project from adopting `mockk` (`mockk-android`) alongside mockito

5.23.0 added the `dispatcher.jar` in #3792, as a result of the dependency on dexmaker.
Unfortunately MockK packages [its own](https://github.com/mockk/mockk/blob/v1.14.11/modules/mockk-agent-android/build.gradle.kts#L57) `dispatcher.jar`, which has different content as it includes its own impl, i.e. they're not interchangeable.

Mockito initially evaluated a similar solution (#3789) but [ultimately went for](https://github.com/mockito/mockito/pull/3789#issuecomment-3986860383) depending directly on dexmaker.

The resulting build error is:
```
2 files found with path 'dispatcher.jar' from inputs:
 - io.mockk:mockk-agent-android:1.14.11/classes.jar
 - com.linkedin.dexmaker:dexmaker-mockito-inline:2.28.6/classes.jar
Adding a packaging block may help, please refer to
https://developer.android.com/reference/tools/gradle-api/com/android/build/api/dsl/Packaging
for more information
```

Note that both implementations are hardcoded with the `dispatcher.jar` filename
mockito 5.23.0: because it depends on dexmaker, which hardcodes the filename [here](https://github.com/linkedin/dexmaker/blob/2.28.6/dexmaker-mockito-inline/src/main/java/com/android/dx/mockito/inline/InlineDexmakerMockMaker.java#L61)
mockk 1.14.11: https://github.com/mockk/mockk/blob/v1.14.11/modules/mockk-agent-android/src/main/kotlin/io/mockk/proxy/android/AndroidMockKAgentFactory.kt#L204


At first look I'm tempted to say this would be easily fixed by MockK renaming the jar to clarify it's mockk's version, but I was wondering if there's anything that can be done on this side of the fence.

Mockito does not build its own dispatcher jar, as presented above, so modifying the filename would not be as easy.

### Summary

I expect Collapse to be able to handle flexbox layout transition.

### Examples

https://stackblitz.com/edit/github-nb4cly3i?file=src%2FApp.tsx

In the example there are 3 columns, the left one is collapsed.
Hit the `Collapse`/`FlexCollapse` button to toggle which component is used.
Hit the `Open`/`Close` button to see the transition in action.
Change the flex input.

### Motivation

body_text:
### Context

Wave 1, item 1. Tracking issue: mui/material-ui#49260.

Icon-only buttons need an accessible name. Focus on 1.1.1 Non-text Content and 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value. Reuse the `ButtonBase` evidence from the Button report.

### Scope

1. Add axe tests and fixtures in `test/regressions/a11y/fixtures/`.
2. Write `IconButton/accessibility.md`.
3. Enroll it in the CSS-dependent suite (1.4.10, 1.4.4, 1.4.12).
4. Run `pnpm a11y:scorecard`.

### Manual tests

Write each check in the report as numbered **Manual testing steps**, as in `Button/accessibility.md`. `pnpm a11y:scorecard` then adds them to `manual-testing.md`. For screen-reader steps, use NVDA with Chrome and VoiceOver with Safari.

- [ ] **1.1.1, 4.1.2** — With a screen reader, press <kbd>Tab</kbd> to each icon-only button. Each one announces its action from `aria-label`, and the icon is silent.
- [ ] **4.1.2** — Focus a disabled IconButton and an `href` IconButton. The screen reader announces "disabled" and "link".
- [ ] **2.4.7** — Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> to an IconButton, also with `disableRipple`. A visible focus indicator shows.
- [ ] **1.4.11** — With a contrast checker, measure the icon and the focus indicator against the background. Each is at least 3:1.
- [ ] **1.4.1** — In grayscale (DevTools > Rendering > Emulate vision deficiencies > Achromatopsia), the purpose of each colored IconButton stays clear.
- [ ] **2.5.8** — Measure `size="small"`. The target is at least 24 × 24 CSS px, or it has enough spacing.

### Done when

* IconButton has a report and is in the scorecard.
* Each manual test in this issue has steps and a result in the report.

### Context

Wave 1, item 2. Tracking issue: mui/material-ui#49260.

Fab reuses most of the Button report. Check the accessible name of icon-only Fabs (1.1.1, 4.1.2) and the color contrast of the variants (1.4.3, 1.4.11).

### Scope

1. Add axe tests and fixtures in `test/regressions/a11y/fixtures/`.
2. Write `Fab/accessibility.md`.
3. Enroll it in the CSS-dependent suite (1.4.10, 1.4.4, 1.4.12).
4. Run `pnpm a11y:scorecard`.

### Manual tests

Write each check in the report as numbered **Manual testing steps**, as in `Button/accessibility.md`. `pnpm a11y:scorecard` then adds them to `manual-testing.md`. For screen-reader steps, use NVDA with Chrome and VoiceOver with Safari.

- [ ] **1.1.1, 4.1.2** — With a screen reader, focus an icon-only Fab and an extended Fab. The icon-only Fab announces its `aria-label`. The extended Fab announces its visible text.
- [ ] **1.4.3** — With a contrast checker, measure the label and the icon against the fill for each color, in the resting, hover and active states.
- [ ] **1.4.11, 2.4.7** — Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> to the Fab. The focus indicator shows, and it is at least 3:1 against the fill and the page.
- [ ] **2.4.11** — Put the Fab in a fixed position at the bottom of a long page. Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> through the content behind it. The Fab does not fully hide a focused element.
- [ ] **1.4.1** — In grayscale, the purpose of the Fab stays clear.

### Done when

* Fab has a report and is in the scorecard.
* Each manual test in this issue has steps and a result in the report.

### Context

Wave 1, item 3. Tracking issue: mui/material-ui#49260.

ButtonGroup reuses most of the Button report. Check the `role="group"` and its label (1.3.1, 4.1.2), and the contrast of the dividers (1.4.11).

### Scope

1. Add axe tests and fixtures in `test/regressions/a11y/fixtures/`.
2. Write `ButtonGroup/accessibility.md`.
3. Enroll it in the CSS-dependent suite (1.4.10, 1.4.4, 1.4.12).
4. Run `pnpm a11y:scorecard`.

### Manual tests

Write each check in the report as numbered **Manual testing steps**, as in `Button/accessibility.md`. `pnpm a11y:scorecard` then adds them to `manual-testing.md`. For screen-reader steps, use NVDA with Chrome and VoiceOver with Safari.

- [ ] **1.3.1, 4.1.2** — With a screen reader, press <kbd>Tab</kbd> into a ButtonGroup that has an `aria-label`. The screen reader announces "group" and the name.
- [ ] **1.3.2, 2.4.3** — Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> through a horizontal and a vertical group. The focus order matches the visual order.
- [ ] **2.4.7** — The focus indicator of each button is fully visible. The adjacent buttons do not clip it.
- [ ] **1.4.11** — With a contrast checker, measure the dividers and the `outlined` border. Each is at least 3:1 against the page.
- [ ] **4.1.2** — In the split button demo, the arrow button announces its name, "expanded" or "collapsed", and that it opens a menu.

### Done when

* ButtonGroup has a report and is in the scorecard.
* Each manual test in this issue has steps and a result in the report.

### Context

Wave 1, item 4. Tracking issue: mui/material-ui#49260.

CircularProgress probably has the same gaps as LinearProgress: 4.1.3 Status Messages and 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide. Reuse the LinearProgress report as the template.

### Scope

1. Add axe tests and fixtures in `test/regressions/a11y/fixtures/`.
2. Write `CircularProgress/accessibility.md`.
3. Enroll it in the CSS-dependent suite (1.4.10, 1.4.4, 1.4.12).
4. Run `pnpm a11y:scorecard`.

### Manual tests

Write each check in the report as numbered **Manual testing steps**, as in `Button/accessibility.md`. `pnpm a11y:scorecard` then adds them to `manual-testing.md`. For screen-reader steps, use NVDA with Chrome and VoiceOver with Safari.

- [ ] **4.1.2** — With a screen reader, go to a determinate and an indeterminate CircularProgress. The determinate one announces "progress bar" and its value. The indeterminate one announces "progress bar" with no value.
- [ ] **4.1.3** — Move focus away while the value changes. Record if the screen reader announces the change. The probable result is "not announced", the same as LinearProgress.
- [ ] **2.2.2** — Look at the indeterminate animation. Record that the component has no pause control. Check the behavior with `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.
- [ ] **2.3.1** — No part flashes more than three times per second.
- [ ] **1.4.11** — With a contrast checker, measure the arc against the page for each color, in light and dark mode. The arc is at least 3:1.

### Done when

* CircularProgress has a report and is in the scorecard.
* Each manual test in this issue has steps and a result in the report.

Wave 1, item 5. Tracking issue: mui/material-ui#49260.

The Checkbox, Radio and Switch reports already test FormControlLabel indirectly. Check the label association (1.3.1, 2.5.3 Label in Name) and the target size of the label (2.5.8).

### Scope

1. Add axe tests and fixtures in `test/regressions/a11y/fixtures/`.
2. Write `FormControlLabel/accessibility.md`.
3. Enroll it in the CSS-dependent suite (1.4.10, 1.4.4, 1.4.12).

Write each check in the report as numbered **Manual testing steps**, as in `Button/accessibility.md`. `pnpm a11y:scorecard` then adds them to `manual-testing.md`. For screen-reader steps, use NVDA with Chrome and VoiceOver with Safari.

- [ ] **2.5.3** — With macOS Voice Control, say "Click" and the visible label. The control toggles.
- [ ] **2.5.8** — Click the label text. The control toggles, so the label is part of the target.

- [ ] **3.3.2** — With `required`, the asterisk shows, and the screen reader announces "required".
- [ ] **1.4.3** — With a contrast checker, measure the label text. It is at least 4.5:1. The disabled label is exempt.

### Done when

* FormControlLabel has a report and is in the scorecard.
* Each manual test in this issue has steps and a result in the report.

### Context

Wave 1, item 6. Tracking issue: mui/material-ui#49260.

The TextField and RadioGroup reports already test FormLabel indirectly. Check the required indicator (1.3.1, 3.3.2) and the error and disabled contrast (1.4.3).

### Scope

1. Add axe tests and fixtures in `test/regressions/a11y/fixtures/`.
2. Write `FormLabel/accessibility.md`.
3. Enroll it in the CSS-dependent suite (1.4.10, 1.4.4, 1.4.12).
4. Run `pnpm a11y:scorecard`.

### Manual tests

Write each check in the report as numbered **Manual testing steps**, as in `Button/accessibility.md`. `pnpm a11y:scorecard` then adds them to `manual-testing.md`. For screen-reader steps, use NVDA with Chrome and VoiceOver with Safari.

- [ ] **1.3.1** — With a screen reader, press <kbd>Tab</kbd> into a group with `FormLabel component="legend"`. The screen reader announces the label as the group name.
- [ ] **3.3.2** — With `required`, the asterisk shows. The screen reader announces "required" from the control, not only "star".

### Context

Wave 1, item 7. Tracking issue: mui/material-ui#49260.

The TextField report already tests FormHelperText indirectly. Check the `aria-describedby` association (1.3.1), error identification (3.3.1) and announcement of errors (4.1.3).

### Scope

1. Add axe tests and fixtures in `test/regressions/a11y/fixtures/`.
2. Write `FormHelperText/accessibility.md`.
3. Enroll it in the CSS-dependent suite (1.4.10, 1.4.4, 1.4.12).
4. Run `pnpm a11y:scorecard`.

### Manual tests

Write each check in the report as numbered **Manual testing steps**, as in `Button/accessibility.md`. `pnpm a11y:scorecard` then adds them to `manual-testing.md`. For screen-reader steps, use NVDA with Chrome and VoiceOver with Safari.

- [ ] **1.3.1** — With a screen reader, press <kbd>Tab</kbd> to a TextField with helper text. The screen reader reads the helper text as the description after the name.
- [ ] **3.3.1** — In the error state, the helper text names the error in words, for example "Enter a valid email".
- [ ] **4.1.3** — Cause an error on blur, then move focus to the next field. Record if the screen reader announces the new error text. The probable result is "not announced".
- [ ] **1.4.3** — With a contrast checker, measure the helper text and the error text on the `outlined`, `filled` and `standard` variants. Each is at least 4.5:1.
- [ ] **1.4.4** — At 200% page zoom, long helper text wraps and is not clipped.

### Done when

* FormHelperText has a report and is in the scorecard.
* Each manual test in this issue has steps and a result in the report.

### Context

Wave 1, item 10. Tracking issue: mui/material-ui#49260.

Check the roles of clickable and static chips (4.1.2), the keyboard behavior of the delete action (2.1.1), the name of the delete icon (1.1.1) and the target size of the delete icon (2.5.8).

### Scope

1. Add axe tests and fixtures in `test/regressions/a11y/fixtures/`.
2. Write `Chip/accessibility.md`.
3. Enroll it in the CSS-dependent suite (1.4.10, 1.4.4, 1.4.12).
4. Run `pnpm a11y:scorecard`.

### Manual tests

Write each check in the report as numbered **Manual testing steps**, as in `Button/accessibility.md`. `pnpm a11y:scorecard` then adds them to `manual-testing.md`. For screen-reader steps, use NVDA with Chrome and VoiceOver with Safari.

- [ ] **2.1.1** — Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> to a deletable chip, then press <kbd>Backspace</kbd> or <kbd>Delete</kbd>. The chip is removed. A clickable chip activates with <kbd>Enter</kbd> and <kbd>Space</kbd>.
- [ ] **4.1.2** — With a screen reader, focus a clickable chip. It announces "button" and its label. A static chip is not in the <kbd>Tab</kbd> order.
- [ ] **1.1.1** — With a screen reader, the delete icon is silent. Record how a screen-reader user learns that the chip can be deleted.
- [ ] **2.4.3** — Delete a chip with the keyboard. Record where focus goes. Focus must not go to the top of the page.
- [ ] **2.5.8** — Measure the delete icon on a `size="small"` chip. It is at least 24 × 24 CSS px, or it has enough spacing.
- [ ] **1.4.3, 1.4.11** — With a contrast checker, measure the label for each color and variant. Also measure the `outlined` border. The label is at least 4.5:1, and the border is at least 3:1.

### Done when

* Chip has a report and is in the scorecard.
* Each manual test in this issue has steps and a result in the report.

body_text:
### Context

Wave 2, item 1. Tracking issue: mui/material-ui#49260.

Assess Dialog first in this wave. Focus trap, focus restore and labelling come from `Modal`. Drawer, Popover, Menu and Select reuse this evidence, so write the `Modal` findings so that later reports can refer to them.

Focus on 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap (Escape closes), 2.4.3 Focus Order (initial focus and focus restore), 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured, 4.1.2 (`role="dialog"`, `aria-modal`, `aria-labelledby` with DialogTitle) and 1.4.10 Reflow (full-screen dialogs at 320 px).

### Scope

1. Add axe tests and fixtures in `test/regressions/a11y/fixtures/`.
2. Write `Dialog/accessibility.md`.
3. Enroll it in the CSS-dependent suite (1.4.10, 1.4.4, 1.4.12).
4. Run `pnpm a11y:scorecard`.

### Manual tests

Write each check in the report as numbered **Manual testing steps**, as in `Button/accessibility.md`. `pnpm a11y:scorecard` then adds them to `manual-testing.md`. For screen-reader steps, use NVDA with Chrome and VoiceOver with Safari.

- [ ] **2.4.3** — Open the Dialog with the keyboard. Focus moves into the Dialog. Close it. Focus goes back to the trigger.
- [ ] **2.1.2** — Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> and <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>Tab</kbd> past the last and the first element. Focus stays in the Dialog. <kbd>Escape</kbd> closes the Dialog.

body_text:
### Context

Wave 2, item 7. Tracking issue: mui/material-ui#49260.

Tooltip uses Popper, not `Modal`. 1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus is a probable ⚠️ rating. Check that the tooltip is dismissible (Escape), hoverable and persistent.

Also check 4.1.2 and 1.3.1 (`aria-describedby` or `aria-label` with `describeChild`), 2.1.1 (keyboard focus opens it) and tooltips on disabled buttons.

### Scope

1. Add axe tests and fixtures in `test/regressions/a11y/fixtures/`.
2. Write `Tooltip/accessibility.md`.
3. Enroll it in the CSS-dependent suite (1.4.10, 1.4.4, 1.4.12).
4. Run `pnpm a11y:scorecard`.

### Manual tests

Write each check in the report as numbered **Manual testing steps**, as in `Button/accessibility.md`. `pnpm a11y:scorecard` then adds them to `manual-testing.md`. For screen-reader steps, use NVDA with Chrome and VoiceOver with Safari.

- [ ] **1.4.13 dismissible** — Show the Tooltip with hover, then press <kbd>Escape</kbd> without moving the pointer or focus. The Tooltip hides.
- [ ] **1.4.13 hoverable** — Move the pointer from the trigger onto the Tooltip. The Tooltip stays visible. Repeat with `disableInteractive`, and record the result.
- [ ] **1.4.13 persistent** — Keep the pointer on the trigger. The Tooltip stays until the pointer or the focus leaves. It does not time out.
- [ ] **2.1.1** — Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> to the trigger. The Tooltip shows on keyboard focus.
- [ ] **1.3.1, 4.1.2** — With a screen reader, focus an icon-only button with a Tooltip. The title is the name. Use `describeChild` on a labelled button. The title is the description.
- [ ] **2.1.1** — Put a Tooltip on a disabled button that is wrapped in a `span`. Record that keyboard and screen-reader users cannot get the Tooltip.
- [ ] **1.4.3, 1.4.4** — The Tooltip text is at least 4.5:1, and at 200% zoom it is fully visible.

### Done when

* Tooltip has a report and is in the scorecard.
* Each manual test in this issue has steps and a result in the report.

### Context

Wave 2, item 8. Tracking issue: mui/material-ui#49260.

Focus on 4.1.3 Status Messages (the live region on SnackbarContent) and 2.2.1 Timing Adjustable (`autoHideDuration`, pause on hover, focus and window blur). Also check 2.4.3: users must be able to reach the actions with the keyboard before the Snackbar closes.

This component can probably share the known gap "Dynamic state changes are not announced" (mui/material-ui#49253).

### Scope

1. Add axe tests and fixtures in `test/regressions/a11y/fixtures/`.
2. Write `Snackbar/accessibility.md`.
3. Enroll it in the CSS-dependent suite (1.4.10, 1.4.4, 1.4.12).
4. Run `pnpm a11y:scorecard`.

### Manual tests

Write each check in the report as numbered **Manual testing steps**, as in `Button/accessibility.md`. `pnpm a11y:scorecard` then adds them to `manual-testing.md`. For screen-reader steps, use NVDA with Chrome and VoiceOver with Safari.

- [ ] **4.1.3** — With a screen reader, keep focus on a button that opens a Snackbar, then press it. The screen reader announces the message, and focus does not move.
- [ ] **2.2.1** — With `autoHideDuration`, move the pointer onto the Snackbar, then move focus into it. The timer pauses in both cases. Switch to another window. The timer pauses.
- [ ] **2.1.1, 2.4.3** — Open a Snackbar with an action. Using only the keyboard, reach and press the action before the Snackbar hides. Record how many <kbd>Tab</kbd> presses it needs.
- [ ] **2.4.11** — With a Snackbar open, press <kbd>Tab</kbd> through the content behind it. The Snackbar does not fully hide a focused element.
- [ ] **1.4.3** — With a contrast checker, measure the message and the action text. Each is at least 4.5:1.

### Done when

* Snackbar has a report and is in the scorecard.
* Each manual test in this issue has steps and a result in the report.

### Context

Wave 2, item 5. Tracking issue: mui/material-ui#49260.

Focus on 4.1.2 (`menuitem`, `menuitemcheckbox` and `menuitemradio` roles, and the selected and disabled states), 1.4.11 (contrast of the focus and selected states) and 2.5.8 Target Size (dense items).

### Scope

1. Add axe tests and fixtures in `test/regressions/a11y/fixtures/`.
2. Write `MenuItem/accessibility.md`.
3. Enroll it in the CSS-dependent suite (1.4.10, 1.4.4, 1.4.12).
4. Run `pnpm a11y:scorecard`.

### Manual tests

Write each check in the report as numbered **Manual testing steps**, as in `Button/accessibility.md`. `pnpm a11y:scorecard` then adds them to `manual-testing.md`. For screen-reader steps, use NVDA with Chrome and VoiceOver with Safari.

- [ ] **4.1.2** — With a screen reader, move to a normal, a disabled and a `selected` MenuItem. The screen reader announces "menu item", "disabled" and the selected state.
- [ ] **4.1.2** — Use `role="menuitemcheckbox"` or `"menuitemradio"` with `aria-checked`. The screen reader announces "checked" and "not checked".
- [ ] **1.4.1** — In grayscale, the selected item stays distinguishable, for example with a check icon.
- [ ] **1.4.11, 2.4.7** — With a contrast checker, measure the focus and selected backgrounds against the Menu background. Record the ratios.
- [ ] **2.5.8** — Measure a `dense` MenuItem. Its height is at least 24 CSS px.

### Done when

* MenuItem has a report and is in the scorecard.
* Each manual test in this issue has steps and a result in the report.

### Context

Wave 2, item 6. Tracking issue: mui/material-ui#49260.

MenuList contains the roving focus and the typeahead logic. Menu and Select use it. Assess it as a standalone component, for example in a composition with Popper.

Focus on 2.1.1 (arrow keys, Home, End, typeahead, disabled items) and 2.4.3 (focus order and wrap-around).

### Scope

1. Add axe tests and fixtures in `test/regressions/a11y/fixtures/`.
2. Write `MenuList/accessibility.md`.
3. Enroll it in the CSS-dependent suite (1.4.10, 1.4.4, 1.4.12).
4. Run `pnpm a11y:scorecard`.

### Manual tests

Write each check in the report as numbered **Manual testing steps**, as in `Button/accessibility.md`. `pnpm a11y:scorecard` then adds them to `manual-testing.md`. For screen-reader steps, use NVDA with Chrome and VoiceOver with Safari.

- [ ] **2.1.1** — In a standalone MenuList, use <kbd>↑</kbd>, <kbd>↓</kbd>, <kbd>Home</kbd>, <kbd>End</kbd> and typeahead with one and with more characters. Focus moves to the correct item.
- [ ] **2.1.1** — Disabled items are skipped. With `disabledItemsFocusable`, they get focus.
- [ ] **2.4.3** — At the last item, <kbd>↓</kbd> wraps to the first item. With `disableListWrap`, it does not wrap.
- [ ] **2.4.3** — With `autoFocusItem`, the first item gets focus when the list mounts.
- [ ] **4.1.2** — With a screen reader, the list announces "menu" and the item count.

### Done when

* MenuList has a report and is in the scorecard.
* Each manual test in this issue has steps and a result in the report.

body_text:
### Context

Wave 3, item 1. Tracking issue: mui/material-ui#49260.

Select builds on Menu from Wave 2, so reuse that evidence. Assess NativeSelect in the same period, because it is a useful accessible alternative.

Focus on 4.1.2 (`combobox` and `listbox` roles, `aria-expanded`, `aria-labelledby` with the InputLabel), 2.1.1 (open with Enter, Space, arrow keys, typeahead), 2.4.3 (focus restore), 3.3.2 (label and helper text) and the `multiple` variant.

### Scope

1. Add axe tests and fixtures in `test/regressions/a11y/fixtures/`.
2. Write `Select/accessibility.md`.
3. Enroll it in the CSS-dependent suite (1.4.10, 1.4.4, 1.4.12).
4. Run `pnpm a11y:scorecard`.

### Manual tests

Write each check in the report as numbered **Manual testing steps**, as in `Button/accessibility.md`. `pnpm a11y:scorecard` then adds them to `manual-testing.md`. For screen-reader steps, use NVDA with Chrome and VoiceOver with Safari.

- [ ] **2.1.1** — Open the Select with <kbd>Enter</kbd>, <kbd>Space</kbd>, <kbd>↑</kbd> and <kbd>↓</kbd>. Use typeahead. <kbd>Escape</kbd> closes it and keeps the old value.
- [ ] **2.4.3** — Select an option. Focus goes back to the Select.
- [ ] **4.1.2** — With a screen reader, focus the Select. It announces the InputLabel as the name, the current value, "collapsed" and that it opens a list.
- [ ] **4.1.2** — With the list open, the screen reader announces each option and its selected state. With `multiple`, it announces that more than one option can be selected.
- [ ] **3.3.2, 1.3.1** — The Select has a visible label. The screen reader reads the helper text as the description.
- [ ] **1.4.11** — With a contrast checker, measure the `outlined` border and the arrow icon. Each is at least 3:1. The TextField border is a known failure, so record the result.
- [ ] **1.4.10** — At 320 CSS px width, the list stays in the viewport and scrolls.

### Done when

* Select has a report and is in the scorecard.
* Each manual test in this issue has steps and a result in the report.

### Context

Wave 3, item 2. Tracking issue: mui/material-ui#49260.

NativeSelect uses the native `<select>` element, so the browser supplies most of the semantics. Its report gives users a documented accessible alternative to Select. Reuse the TextField evidence for the label, helper text and contrast.

### Scope

1. Add axe tests and fixtures in `test/regressions/a11y/fixtures/`.
2. Write `NativeSelect/accessibility.md`.
3. Enroll it in the CSS-dependent suite (1.4.10, 1.4.4, 1.4.12).
4. Run `pnpm a11y:scorecard`.

### Manual tests

Write each check in the report as numbered **Manual testing steps**, as in `Button/accessibility.md`. `pnpm a11y:scorecard` then adds them to `manual-testing.md`. For screen-reader steps, use NVDA with Chrome and VoiceOver with Safari. Also use VoiceOver with Safari on iOS.

- [ ] **4.1.2** — With a screen reader, focus the NativeSelect. It announces the label, the value and the native role of the platform.
- [ ] **2.1.1** — Change the value with the keyboard only. On iOS, the native picker opens and works with VoiceOver.
- [ ] **3.3.2, 1.3.1** — The NativeSelect has a visible label. The screen reader reads the helper text as the description.
- [ ] **1.4.3** — With a contrast checker, measure the value text. It is at least 4.5:1.
- [ ] **1.4.11** — Measure the border and the arrow icon. Each is at least 3:1.

### Done when

* NativeSelect has a report and is in the scorecard.
* Each manual test in this issue has steps and a result in the report.

### Context

Wave 3, item 4. Tracking issue: mui/material-ui#49260.

Include Tab and TabScrollButton. Focus on 4.1.2 (`tablist`, `tab` and `tabpanel` roles, `aria-selected`, `aria-controls`), 2.1.1 (arrow keys, Home, End, manual and automatic activation), 1.4.11 (contrast of the indicator), 1.4.10 Reflow (scrollable tabs at 320 px) and the scroll buttons, which are hidden from assistive technology.

### Scope

1. Add axe tests and fixtures in `test/regressions/a11y/fixtures/`.
2. Write `Tabs/accessibility.md`.
3. Enroll it in the CSS-dependent suite (1.4.10, 1.4.4, 1.4.12).
4. Run `pnpm a11y:scorecard`.

### Manual tests

Write each check in the report as numbered **Manual testing steps**, as in `Button/accessibility.md`. `pnpm a11y:scorecard` then adds them to `manual-testing.md`. For screen-reader steps, use NVDA with Chrome and VoiceOver with Safari.

- [ ] **2.1.1** — Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> into the tab list. Focus goes to the selected tab. Use <kbd>←</kbd> and <kbd>→</kbd> (<kbd>↑</kbd> and <kbd>↓</kbd> for `vertical`), <kbd>Home</kbd> and <kbd>End</kbd>.
- [ ] **2.1.1** — With `selectionFollowsFocus`, the arrow keys change the panel. Without it, <kbd>Enter</kbd> or <kbd>Space</kbd> changes the panel.
- [ ] **4.1.2** — With a screen reader, the screen reader announces "tab", the name, "selected" and the position, for example "2 of 4". The panel is announced with the name of its tab.
- [ ] **1.4.1, 1.4.11** — In grayscale, the selected tab stays distinguishable by the indicator. The indicator is at least 3:1 against the background.
- [ ] **2.4.7** — The focused tab shows a visible focus indicator.
- [ ] **1.4.10** — With `variant="scrollable"` at 320 CSS px width, all tabs are reachable with the keyboard. The scroll buttons are silent for the screen reader.

### Done when

* Tabs has a report and is in the scorecard.
* Each manual test in this issue has steps and a result in the report.

body_text:
### Context

Wave 3, item 5. Tracking issue: mui/material-ui#49260.

Focus on 2.5.7 Dragging Movements (new in WCAG 2.2; check the click-on-track and keyboard alternatives), 4.1.2 (`aria-valuetext` and `getAriaValueText`, the label of each thumb in range sliders), 2.1.1 (arrow keys, Page Up, Page Down, Home, End), 2.5.8 Target Size (thumb) and 1.4.11 (contrast of the track and the thumb).

### Scope

1. Add axe tests and fixtures in `test/regressions/a11y/fixtures/`.
2. Write `Slider/accessibility.md`.
3. Enroll it in the CSS-dependent suite (1.4.10, 1.4.4, 1.4.12).
4. Run `pnpm a11y:scorecard`.

### Manual tests

Write each check in the report as numbered **Manual testing steps**, as in `Button/accessibility.md`. `pnpm a11y:scorecard` then adds them to `manual-testing.md`. For screen-reader steps, use NVDA with Chrome and VoiceOver with Safari.

- [ ] **2.1.1** — Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> to the thumb. Change the value with the arrow keys, <kbd>Page Up</kbd>, <kbd>Page Down</kbd>, <kbd>Home</kbd> and <kbd>End</kbd>. On a range Slider, do this for both thumbs.
- [ ] **2.5.7** — Click a point on the track. The value changes without a drag.
- [ ] **4.1.2** — With a screen reader, the thumb announces "slider", its name and its value. With `getAriaValueText`, it announces the text with the unit, for example "20°C".
- [ ] **4.1.2** — On a range Slider, each thumb has its own name, for example "Minimum price" and "Maximum price".
- [ ] **1.4.11** — With a contrast checker, measure the thumb, the track and the rail. Each is at least 3:1 against the adjacent colors.
- [ ] **2.5.8** — Measure the thumb on `size="small"`. The target is at least 24 × 24 CSS px, or it has enough spacing.
- [ ] **1.4.4** — At 200% zoom, the mark labels and the value label are fully visible.
