### Context

Wave 3, item 3. Tracking issue: mui/material-ui#49260.

Autocomplete is the most important component in this wave and the most difficult one. Do it after Select. Plan more time than for the other reports, and consider one PR for each variant group.

Focus on 4.1.2 (combobox with listbox, `aria-activedescendant`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-autocomplete`), 4.1.3 (announcement of the result count and "No options"), 2.1.1 (arrow keys, Escape, Enter, Home and End in the input), 2.4.3, and the variants: `multiple` with chips (delete with Backspace), `freeSolo`, grouped options and async loading.

### Scope

1. Add axe tests and fixtures in `test/regressions/a11y/fixtures/`.
2. Write `Autocomplete/accessibility.md`.
3. Enroll it in the CSS-dependent suite (1.4.10, 1.4.4, 1.4.12).
4. Run `pnpm a11y:scorecard`.

### Manual tests

Write each check in the report as numbered **Manual testing steps**, as in `Button/accessibility.md`. `pnpm a11y:scorecard` then adds them to `manual-testing.md`. For screen-reader steps, use NVDA with Chrome and VoiceOver with Safari. Test both screen readers, because their support of `aria-activedescendant` is different.

- [ ] **2.1.1** — In the input, <kbd>↓</kbd> opens the list. The arrow keys move through the options. <kbd>Enter</kbd> selects. The first <kbd>Escape</kbd> closes the list, and the second clears the input. <kbd>Home</kbd> and <kbd>End</kbd> move the caret.
- [ ] **4.1.2** — With a screen reader, focus the input. It announces "combo box", the name and "collapsed". Move through the options. The screen reader announces each active option.
- [ ] **4.1.3** — Type a value that filters the list. Record if the screen reader announces the result count, "No options" and "Loading…". The probable result is "not announced".
- [ ] **2.1.1, 4.1.2** — With `multiple`, <kbd>Backspace</kbd> in an empty input removes the last chip. <kbd>←</kbd> and <kbd>→</kbd> move between the chips. The screen reader announces each chip.
- [ ] **4.1.2** — The clear button and the popup button announce their names, "Clear" and "Open" or "Close".
- [ ] **2.1.1** — With `freeSolo`, <kbd>Enter</kbd> accepts a typed value. With grouped options, the screen reader announces the group headers.
- [ ] **2.4.11, 1.4.10** — At 320 CSS px width, the list stays in the viewport and does not fully hide the input.

### Done when

* Autocomplete has a report and is in the scorecard.
* Each manual test in this issue has steps and a result in the report.

### Context

Wave 4, item 2. Tracking issue: mui/material-ui#49260.

Focus on the names of the navigation buttons (4.1.2), the label of the rows-per-page Select (3.3.2), announcement of the displayed rows (4.1.3) and Reflow (1.4.10).

### Scope

1. Add axe tests and fixtures in `test/regressions/a11y/fixtures/`.

- [ ] **1.4.10** — At 320 CSS px width, all controls stay visible and do not overlap.

* Each manual test in this issue has steps and a result in the report.

Wave 4, item 3. Tracking issue: mui/material-ui#49260.

Focus on `aria-sort` on the header cell (4.1.2), the sort direction that only the icon shows (1.1.1, 1.4.1) and the contrast of the sort icon (1.4.11).

### Scope

1. Add axe tests and fixtures in `test/regressions/a11y/fixtures/`.

* Each manual test in this issue has steps and a result in the report.

body_text:
### Context

Wave 4, item 4. Tracking issue: mui/material-ui#49260.

Include PaginationItem. Focus on the `nav` landmark and its label (1.3.1), `aria-current="page"` (4.1.2), the names of the items (`getItemAriaLabel`), the target size (2.5.8) and the contrast of the selected item (1.4.11).

### Scope

1. Add axe tests and fixtures in `test/regressions/a11y/fixtures/`.
2. Write `Pagination/accessibility.md`.
3. Enroll it in the CSS-dependent suite (1.4.10, 1.4.4, 1.4.12).
4. Run `pnpm a11y:scorecard`.

### Manual tests

Write each check in the report as numbered **Manual testing steps**, as in `Button/accessibility.md`. `pnpm a11y:scorecard` then adds them to `manual-testing.md`. For screen-reader steps, use NVDA with Chrome and VoiceOver with Safari.

- [ ] **1.3.1** — With a screen reader, list the landmarks. Pagination shows as a navigation landmark with the name "pagination navigation".
- [ ] **4.1.2** — Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> to the items. Each item announces its name, for example "Go to page 3". The current page announces "current page".
- [ ] **2.4.3** — After a page change, focus stays on the item that was pressed, or moves to a logical place.
- [ ] **1.4.1, 1.4.11** — In grayscale and with the `text` variant, the current page stays distinguishable. Its indicator is at least 3:1.
- [ ] **2.5.8** — Measure the items on `size="small"`. Each is at least 24 × 24 CSS px, or it has enough spacing.
- [ ] **1.4.10** — At 320 CSS px width, the items wrap and no item is lost.

### Done when

* Pagination has a report and is in the scorecard.
* Each manual test in this issue has steps and a result in the report.

### Context

Wave 4, item 5. Tracking issue: mui/material-ui#49260.

Focus on the `nav` landmark and its label (1.3.1), `aria-current` on the last item (4.1.2), separators hidden from assistive technology, and the collapse button (`expandText`, 2.1.1).

### Scope

1. Add axe tests and fixtures in `test/regressions/a11y/fixtures/`.
2. Write `Breadcrumbs/accessibility.md`.
3. Enroll it in the CSS-dependent suite (1.4.10, 1.4.4, 1.4.12).
4. Run `pnpm a11y:scorecard`.

### Manual tests

Write each check in the report as numbered **Manual testing steps**, as in `Button/accessibility.md`. `pnpm a11y:scorecard` then adds them to `manual-testing.md`. For screen-reader steps, use NVDA with Chrome and VoiceOver with Safari.

- [ ] **1.3.1** — With a screen reader, list the landmarks. Breadcrumbs shows as a navigation landmark with the name "breadcrumb". The screen reader announces it as a list with the item count.
- [ ] **4.1.2** — The last item announces "current page" when the author sets `aria-current="page"`.
- [ ] **1.3.1** — The separators are silent.
- [ ] **2.1.1, 2.4.3** — With collapsed items, press <kbd>Tab</kbd> to the ellipsis button. It announces its `expandText` name. Press <kbd>Enter</kbd>. The items expand, and focus moves to the first new item.
- [ ] **1.4.1, 1.4.3** — The links stay distinguishable from the current page without color. The link text is at least 4.5:1.
- [ ] **1.4.10** — At 320 CSS px width, the items wrap and no item is lost.

### Done when

* Breadcrumbs has a report and is in the scorecard.
* Each manual test in this issue has steps and a result in the report.

### Context

Wave 4, item 6. Tracking issue: mui/material-ui#49260.

Include Step, StepButton, StepLabel, StepIcon, StepContent and MobileStepper. Focus on the current step (`aria-current`, 4.1.2), states shown only by the icon or color (1.1.1, 1.4.1), the contrast of StepIcon (1.4.3, 1.4.11) and keyboard access to non-linear steps (2.1.1).

### Scope

1. Add axe tests and fixtures in `test/regressions/a11y/fixtures/`.
2. Write `Stepper/accessibility.md`.
3. Enroll it in the CSS-dependent suite (1.4.10, 1.4.4, 1.4.12).
4. Run `pnpm a11y:scorecard`.

### Manual tests

Write each check in the report as numbered **Manual testing steps**, as in `Button/accessibility.md`. `pnpm a11y:scorecard` then adds them to `manual-testing.md`. For screen-reader steps, use NVDA with Chrome and VoiceOver with Safari.

- [ ] **4.1.2** — With a screen reader, read the Stepper. The active step announces "current step". Record how the screen reader announces the completed and the error states.
- [ ] **1.1.1, 1.4.1** — The completed state (check icon) and the error state (warning icon) are also available as text, not only as an icon or a color.
- [ ] **1.4.3, 1.4.11** — With a contrast checker, measure the number in the StepIcon against its circle and the circle against the page.
- [ ] **2.1.1** — In a non-linear Stepper, press <kbd>Tab</kbd> to each StepButton and activate it with <kbd>Enter</kbd>.
- [ ] **1.1.1** — In MobileStepper, the dots and the progress bar have a text alternative, for example "Step 2 of 6". The Back and Next buttons have names.
- [ ] **1.4.10** — At 320 CSS px width, a horizontal Stepper with `alternativeLabel` does not need horizontal scroll.

### Done when

* Stepper has a report and is in the scorecard.
* Each manual test in this issue has steps and a result in the report.

### Context

Wave 4, item 7. Tracking issue: mui/material-ui#49260.

Include ListItem, ListItemText, ListItemIcon, ListItemAvatar, ListItemSecondaryAction and ListSubheader. Focus on list semantics (1.3.1), the association of ListSubheader with its group, and secondary actions in the reading and focus order (1.3.2, 2.4.3).

### Scope

1. Add axe tests and fixtures in `test/regressions/a11y/fixtures/`.
2. Write `List/accessibility.md`.
3. Enroll it in the CSS-dependent suite (1.4.10, 1.4.4, 1.4.12).
4. Run `pnpm a11y:scorecard`.

### Manual tests

Write each check in the report as numbered **Manual testing steps**, as in `Button/accessibility.md`. `pnpm a11y:scorecard` then adds them to `manual-testing.md`. For screen-reader steps, use NVDA with Chrome and VoiceOver with Safari.

- [ ] **1.3.1** — With a screen reader, go to a List. The screen reader announces "list" and the item count.
- [ ] **1.3.1** — Record how the screen reader relates a ListSubheader to the items under it.
- [ ] **1.3.2, 2.4.3** — In a list with secondary actions, the reading order and the focus order go from the primary content to the secondary action of the same item.
- [ ] **2.4.11** — With a sticky ListSubheader, press <kbd>Tab</kbd> through the items. The subheader does not fully hide a focused element.
- [ ] **1.4.3** — With a contrast checker, measure the primary and the secondary text of ListItemText. Each is at least 4.5:1.

### Done when

* List has a report and is in the scorecard.
* Each manual test in this issue has steps and a result in the report.

### Context

Wave 4, item 8. Tracking issue: mui/material-ui#49260.

ListItemButton uses `ButtonBase`, so reuse the Button evidence. Focus on the selected state (`aria-current` or `aria-selected`, 4.1.2), the contrast of the selected and focus states (1.4.11) and nested navigation lists (1.3.1, 2.4.3).

### Scope

1. Add axe tests and fixtures in `test/regressions/a11y/fixtures/`.
2. Write `ListItemButton/accessibility.md`.
3. Enroll it in the CSS-dependent suite (1.4.10, 1.4.4, 1.4.12).
4. Run `pnpm a11y:scorecard`.

### Manual tests

Write each check in the report as numbered **Manual testing steps**, as in `Button/accessibility.md`. `pnpm a11y:scorecard` then adds them to `manual-testing.md`. For screen-reader steps, use NVDA with Chrome and VoiceOver with Safari.

- [ ] **4.1.2** — With a screen reader, focus a ListItemButton and a ListItemButton with `component="a"`. They announce "button" and "link".
- [ ] **4.1.2** — Focus a `selected` item. Record what the screen reader announces. The author must add `aria-current` or `aria-selected`.
- [ ] **4.1.2** — In a nested list, the parent button announces "expanded" or "collapsed" when the author sets `aria-expanded`.
- [ ] **1.4.1** — In grayscale, the selected item stays distinguishable.
- [ ] **2.4.7, 1.4.11** — Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> to an item. Measure the focus and selected backgrounds. Record the ratios. The tint is probably below 3:1.
- [ ] **2.5.8** — Measure a `dense` item. Its height is at least 24 CSS px.

### Done when

* ListItemButton has a report and is in the scorecard.
* Each manual test in this issue has steps and a result in the report.

### Scope

* BottomNavigation has a report and is in the scorecard.

### Context

Wave 4, item 10. Tracking issue: mui/material-ui#49260.

Rating uses a radio group internally. Reuse the Radio and RadioGroup evidence. Focus on the names of the values (`getLabelText`, 4.1.2), the read-only variant (`role="img"`), half-star precision, 1.4.11 (contrast of the empty icons) and 2.5.8 Target Size.

### Scope

1. Add axe tests and fixtures in `test/regressions/a11y/fixtures/`.
2. Write `Rating/accessibility.md`.
3. Enroll it in the CSS-dependent suite (1.4.10, 1.4.4, 1.4.12).
4. Run `pnpm a11y:scorecard`.

### Manual tests

Write each check in the report as numbered **Manual testing steps**, as in `Button/accessibility.md`. `pnpm a11y:scorecard` then adds them to `manual-testing.md`. For screen-reader steps, use NVDA with Chrome and VoiceOver with Safari.

- [ ] **2.1.1** — Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> into the Rating. Change the value with the arrow keys. With `precision={0.5}`, the arrow keys move in half steps.
- [ ] **4.1.2** — With a screen reader, each value announces "radio button" and the `getLabelText` text, for example "3 Stars", with the checked state.
- [ ] **1.1.1** — With `readOnly`, the screen reader announces the Rating as an image with a name, for example "3.5 Stars".
- [ ] **2.4.7** — The focused value shows a visible focus indicator.
- [ ] **1.4.1, 1.4.11** — In grayscale, the filled and the empty icons stay distinguishable. The empty icon is at least 3:1 against the background.
- [ ] **2.5.8** — Measure each icon on `size="small"`. Each is at least 24 × 24 CSS px, or it has enough spacing.

### Done when

* Rating has a report and is in the scorecard.
* Each manual test in this issue has steps and a result in the report.

### Context

Wave 4, item 12 (lower risk). Tracking issue: mui/material-ui#49260.

Focus on 1.3.1 (assistive technology does not get the badge content unless the parent label includes it) and 1.4.3 (contrast of the badge colors). The `dot` variant has no text alternative.

### Scope

1. Add axe tests and fixtures in `test/regressions/a11y/fixtures/`.
2. Write `Badge/accessibility.md`.
3. Enroll it in the CSS-dependent suite (1.4.10, 1.4.4, 1.4.12).
4. Run `pnpm a11y:scorecard`.

### Manual tests

Write each check in the report as numbered **Manual testing steps**, as in `Button/accessibility.md`. `pnpm a11y:scorecard` then adds them to `manual-testing.md`. For screen-reader steps, use NVDA with Chrome and VoiceOver with Safari.

- [ ] **1.3.1** — With a screen reader, focus an IconButton with a Badge. Record if the screen reader announces the count. The author must put the count in the name, for example "4 new notifications".
- [ ] **1.4.1** — With `variant="dot"`, the information is only a colored dot. Record that the author must add a text alternative.
- [ ] **1.4.3** — With a contrast checker, measure the badge text against the badge color for each color. Each is at least 4.5:1.
- [ ] **1.4.4** — At 200% zoom, the badge content, for example "99+", is not clipped.
- [ ] **1.3.1** — With `invisible`, the screen reader does not announce the badge content.

### Done when

* Badge has a report and is in the scorecard.
* Each manual test in this issue has steps and a result in the report.

### Context

Wave 4, item 13 (lower risk). Tracking issue: mui/material-ui#49260.

Focus on the loading state for assistive technology (`aria-busy`, 4.1.3), 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide (pulse and wave animations) and `prefers-reduced-motion`. Compare with the LinearProgress gaps.

### Scope

1. Add axe tests and fixtures in `test/regressions/a11y/fixtures/`.
2. Write `Skeleton/accessibility.md`.
3. Enroll it in the CSS-dependent suite (1.4.10, 1.4.4, 1.4.12).
4. Run `pnpm a11y:scorecard`.

### Manual tests

Write each check in the report as numbered **Manual testing steps**, as in `Button/accessibility.md`. `pnpm a11y:scorecard` then adds them to `manual-testing.md`. For screen-reader steps, use NVDA with Chrome and VoiceOver with Safari.

- [ ] **4.1.2, 4.1.3** — With a screen reader, read a region that shows Skeletons. Record what the screen reader announces. The author can set `aria-busy` on the region.
- [ ] **4.1.3** — Replace the Skeletons with the content. Record if the screen reader announces the change.
- [ ] **2.2.2** — Look at the `pulse` and `wave` animations. Record if they stop when the content loads, and the behavior with `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.
- [ ] **2.3.1** — No part flashes more than three times per second.

### Done when

* Skeleton has a report and is in the scorecard.
* Each manual test in this issue has steps and a result in the report.

### Context

Wave 4, item 14 (lower risk). Tracking issue: mui/material-ui#49260.

Include CardHeader, CardContent, CardMedia and CardActions. Focus on the heading level of CardHeader (1.3.1), the text alternative of CardMedia (1.1.1) and the contrast of the outlined variant boundary (1.4.11).

### Scope

1. Add axe tests and fixtures in `test/regressions/a11y/fixtures/`.
2. Write `Card/accessibility.md`.
3. Enroll it in the CSS-dependent suite (1.4.10, 1.4.4, 1.4.12).
4. Run `pnpm a11y:scorecard`.

### Manual tests

Write each check in the report as numbered **Manual testing steps**, as in `Button/accessibility.md`. `pnpm a11y:scorecard` then adds them to `manual-testing.md`. For screen-reader steps, use NVDA with Chrome and VoiceOver with Safari.

- [ ] **1.3.1, 2.4.6** — With a screen reader, list the headings. Record if the CardHeader title is a heading. The author sets the level through `slotProps`.
- [ ] **1.1.1** — A CardMedia `img` has an `alt` text. A CardMedia with a background image has `role="img"` and an `aria-label`, or it is decorative.
- [ ] **1.3.2** — The reading order is header, media, content and actions, as on the screen.
- [ ] **1.4.10** — At 320 CSS px width, the Card content scrolls vertically only.
- [ ] **1.4.3** — With a contrast checker, measure the title and the subheader text. Each is at least 4.5:1.

### Done when

* Card has a report and is in the scorecard.
* Each manual test in this issue has steps and a result in the report.

### Context

Wave 4, item 15 (lower risk). Tracking issue: mui/material-ui#49260.

CardActionArea uses `ButtonBase`, so reuse the Button evidence. Focus on the accessible name of a large clickable area (4.1.2, 2.5.3), nested interactive content (4.1.2) and the focus indicator (2.4.7, 1.4.11).

### Scope

1. Add axe tests and fixtures in `test/regressions/a11y/fixtures/`.
2. Write `CardActionArea/accessibility.md`.
3. Enroll it in the CSS-dependent suite (1.4.10, 1.4.4, 1.4.12).
4. Run `pnpm a11y:scorecard`.

### Manual tests

Write each check in the report as numbered **Manual testing steps**, as in `Button/accessibility.md`. `pnpm a11y:scorecard` then adds them to `manual-testing.md`. For screen-reader steps, use NVDA with Chrome and VoiceOver with Safari.

- [ ] **4.1.2, 2.4.6** — With a screen reader, press <kbd>Tab</kbd> to a CardActionArea. Record the full name that the screen reader announces. A long name made from all the content is hard to use.
- [ ] **4.1.2** — Put a button inside the CardActionArea. Record that the screen reader and the keyboard cannot reach it correctly. The author must not nest interactive content.
- [ ] **2.1.1** — <kbd>Enter</kbd> activates the CardActionArea.
- [ ] **2.4.7, 1.4.11** — The focus highlight is visible. Measure it against the Card. Record the ratio. The tint is probably below 3:1.

### Done when

* CardActionArea has a report and is in the scorecard.
* Each manual test in this issue has steps and a result in the report.

### Context

Wave 4, item 16 (lower risk). Tracking issue: mui/material-ui#49260.

Include Toolbar. Focus on the `banner` landmark (1.3.1), the contrast of the color variants (1.4.3), 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (fixed and sticky AppBar over focused content) and 1.4.10 Reflow.

### Scope

1. Add axe tests and fixtures in `test/regressions/a11y/fixtures/`.
2. Write `AppBar/accessibility.md`.
3. Enroll it in the CSS-dependent suite (1.4.10, 1.4.4, 1.4.12).
4. Run `pnpm a11y:scorecard`.

### Manual tests

Write each check in the report as numbered **Manual testing steps**, as in `Button/accessibility.md`. `pnpm a11y:scorecard` then adds them to `manual-testing.md`. For screen-reader steps, use NVDA with Chrome and VoiceOver with Safari.

- [ ] **1.3.1** — With a screen reader, list the landmarks. The AppBar shows as the banner landmark. A page with more than one AppBar has more than one banner. Record this.
- [ ] **2.4.11** — With `position="fixed"` and `"sticky"`, press <kbd>Tab</kbd> through the page while it scrolls. The AppBar does not fully hide a focused element. Record if the author must set `scroll-padding-top`.
- [ ] **1.4.3** — With a contrast checker, measure the title and the icons for each color, in light and dark mode, and with `enableColorOnDark`. The text is at least 4.5:1.
- [ ] **1.4.10** — At 320 CSS px width, the Toolbar content stays usable, and the page does not scroll horizontally.
- [ ] **1.4.4** — At 200% zoom, the title and the actions are fully visible.

### Done when

* AppBar has a report and is in the scorecard.
* Each manual test in this issue has steps and a result in the report.

### Context

Wave 4, item 17 (lower risk). Tracking issue: mui/material-ui#49260.

Include SpeedDialAction and SpeedDialIcon. Focus on `aria-expanded` and `aria-haspopup` on the trigger (4.1.2), keyboard navigation of the actions (2.1.1), the action names that show only in tooltips (1.1.1, 1.4.13) and hover-to-open (1.4.13).

### Scope

1. Add axe tests and fixtures in `test/regressions/a11y/fixtures/`.

- [ ] **2.1.1** — Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> to the SpeedDial button. <kbd>Enter</kbd> or <kbd>Space</kbd> opens it. The arrow keys for the `direction` move between the actions. <kbd>Escape</kbd> closes it, and focus goes back to the button.
- [ ] **4.1.2** — With a screen reader, the button announces its name, that it opens a menu, and "expanded" or "collapsed". Each action announces its `tooltipTitle` as the name.
- [ ] **1.4.13** — Open the SpeedDial with hover. Move the pointer onto the actions and their tooltips. They stay visible. <kbd>Escape</kbd> closes them without a pointer move.
- [ ] **1.1.1** — With `tooltipOpen`, the action names are visible. Without it, record that the names are visible only on hover or focus.
- [ ] **2.4.11** — With the SpeedDial in a fixed position, press <kbd>Tab</kbd> through the page. It does not fully hide a focused element.
- [ ] **2.5.8** — Each action is at least 24 × 24 CSS px.

### Done when

* SpeedDial has a report and is in the scorecard.
* Each manual test in this issue has steps and a result in the report.

I would like to group data in the colors of a `so.Plot` object by grouping their values. For scatter plots, this is mostly okay. But for line plots, it can get unruly fast if you don't do the grouping, as each individual value gets its own unique color. ## Example ```python import seaborn as sns df = sns.load_dataset("penguins") sns.objects.Plot( df, x="bill_length_mm", y="body_mass_g", color="flipper_length_mm", ).add(mark=sns.objects.Line()) ``` If I make a "group" of the flipper data, seaborn errors ```python df["flipper_group"] = pd.cut(df["flipper_length_mm"], bins=7) sns.objects.Plot( df, x="bill_length_mm", y="body_mass_g", color="flipper_group", ).add(mark=sns.objects.Line()) [...] TypeError: 'pandas._libs.interval.Interval' object is not iterable The above exception was the direct cause of the following exception: [...] PlotSpecError: Scaling operation failed for the `color` variable. See the traceback above for more information. ```
Full traceback ```python --------------------------------------------------------------------------- TypeError Traceback (most recent call last) File [...]/lib/python3.14/site-packages/seaborn/_marks/base.py:180, in Mark._resolve(self, data, name, scales) 179 try: --> 180 feature = scale(value) 181 except Exception as err: File [...]/lib/python3.14/site-packages/seaborn/_core/scales.py:129, in Scale.__call__(self, data) 128 if func is not None: --> 129 trans_data = func(trans_data) 131 if scalar_data: File [...]/lib/python3.14/site-packages/seaborn/_core/scales.py:311, in Nominal._setup..convert_units(x) 305 def convert_units(x): 306 # TODO only do this with explicit order? 307 # (But also category dtype?) 308 # TODO isin fails when units_seed mixes numbers and strings (numpy error?) 309 # but np.isin also does not seem any faster? (Maybe not broadcasting in C) 310 # keep = x.isin(units_seed) --> 311 keep = np.array([x_ in units_seed for x_ in x], bool) 312 out = np.full(len(x), np.nan) TypeError: 'pandas._libs.interval.Interval' object is not iterable The above exception was the direct cause of the following exception: PlotSpecError Traceback (most recent call last) File [...]/lib/python3.14/site-packages/seaborn/_core/plot.py:387, in Plot._repr_png_(self) 385 if Plot.config.display["format"] != "png": 386 return None --> 387return self.plot()._repr_png_() File [...]/lib/python3.14/site-packages/seaborn/_core/plot.py:932, in Plot.plot(self, pyplot) 928 """ 929 Compile the plot spec and return the Plotter object. 930 """ 931 with theme_context(self._theme_with_defaults()): --> 932 return self._plot(pyplot) File [...]/lib/python3.14/site-packages/seaborn/_core/plot.py:962, in Plot._plot(self, pyplot) 960 # Process the data for each layer and add matplotlib artists 961 for layer in layers: --> 962 plotter._plot_layer(self, layer) 964 # Add various figure decorations 965 plotter._make_legend(self) File [...]/lib/python3.14/site-packages/seaborn/_core/plot.py:1488, in Plotter._plot_layer(self, p, layer) 1485 grouping_vars = mark._grouping_props + default_grouping_vars 1486 split_generator = self._setup_split_generator(grouping_vars, df, subplots) -> 1488 mark._plot(split_generator, scales, orient) 1490 # TODO is this the right place for this? 1491 for view in self._subplots: File [...]/lib/python3.14/site-packages/seaborn/_marks/line.py:52, in Path._plot(self, split_gen, scales, orient) 48 def _plot(self, split_gen, scales, orient): 50 for keys, data, ax in split_gen(keep_na=not self._sort): ---> 52 vals = resolve_properties(self, keys, scales) 53 vals["color"] = resolve_color(self, keys, scales=scales) 54 vals["fillcolor"] = resolve_color(self, keys, prefix="fill", scales=scales) File [...]/lib/python3.14/site-packages/seaborn/_marks/base.py:237, in resolve_properties(mark, data, scales) 232 def resolve_properties( 233 mark: Mark, data: DataFrame, scales: dict[str, Scale] 234 ) -> dict[str, Any]: 236 props = { --> 237 name: mark._resolve(data, name, scales) for name in mark._mappable_props 238 } 239 return props File [...]/lib/python3.14/site-packages/seaborn/_marks/base.py:182, in Mark._resolve(self, data, name, scales) 180 feature = scale(value) 181 except Exception as err: --> 182 raise PlotSpecError._during("Scaling operation", name) from err 184 if return_array: 185 feature = np.asarray(feature) PlotSpecError: Scaling operation failed for the `color` variable. See the traceback above for more information. ```
I can kind of get around this by casting the data to strings, but the sorting is not consistent ```python df["flipper_group_str"] = df["flipper_group"].astype(str) sns.objects.Plot( df, x="bill_length_mm", y="body_mass_g", color="flipper_group_str", ).add(mark=sns.objects.Line()) ``` Note the last three entries of the grouping are not numerically sorted. Which makes sense, because seaborn is not seeing numbers. But they aren't even sorted lexicographically, going 205 -> 222 -> 214. ## Context This is in reference to https://codeberg.org/djsn/sweet-pareto/issues/15 There, I use the `so.Plot` and faceting with a custom `so.Mark` to make graphs that would otherwise be challenging to make. The faceting and coloring provided by `so.Plot` is exceptional. Thank you for this

### Environment
- **OS:** Windows / Linux / macOS
- **Python Version:** 3.10+
- **Seaborn Version:** `0.13.2` / `main` commit `c1cb287`
- **Component:** `seaborn._stats.counting.Hist`

### Description
In `seaborn.objects.Hist`, the parameter `common_norm` defaults to `True`. According to the documentation:
> `common_norm : bool or list of variables`
> *When not False, the normalization is applied across groups. Use True to normalize across all groups, or pass variable name(s) that define normalization groups.*

For all other relative statistics (`percent`, `proportion`, `probability`), `Hist` correctly computes normalization across groups when `common_norm=True`. Furthermore, both `sns.histplot(stat="density", common_norm=True)` and `so.KDE(common_norm=True)` properly weight group densities by relative sample sizes so that the total area integrates to 1.0.

However, in `so.Hist(stat="density")`, `common_norm=True` is completely ignored. Each group is normalized independently so that its individual area sums to 1.0. As a result, groups with radically different sample sizes (e.g. 10 vs 100 observations) are displayed with identical densities, misrepresenting the underlying distribution.

### Minimal Reproducible Example (MRE)
```python
import pandas as pd
from seaborn._core.groupby import GroupBy
from seaborn._core.scales import Continuous
from seaborn._stats.counting import Hist

# Two groups: 'small' has 10 samples, 'large' has 100 samples (10x larger)
df = pd.DataFrame({
    "x": [1, 2] * 5 + [1, 2] * 50,
    "group": ["small"] * 10 + ["large"] * 100
})

gb = GroupBy(["group"])
scales = {"x": Continuous()}

# common_norm=True is the default
h_true = Hist(stat="density", common_norm=True)
res_true = h_true(df, gb, "x", scales)

print(res_true[["group", "x", "count", "density"]])
```

### Actual Behavior
Both groups receive the exact same density `1.0`:
```text
   group    x  count  density
0  small  1.5    1.0      1.0
1  large  1.5    1.0      1.0
```
Toggling `common_norm=False` vs `common_norm=True` produces identical outputs.

### Expected Behavior
Under `common_norm=True`, the densities should be proportional to sample weight:
- `small` group (10 / 110 observations): `density ≈ 0.0909`
- `large` group (100 / 110 observations): `density ≈ 0.9091`

### Root Cause Analysis
In `seaborn/_stats/counting.py`:
1. In `_eval`:
   ```python
   # lines 175-176
   density = self.stat == "density"
   hist, edges = np.histogram(vals, **bin_kws, weights=weights, density=density)
   ```
   Because `_eval` is invoked on each group via `groupby.apply(data, self._eval, ...)`, `np.histogram(..., density=True)` calculates the density prematurely within the single group subset.
2. In `_normalize`:
   ```python
   # lines 185-192
   hist = data["count"]
   if self.stat == "probability" or self.stat == "proportion":
       hist = hist.astype(float) / hist.sum()
   elif self.stat == "percent":
       hist = hist.astype(float) / hist.sum() * 100
   elif self.stat == "frequency":
       hist = hist.astype(float) / data["space"]
   ```
   There is **no condition for `self.stat == "density"`** in `_normalize`!
3. In `__call__`:
   ```python
   # lines 221-229
   if not grouping_vars or self.common_norm is True:
       data = self._normalize(data)
   else:
       ...
       data = norm_groupby.apply(data, self._normalize)
   ```
   Whether `self._normalize` is called on the concatenated data or per group, it does nothing for `density`. Thus `common_norm` is entirely inert for density histograms.

### Proposed Fix
Compute raw counts in `_eval` and apply density normalization inside `_normalize`:

```diff
--- a/seaborn/_stats/counting.py
+++ b/seaborn/_stats/counting.py
@@ -172,8 +172,7 @@ class Hist(Stat):
         vals = data[orient]
         weights = data.get("weight", None)

-        density = self.stat == "density"
-        hist, edges = np.histogram(vals, **bin_kws, weights=weights, density=density)
+        hist, edges = np.histogram(vals, **bin_kws, weights=weights, density=False)

         width = np.diff(edges)
         center = edges[:-1] + width / 2
@@ -188,6 +187,8 @@ class Hist(Stat):
             hist = hist.astype(float) / hist.sum()
         elif self.stat == "percent":
             hist = hist.astype(float) / hist.sum() * 100
+        elif self.stat == "density":
+            hist = hist.astype(float) / (hist.sum() * data["space"])
         elif self.stat == "frequency":
             hist = hist.astype(float) / data["space"]
```

### Pytest Regression Test
```python
def test_hist_density_common_norm():
    df = pd.DataFrame({
        "x": [1, 2] * 5 + [1, 2] * 50,
        "group": ["small"] * 10 + ["large"] * 100
    })
    gb = GroupBy(["group"])
    scales = {"x": Continuous()}
    
    res = Hist(stat="density", common_norm=True)(df, gb, "x", scales)
    small_density = res.loc[res["group"] == "small", "density"].iloc[0]
    large_density = res.loc[res["group"] == "large", "density"].iloc[0]
    assert np.isclose(large_density / small_density, 10.0)
```

### Environment
- **OS:** Any
- **Python Version:** 3.10+
- **Seaborn Version:** `0.13.2` / `main` commit `c1cb287`
- **Component:** `seaborn.matrix._matrix_mask` (`sns.heatmap`, `sns.clustermap`)

### Description
In `seaborn/matrix.py`, `_matrix_mask(data, mask)` validates that if `mask` is a `pandas.DataFrame`, its row index and column names match `data` before plotting a heatmap or clustermap.

Due to a boolean operator precedence omission (`not A and B` instead of `not (A and B)`), if the mask has **different columns**, or **both different index and columns**, the validation condition evaluates to `False`. The mismatched mask silently bypasses validation, undergoes Pandas outer-join alignment in `mask | pd.isnull(data)`, expands with NaNs, and subsequently crashes inside NumPy with:
`IndexError: Inconsistent shape between the condition and the input (got (M, N) and (X, Y))`
instead of raising the intended:
`ValueError: Mask must have the same index and columns as data.`

### Minimal Reproducible Example (MRE)
```python
import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns

data = pd.DataFrame([[1, 2], [3, 4]], index=["a", "b"], columns=["x", "y"])

# Mask has completely different columns ("w", "z")
mask_bad = pd.DataFrame([[True, False], [False, True]], index=["a", "b"], columns=["w", "z"])

# Should raise ValueError: Mask must have the same index and columns as data.
sns.heatmap(data, mask=mask_bad)
```

### Actual Behavior
The code crashes deep inside `numpy.ma.masked_where` with an obscure `IndexError`:
```text
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
  File "seaborn/matrix.py", line 115, in __init__
    plot_data = np.ma.masked_where(np.asarray(mask), plot_data)
  File "numpy/ma/core.py", line 1991, in masked_where
    raise IndexError("Inconsistent shape between the condition and the input"
IndexError: Inconsistent shape between the condition and the input (got (2, 4) and (2, 2))
```

### Expected Behavior
`_matrix_mask` should immediately raise:
```text
ValueError: Mask must have the same index and columns as data.
```

### Root Cause Analysis
In `seaborn/matrix.py`, lines 74-77:
```python
    if isinstance(mask, pd.DataFrame):
        # For DataFrame masks, ensure that semantic labels match data
        if not mask.index.equals(data.index) \
           and mask.columns.equals(data.columns):
            err = "Mask must have the same index and columns as data."
            raise ValueError(err)
```
In Python, `not A and B` binds as `(not A) and B`.
- If `mask.columns.equals(data.columns)` is `False` (i.e. columns do not match), the condition evaluates to `True and False == False`!
- If neither index nor columns match, it evaluates to `True and False == False`!
- The error is **only** raised if `mask.index` does NOT match **AND** `mask.columns` DOES match.

Because the check is bypassed, line 92 executes:
```python
mask = mask | pd.isnull(data)
```
Since index/columns differ, Pandas reindexes to the union of row indices and column names, inflating the mask's dimensions and causing the NumPy shape mismatch crash.

### Proposed Fix
Group the conjunction in parentheses:

```diff
--- a/seaborn/matrix.py
+++ b/seaborn/matrix.py
@@ -71,8 +71,8 @@ def _matrix_mask(data, mask):

     if isinstance(mask, pd.DataFrame):
         # For DataFrame masks, ensure that semantic labels match data
-        if not mask.index.equals(data.index) \
-           and mask.columns.equals(data.columns):
+        if not (mask.index.equals(data.index)
+                and mask.columns.equals(data.columns)):
             err = "Mask must have the same index and columns as data."
             raise ValueError(err)
     elif hasattr(mask, "__array__"):
```

### Pytest Regression Test
```python
def test_matrix_mask_mismatched_columns():
    data = pd.DataFrame([[1, 2], [3, 4]], index=["a", "b"], columns=["x", "y"])
    mask = pd.DataFrame([[True, False], [False, True]], index=["a", "b"], columns=["w", "z"])
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="Mask must have the same index and columns as data"):
        sns.matrix._matrix_mask(data, mask)
```

### Environment
- **OS:** Any
- **Python Version:** 3.10+
- **Seaborn Version:** `0.13.2` / `main` commit `c1cb287`
- **Component:** `seaborn.categorical.catplot`

### Description
Calling any categorical plotting function directly with an empty DataFrame (e.g. `sns.stripplot(data=df, x="x", y="y")`, `sns.boxplot(data=df, x="x", y="y")`, etc.) safely checks `if p.plot_data.empty: return ax` and returns the empty axis.

However, the figure-level equivalent `sns.catplot(data=df, x="x", y="y")` crashes with unhandled internal exceptions across 6 of its 8 plot kinds (`strip`, `swarm`, `violin`, `boxen` crash with `IndexError: single positional indexer is out-of-bounds`; `box` and `point` crash with `ValueError`).

### Minimal Reproducible Example (MRE)
```python
import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns

df = pd.DataFrame(columns=["x", "y"])

# Raises IndexError: single positional indexer is out-of-bounds
sns.catplot(data=df, x="x", y="y", kind="strip")
```

### Actual Behavior
Unhandled exception terminates execution:
```text
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "seaborn/categorical.py", line 2888, in catplot
    p.plot_strips(jitter=jitter, ...)
  File "seaborn/categorical.py", line 496, in plot_strips
    for sub_vars, sub_data in self.iter_data(iter_vars, from_comp_data=True, allow_empty=True):
  File "seaborn/_base.py", line 910, in iter_data
    converter = self.converters[axis].iloc[0]
  File "pandas/core/indexing.py", line 1706, in _validate_integer
    raise IndexError("single positional indexer is out-of-bounds")
IndexError: single positional indexer is out-of-bounds
```

### Expected Behavior
`catplot` should return an empty `FacetGrid` object with initialized axes and labels, matching all other figure-level functions (`relplot`, `displot`) and axes-level functions.

### Root Cause Analysis
In `seaborn/categorical.py` (lines 2830-2838):
```python
    # Capture this here because scale_categorical is going to insert a (null)
    # x variable even if it is empty. It's not clear whether that needs to
    # happen or if disabling that is the cleaner solution.
    has_xy_data = p.has_xy_data

    if not native_scale or p.var_types[p.orient] == "categorical":
        p.scale_categorical(p.orient, order=order, formatter=formatter)

    p._attach(g, log_scale=log_scale)

    if not has_xy_data:
        return g
```
Notice the comment: the author intended to guard against empty data before categorical dummy insertion.
However, `has_xy_data` is defined in `VectorPlotter` (`seaborn/_base.py`, line 643):
```python
@property
def has_xy_data(self):
    """Return True at least one of x or y is defined."""
    return bool({"x", "y"} & set(self.variables))
```
`has_xy_data` only checks if the variable names `'x'` or `'y'` are mapped, **not** whether the DataFrame has any observations!
When `x="x", y="y"` is passed with an empty DataFrame, `p.has_xy_data` evaluates to `True`. Consequently, `if not has_xy_data: return g` fails to trigger, and `catplot` proceeds to iterate over empty converters, blowing up on `.iloc[0]`.

### Proposed Fix
Ensure `has_xy_data` also checks that `plot_data` is non-empty:

```diff
--- a/seaborn/categorical.py
+++ b/seaborn/categorical.py
@@ -2828,7 +2828,7 @@ def catplot(
     # Capture this here because scale_categorical is going to insert a (null)
     # x variable even if it is empty. It's not clear whether that needs to
     # happen or if disabling that is the cleaner solution.
-    has_xy_data = p.has_xy_data
+    has_xy_data = p.has_xy_data and not p.plot_data.empty

     if not native_scale or p.var_types[p.orient] == "categorical":
         p.scale_categorical(p.orient, order=order, formatter=formatter)
```

### Pytest Regression Test
```python
@pytest.mark.parametrize("kind", ["strip", "swarm", "box", "violin", "boxen", "point", "bar"])
def test_catplot_empty_dataframe(kind):
    df = pd.DataFrame(columns=["x", "y"])
    g = sns.catplot(data=df, x="x", y="y", kind=kind)
    assert isinstance(g, sns.axisgrid.FacetGrid)
```

{"repository": "mwaskom/seaborn", "task_candidate_id": 17119, "repository_id": 177, "issue_number": 4017, "github_issue_id": 5860501969, "html_url": "https://github.com/mwaskom/seaborn/issues/4017", "created_at": "2026-10-15T05:11:15+00:00", "author_association": "NONE", "title": "catplot crashes on empty DataFrame with defined x/y due to has_xy_data property misconception`", "body_text": "### Environment
- **OS:** Any
- **Python Version:** 3.10+
- **Seaborn Version:** `0.13.2` / `main` commit `c1cb287`
- **Component:** `seaborn.categorical.catplot`

### Description
Calling any categorical plotting function directly with an empty DataFrame (e.g. `sns.stripplot(data=df, x="x", y="y")`, `sns.boxplot(data=df, x="x", y="y")`, etc.) safely checks `if p.plot_data.empty: return ax` and returns the empty axis.

However, the figure-level equivalent `sns.catplot(data=df, x="x", y="y")` crashes with unhandled internal exceptions across 6 of its 8 plot kinds (`strip`, `swarm`, `violin`, `boxen` crash with `IndexError: single positional indexer is out-of-bounds`; `box` and `point` crash with `ValueError`).

### Minimal Reproducible Example (MRE)
```python
import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns

df = pd.DataFrame(columns=["x", "y"])

# Raises IndexError: single positional indexer is out-of-bounds
sns.catplot(data=df, x="x", y="y", kind="strip")
```

### Actual Behavior
Unhandled exception terminates execution:
```text
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "seaborn/categorical.py", line 2888, in catplot
    p.plot_strips(jitter=jitter, ...)
  File "seaborn/categorical.py", line 496, in plot_strips
    for sub_vars, sub_data in self.iter_data(iter_vars, from_comp_data=True, allow_empty=True):
  File "seaborn/_base.py", line 910, in iter_data
    converter = self.converters[axis].iloc[0]
  File "pandas/core/indexing.py", line 1706, in _validate_integer
    raise IndexError("single positional indexer is out-of-bounds")
IndexError: single positional indexer is out-of-bounds
```

### Expected Behavior
`catplot` should return an empty `FacetGrid` object with initialized axes and labels, matching all other figure-level functions (`relplot`, `displot`) and axes-level functions.

### Root Cause Analysis
In `seaborn/categorical.py` (lines 2830-2838):
```python
    # Capture this here because scale_categorical is going to insert a (null)
    # x variable even if it is empty. It's not clear whether that needs to
    # happen or if disabling that is the cleaner solution.
    has_xy_data = p.has_xy_data

    if not native_scale or p.var_types[p.orient] == "categorical":
        p.scale_categorical(p.orient, order=order, formatter=formatter)

    p._attach(g, log_scale=log_scale)

    if not has_xy_data:
        return g
```
Notice the comment: the author intended to guard against empty data before categorical dummy insertion.
However, `has_xy_data` is defined in `VectorPlotter` (`seaborn/_base.py`, line 643):
```python
@property
def has_xy_data(self):
    """Return True at least one of x or y is defined."""
    return bool({"x", "y"} & set(self.variables))
```
`has_xy_data` only checks if the variable names `'x'` or `'y'` are mapped, **not** whether the DataFrame has any observations!
When `x="x", y="y"` is passed with an empty DataFrame, `p.has_xy_data` evaluates to `True`. Consequently, `if not has_xy_data: return g` fails to trigger, and `catplot` proceeds to iterate over empty converters, blowing up on `.iloc[0]`.

### Proposed Fix
Ensure `has_xy_data` also checks that `plot_data` is non-empty:

```diff
--- a/seaborn/categorical.py
+++ b/seaborn/categorical.py
@@ -2828,7 +2828,7 @@ def catplot(
     # Capture this here because scale_categorical is going to insert a (null)
     # x variable even if it is empty. It's not clear whether that needs to
     # happen or if disabling that is the cleaner solution.
-    has_xy_data = p.has_xy_data
+    has_xy_data = p.has_xy_data and not p.plot_data.empty

     if not native_scale or p.var_types[p.orient] == "categorical":
         p.scale_categorical(p.orient, order=order, formatter=formatter)
```

### Pytest Regression Test
```python
@pytest.mark.parametrize("kind", ["strip", "swarm", "box", "violin", "boxen", "point", "bar"])
def test_catplot_empty_dataframe(kind):
    df = pd.DataFrame(columns=["x", "y"])
    g = sns.catplot(data=df, x="x", y="y", kind=kind)
    assert isinstance(g, sns.axisgrid.FacetGrid)
```

body_text:
### Bug Description

When using the AI Agent node with tool nodes (e.g., Jira tools), any error returned by the tool causes the entire workflow to fail immediately. The error is not passed back to the AI Agent for processing, which prevents the agent from implementing error-handling logic defined in its system prompt.

  This is a significant limitation because it defeats the purpose of agentic error handling. The AI Agent should receive tool errors as feedback so it can decide how to proceed (retry, try alternative approach, report the issue, etc.) based on its instructions.

### To Reproduce

1. Create a workflow with an AI Agent node
  2. Add Jira tools (or other tool nodes) to the agent
  3. Configure the agent's system prompt to handle errors, e.g., "If you receive a 4xx error when assigning a user, try looking up the correct assignee first"
  4. Trigger the agent to use a tool that will return an error (e.g., Jira "Assign Issue" with an invalid assignee, which returns HTTP 400 "the user is not able to be assigned")
  5. Observe that the workflow fails immediately instead of the error being passed to the agent

### Expected behavior

Tool node errors should be returned to the AI Agent as tool call results, allowing the agent to:
  - See the error message in the tool response
  - Process it according to its system prompt instructions
  - Decide on next steps (retry, use different parameters, call another tool, or respond to the user with the error)

  This is how tool errors are handled in other AI agent frameworks (LangChain, OpenAI function calling, etc.) - the error becomes part of the conversation context rather than a workflow failure.

body_text: ## Describe the problem When using the **AI Agent node version 3.1 (Latest)**, upstream execution context is lost when the Agent either: * delegates to a **sub-agent**, or * calls **another workflow that contains an Agent** As a result, expressions referencing upstream nodes (e.g. a Telegram Trigger) stop working, even though the workflow structure remains visually unchanged. This behavior did **not occur with Agent node version 2.x**, where upstream node expressions continued to work reliably. --- ## Expected behavior Expressions referencing upstream nodes (for example: ```js {{ $('Telegram Trigger').item.json.message.chat.id }} ``` ) should behave consistently regardless of whether the Agent: * answers directly, * uses a sub-agent, or * calls another workflow containing an Agent. If this behavior is expected due to execution boundaries, the UI should clearly warn about it or document it explicitly. --- ## Actual behavior Workflow structure: ``` Telegram Trigger → Agent (v3.1, may use sub-agent OR call another workflow with an Agent) → Telegram Send Message ``` Observed behavior: * If the Agent **does NOT delegate**, the expression works correctly. * If the Agent **uses a sub-agent**, the expression evaluates to `undefined`. * If the Agent **calls another workflow that contains an Agent**, the expression also evaluates to `undefined`. This causes the Telegram Send node to fail due to a missing Chat ID. No warning or error explains why the upstream node context is no longer available. --- ## Why this is problematic * The workflow is visually linear but behaves differently at runtime. * The failure is **non-deterministic**, depending on LLM decisions. * The same expression works or fails depending on Agent behavior. * There is no UI indication that Agent v3 introduces execution boundaries. * This represents a **behavior change/regression compared to Agent v2.x**. From a user perspective, this breaks the expected mental model of how expressions and node context work in n8n. --- ## Reproduction steps 1. Create a workflow: * Telegram Trigger * AI Agent node (version 3.1, Latest) * Telegram Send Message 2. Configure the Agent so it may: * use a sub-agent, or * call another workflow that contains an Agent 3. In the Telegram Send node, set Chat ID to: ```js {{ $('Telegram Trigger').item.json.message.chat.id }} ``` 4. Send a message to the bot: * Case A: Agent answers directly → message is sent successfully. * Case B: Agent delegates (sub-agent or workflow with Agent) → Chat ID is `undefined` and message fails. --- ## Environment * **n8n version:** 2.3.5 * **AI Agent node version:** 3.1 (Latest) * **Deployment:** Docker * **OS:** Linux (Docker host) * **Trigger:** Telegram Trigger --- ## Screenshots The last node has the chat_id value when no sub-agent or workflow is called by the Main Agent: The last node does not have the chat_id value when a sub-workflow was called: The last node does not have the chat_id value when a sub-agent was called: With **AI Agent node version 2.x**, the execution context appeared to be preserved when calling a workflow

body_text:
### Bug Description

When n8n is configured to use **AWS ElastiCache** with Redis TLS disabled (`redis.tls: false`), the application silently fails to complete initialization while the pod remains reported as healthy. Health checks pass, so Kubernetes never restarts the pod.

This is a **silent failure**: the pod stays Running, `/healthz` returns `{"status":"ok"}`, and readiness/liveness probes pass, yet the application never reaches a usable state.

Helm chart used: https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n-hosting

3. Start n8n and observe logs.

## Observed behavior

**With `redis.tls: false`:**

- Process starts, listens on port 5678.
- Task Broker starts on port 5679.
- `/healthz` returns `200` and `{"status":"ok"}`.
- Pod is marked Ready, passes health checks.
- Logs stop after:

```
Permissions 0660 for n8n settings file /home/node/.n8n/config are too wide. Changing permissions to 0600..
Initializing n8n process
n8n ready on ::, port 5678
n8n Task Broker ready on 127.0.0.1, port 5679

There is a deprecation related to your environment variables. Please take the recommended actions to update your configuration:
 - N8N_AVAILABLE_BINARY_DATA_MODES -> Remove this environment variable; it is no longer needed.
```

- No further startup logs (e.g. no "Building workflow dependency index...", no "Editor is now accessible via...").
- UI does not load; workflows cannot be created or executed.

**With `redis.tls: true`:**

- Startup completes normally:

```
[license SDK] Skipping renewal on init: license cert is not initialized
Version: 2.10.4
Building workflow dependency index...

Editor is now accessible via:
https://n8n...

Finished building workflow dependency index. Processed 0 draft workflows, 0 published workflows.
```

- UI loads and workflows work.


### To Reproduce

## To reproduce

1. Deploy n8n in queue mode with AWS ElastiCache (e.g. Serverless) as the Redis backend.
2. Set Redis TLS to false:
   ```yaml
   redis:
     host: "your-elasticache-endpoint.serverless.euc1.cache.amazonaws.com"
     tls: false

### Expected behavior

## Expected behavior

Either:
1. Fail fast with a clear error when Redis connection fails (due to TLS requirement), so the pod restarts, or
2. Auto-detect that ElastiCache requires TLS and enable it

## Why this is problematic

- **Silent failure**: Health checks pass while the app is unusable.
- **Misleading**: Pods appear healthy in Kubernetes.
- **Hard to debug**: No explicit error in logs.
- **Common setup**: AWS ElastiCache is a typical choice for n8n on AWS.

## Environment

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **n8n version** | 2.10.4 |
| **Execution mode** | main (queue mode) |
| **Database** | PostgreSQL (RDS Aurora) |
| **Redis** | AWS ElastiCache Serverless |
| **Hosting** | Self-hosted (Kubernetes/EKS) |

## Fix

Set Redis TLS to true for ElastiCache:

```yaml
redis:
  host: "your-elasticache-endpoint.serverless.euc1.cache.amazonaws.com"
  tls: true
```

### Debug Info

## Additional context

AWS ElastiCache (including Serverless) requires TLS by default. Connecting without TLS causes the Redis client to fail or hang, which blocks queue initialization. Because the HTTP server and health endpoint start before Redis is fully used, `/healthz` still succeeds while the rest of the app never finishes starting.


### Operating System

EKS - Linux Nodes

### n8n Version

2.10.4

### Node.js Version

dont' know

### Database

PostgreSQL

### Execution mode

queue

### Hosting

self hosted

### To Reproduce

## To reproduce

1. Deploy n8n in queue mode with AWS ElastiCache (e.g. Serverless) as the Redis backend.
2. Set Redis TLS to false:
   ```yaml
   redis:
     host: "your-elasticache-endpoint.serverless.euc1.cache.amazonaws.com"
     tls: false

### Expected behavior

## Expected behavior

Either:
1. Fail fast with a clear error when Redis connection fails (due to TLS requirement), so the pod restarts, or
2. Auto-detect that ElastiCache requires TLS and enable it

## Why this is problematic

- **Silent failure**: Health checks pass while the app is unusable.
- **Misleading**: Pods appear healthy in Kubernetes.
- **Hard to debug**: No explicit error in logs.
- **Common setup**: AWS ElastiCache is a typical choice for n8n on AWS.

## Environment

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **n8n version** | 2.10.4 |
| **Execution mode** | main (queue mode) |
| **Database** | PostgreSQL (RDS Aurora) |
| **Redis** | AWS ElastiCache Serverless |
| **Hosting** | Self-hosted (Kubernetes/EKS) |

## Fix

Set Redis TLS to true for ElastiCache:

```yaml
redis:
  host: "your-elasticache-endpoint.serverless.euc1.cache.amazonaws.com"
  tls: true
```

### Debug Info

## Additional context

AWS ElastiCache (including Serverless) requires TLS by default. Connecting without TLS causes the Redis client to fail or hang, which blocks queue initialization. Because the HTTP server and health endpoint start before Redis is fully used, `/healthz` still succeeds while the rest of the app never finishes starting.

body_text:
### Bug Description

In a self-hosted single-container Docker deployment using SQLite and main execution mode, all Schedule Trigger workflows remained active and manual executions succeeded, but the instance produced zero automatic `mode=trigger` executions.

This persisted across multiple n8n upgrades and after changing interval schedules to raw cron expressions. The container clock and both timezone settings were correct. The workflows had active versions and n8n logged them as activated, yet no scheduled execution was created, including no failed execution.

### Diagnostic recovery

Enabling both `N8N_SCHEDULER_ENABLED=true` and `N8N_USE_WORKFLOW_PUBLICATION_SERVICE=true` showed that the previously active workflows were absent from `workflow_published_version`. After publishing the same workflows into the publication service and restarting:

- durable `scheduled_job` records were created;
- each job was enabled with a future `nextRunAt`;
- two independent workflows then fired automatically at 6:30 AM and 7:00 AM the next morning.

This points to a legacy scheduler/publication registration-state problem, but I cannot claim the exact root cause.

Similar symptoms appear in #35025 and #31326, but this report is for single-container main mode with SQLite, not Swarm/queue mode with PostgreSQL.

### To Reproduce

1. Run n8n 2.35.7 from the official Docker image as a single container using the default SQLite database and main execution mode.
2. Set both `TZ` and `GENERIC_TIMEZONE` to `America/New_York`.
3. Create and publish multiple workflows containing Schedule Trigger nodes (typeVersion 1.3), using raw cron expressions such as `30 6 * * *`, `0 7 * * *`, and `0 16 * * *`.
4. Confirm the workflows appear active and manual executions succeed.
5. Restart or upgrade the n8n container.
6. Wait through scheduled times and inspect executions.

Observed result: no automatic trigger execution is created anywhere in the instance, even though the workflows still appear active. Replacing interval rules with raw cron does not resolve it.

The persistent state originated on an older n8n version and survived several upgrades, so I do not yet have a clean-from-scratch minimal reproduction.

### Expected behavior

Active and published Schedule Trigger workflows should reliably register and dispatch after startup or upgrade. If registration fails or the workflow is missing required publication state, n8n should surface an activation/registration error rather than silently displaying it as active.

### Debug Info

- Deployment type: self-hosted Docker Compose
- Topology: one n8n container
- Database: SQLite (default)
- Execution mode: main/regular
- n8n version: 2.35.7
- Schedule Trigger node: typeVersion 1.3
- Timezone: America/New_York via both TZ and GENERIC_TIMEZONE
- Workflows showed active=1 with non-null activeVersionId
- n8n startup logs reported the workflows as activated
- Manual executions succeeded
- Zero automatic mode=trigger executions were recorded after restart
- Recovery was confirmed by automatic scheduled executions after durable scheduler/publication migration

### Operating System

Windows host with Docker Desktop; official n8n Linux container

### n8n Version

2.35.7

### Node.js Version

Bundled with official n8n 2.35.7 Docker image (exact version not captured)

### Database

SQLite (default)

### Execution mode

main (default)

In a self-hosted single-container Docker deployment using SQLite and main execution mode, all Schedule Trigger workflows remained active and manual executions succeeded, but the instance produced zero automatic `mode=trigger` executions.

This persisted across multiple n8n upgrades and after changing interval schedules to raw cron expressions. The container clock and both timezone settings were correct. The workflows had active versions and n8n logged them as activated, yet no scheduled execution was created, including no failed execution.

### Diagnostic recovery

Enabling both `N8N_SCHEDULER_ENABLED=true` and `N8N_USE_WORKFLOW_PUBLICATION_SERVICE=true` showed that the previously active workflows were absent from `workflow_published_version`. After publishing the same workflows into the publication service and restarting:

- durable `scheduled_job` records were created;
- each job was enabled with a future `nextRunAt`;
- two independent workflows then fired automatically at 6:30 AM and 7:00 AM the next morning.

This points to a legacy scheduler/publication registration-state problem, but I cannot claim the exact root cause.

Similar symptoms appear in #35025 and #31326, but this report is for single-container main mode with SQLite, not Swarm/queue mode with PostgreSQL.

### To Reproduce

1. Run n8n 2.35.7 from the official Docker image as a single container using the default SQLite database and main execution mode.
2. Set both `TZ` and `GENERIC_TIMEZONE` to `America/New_York`.
3. Create and publish multiple workflows containing Schedule Trigger nodes (typeVersion 1.3), using raw cron expressions such as `30 6 * * *`, `0 7 * * *`, and `0 16 * * *`.
4. Confirm the workflows appear active and manual executions succeed.
5. Restart or upgrade the n8n container.
6. Wait through scheduled times and inspect executions.

Observed result: no automatic trigger execution is created anywhere in the instance, even though the workflows still appear active. Replacing interval rules with raw cron does not resolve it.

The persistent state originated on an older n8n version and survived several upgrades, so I do not yet have a clean-from-scratch minimal reproduction.

### Expected behavior

Active and published Schedule Trigger workflows should reliably register and dispatch after startup or upgrade. If registration fails or the workflow is missing required publication state, n8n should surface an activation/registration error rather than silently displaying it as active.

- Topology: one n8n container

- n8n startup logs reported the workflows as activated
- Manual executions succeeded
- Zero automatic mode=trigger executions were recorded after restart
- Recovery was confirmed by automatic scheduled executions after durable scheduler/publication migration

### Operating System

Windows host with Docker Desktop; official n8n Linux container

2.35.7

### Node.js Version

Bundled with official n8n 2.35.7 Docker image (exact version not captured)

body_text:
### Bug Description

When an `mcpClientTool` node is connected as an `ai_tool` child of an
`mcpTrigger` (n8n proxying a third-party MCP server to an external MCP
client), tool listing works but every tool call fails.

- `tools/list` returns all 45 tools of the upstream server, with full
  parameter schemas, to the connected client. The list is live: it changes
  immediately when the node's `include` parameter is changed.
- `tools/call` fails with `Tool node "coolify" did not return a valid Tool`.

The error surfaces in `getConnectedTools`
(`@n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain/utils/helpers.ts:198`), called from
`McpTrigger.webhook` (`McpTrigger.node.ts:258`) via
`WebhookContext.getInputConnectionData`.

Two things make this hard to diagnose:

1. **The message does not name its cause.** It is the type check itself.
2. **The execution is recorded as `success`**, with empty `runData` and no
   `subRun` entry for the node. Searching for a failed execution finds
   nothing. Only the client sees an error.

### To Reproduce

1. Add an MCP Server Trigger (v2).
2. Add an MCP Client Tool (v1.4, `serverTransport: httpStreamable`) pointing
   at any reachable third-party MCP server, and connect it to the trigger as
   `ai_tool`.
3. Connect an external MCP client to the trigger. Tool listing shows all
   upstream tools.
4. Call any of them.

### Expected behavior

Either the call succeeds and is proxied to the upstream server, or the
listing already fails and the error names the reason. The current behavior
advertises tools that cannot be called.

At minimum: the execution should be recorded as `error`, not `success`.

Further Context;

## Ruled out by measurement

- Upstream server: reachable, MCP enabled, no IP allowlist, token used
  (confirmed via its `last_used` timestamp).
- Transport: switching to `sse` produces a *different* and correctly reported
  error ("Could not connect to your MCP server", execution status `error`,
  `subRun` present). With `httpStreamable` there is no connection error at all.
- Stale registration: the tool list changes immediately when `include` is set
  to `selected`, so listing is live.
- Individual tool schema: a single selected tool with real parameters fails
  the same way as a single tool with empty `properties`.
- Tool count: one tool fails exactly like 45.

Other `ai_tool` children of the same trigger (GitHub, HTTP Request, Call n8n
Workflow) work correctly. `mcpClientTool` is the only node type affected.

## Workaround

Wrap the standalone `mcpClient` action node (a different node) in a
sub-workflow and attach that via `toolWorkflow`. The action node handles
`initialize`, session and `tools/call` correctly against the same server with
the same credential.

### Bug Description

On n8n Cloud 2.35.4 (docker cloud, enterprise sandbox), inbound chat triggers do not become usable.

1. Slack Trigger: the Slack Events API Request URL path never completes. The workflow does not wake on channel messages. Setup hangs before a live inbound connection.

2. Telegram Trigger: Telegram shows the DM as delivered (two checkmarks). n8n does not start an execution for that message. No Telegram inbound webhook URL is available on the Cloud instance to finish wiring, so related workflows stay unpublished.

Because those trigger nodes never emit an item, downstream nodes never run. This is not a feature request. It is inbound trigger connectivity on Cloud.

### To Reproduce

1. Open n8n Cloud 2.35.4 (docker cloud).
2. Create a workflow with a Slack Trigger (message in a channel / Events API).
3. Copy the production webhook URL into the Slack app Event Subscriptions Request URL and try to verify.
4. Observe: verification / inbound wake does not complete; sending a Slack message does not create an n8n execution.
5. Create a second workflow with a Telegram Trigger for bot DMs.
6. Send a DM to the bot (Telegram shows delivered, two checkmarks).
7. Observe: n8n Executions stays at zero for that workflow. No Telegram inbound URL is exposed to finish the trigger. Workflow cannot be published as live intake.be the problem/err

### Expected behavior

Slack: Request URL verifies and a channel message creates one execution with the message payload.

Telegram: A delivered DM creates one execution with chat_id and text. Cloud should expose the Telegram Trigger webhook URL needed to complete setup.

Actual: neither trigger produces a production execution, so the hosted instance cannot receive Slack or Telegram events.

## Describe the problem/error/question

I have an active n8n Cloud workspace and have enabled **Instance-level MCP** from:

Settings → Instance-level MCP

Workspace hostname:

`sepidraai.app.n8n.cloud`

The n8n UI is working normally and is accessible at:

`https://sepidraai.app.n8n.cloud/home/workflows`

Instance-level MCP shows **Enabled** in the n8n UI.

n8n provides the following MCP Server URL:

`https://sepidraai.app.n8n.cloud/mcp-server/http`

I am attempting to connect **Claude Code 2.1.241 on Windows** to the n8n Instance-level MCP server.

I tested both authentication methods presented by n8n:

1. OAuth
2. API key / Bearer token

### OAuth behaviour

Using the OAuth setup, connection fails during registration with n8n's sign-in service.

### API key / Bearer token behaviour

I generated a new access token from the n8n Instance-level MCP configuration and configured Claude Code with:

- Transport: HTTP
- MCP endpoint: `https://sepidraai.app.n8n.cloud/mcp-server/http`
- Authorization: Bearer token generated by n8n

Claude Code successfully registers the MCP server locally, but cannot connect to it.

To isolate the issue, I also performed a direct protocol-level connectivity test against the endpoint using a minimal MCP `initialize` handshake.

Request:

`POST https://sepidraai.app.n8n.cloud/mcp-server/http`

Headers:

- `Authorization: Bearer [REDACTED]`
- `Content-Type: application/json`
- `Accept: application/json, text/event-stream`

The request used a minimal MCP `initialize` handshake with protocol version `2024-11-05`.

The response is HTTP 404 with an n8n-branded HTML page saying:

`404 - No workspace here`

The response appears to come from the n8n Cloud/Cloudflare routing layer before the request reaches MCP authentication or protocol handling.

This is confusing because the exact same workspace hostname is active and accessible through the browser at:

`https://sepidraai.app.n8n.cloud/home/workflows`

The workspace is currently active and the n8n UI reports that the trial still has time remaining.

Could you please check whether **Instance-level MCP routing/provisioning** is functioning correctly for this n8n Cloud workspace?

## What is the error message (if any)?

### API key / Bearer token connection

Direct MCP endpoint request returns:

`HTTP 404`

Response page:

`404 - No workspace here`

The response is `text/html`, rather than an MCP/authentication response.

### OAuth connection

Claude/n8n reports:

`Couldn't register with n8n's sign-in service. You can try again, or add an OAuth Client ID in the connector settings.`

OAuth support/reference IDs were generated during testing and can be provided privately if required.

## Please share your workflow/screenshots/recording

This issue concerns **Instance-level MCP**, rather than an individual workflow using an MCP Server Trigger node.

Therefore there is no workflow JSON relevant to reproducing the routing problem.

I can provide screenshots showing:

- Active n8n Cloud workspace
- Instance-level MCP enabled
- MCP Server URL generated by n8n
- OAuth connection failure
- Claude Code MCP connection failure
- HTTP 404 response from the MCP endpoint

No API keys, Bearer tokens, credentials, or other secrets will be shared.

## Share the output returned by the last node

Not applicable.

The failure occurs while connecting to the **Instance-level MCP endpoint**, before any workflow or node is executed.

Direct endpoint test result:

- HTTP Status: `404`
- Content-Type: `text/html`
- Server: `cloudflare`
- Response: n8n-branded `404 - No workspace here` page

body_text:
### Bug Description

When using the **Send and Wait** operation on messaging nodes (Gmail, Telegram, WhatsApp, Email Send, Teams, Outlook, Discord, Google Chat), the **Custom Form** response type renders only the old single "Field Name" input per element. The regular n8n Form / Form Trigger nodes show the modern editor with separate **Label**, **Element Type**, **Custom Field Name**, **Placeholder** and **Default Value** fields.

This means:

- On most channels you cannot give an output key its own name — output items are always keyed by the visible label.
- The same operation looks and behaves differently depending on which node it lives in.

The shared `formFieldsProperties` definitions carry `@version` display conditions written against the Form node's version history (name/label split at 2.4, Custom Field Name at 2.5). Because Send and Wait embeds them into nodes with their own lower versions, those conditions resolve against e.g. Gmail 2.2 or Telegram 1.2 and fall back to the pre-2.4 legacy field.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a workflow with a Gmail node (Telegram or WhatsApp show it too).
2. Pick the **Send and Wait** operation and set **Response Type → Custom Form**.
3. Look at the **Form Elements** editor.
4. Compare it with a Form Trigger node's Form Elements editor.

### Expected Behavior

The custom-form field editor should look the same everywhere: Label, Element Type, Custom Field Name, Placeholder and Default Value, like the current Form node. Setting a Custom Field Name should also control the output item's keys.

### Compatibility Consideration

Whichever way this gets fixed, existing workflows must keep their current output keys. On the affected channels the editor never exposed a separate field name, but stored workflow JSON can still contain one (imports, API-created workflows, AI-generated workflows). A fix that starts preferring the stored field name unconditionally would silently rename output keys for those workflows. Any solution should either gate the new behavior behind an explicit user choice or a node version bump.

### Operating System

Linux (reproduces regardless of OS)

### n8n Version

2.36.0 (master)

### Node.js Version

24.x

### Database

SQLite

### Execution Mode

main

### Hosting

self hosted

### Proposed Fix

A draft implementation is open for reference: #36959 (adds an explicit Field Naming option to the Custom Form response type).

When using the **Send and Wait** operation on messaging nodes (Gmail, Telegram, WhatsApp, Email Send, Teams, Outlook, Discord, Google Chat), the **Custom Form** response type renders only the old single "Field Name" input per element. The regular n8n Form / Form Trigger nodes show the modern editor with separate **Label**, **Element Type**, **Custom Field Name**, **Placeholder** and **Default Value** fields.

This means:

- On most channels you cannot give an output key its own name — output items are always keyed by the visible label.
- The same operation looks and behaves differently depending on which node it lives in.

The shared `formFieldsProperties` definitions carry `@version` display conditions written against the Form node's version history (name/label split at 2.4, Custom Field Name at 2.5). Because Send and Wait embeds them into nodes with their own lower versions, those conditions resolve against e.g. Gmail 2.2 or Telegram 1.2 and fall back to the pre-2.4 legacy field.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a workflow with a Gmail node (Telegram or WhatsApp show it too).
2. Pick the **Send and Wait** operation and set **Response Type → Custom Form**.
3. Look at the **Form Elements** editor.
4. Compare it with a Form Trigger node's Form Elements editor.

### Expected Behavior

The custom-form field editor should look the same everywhere: Label, Element Type, Custom Field Name, Placeholder and Default Value, like the current Form node. Setting a Custom Field Name should also control the output item's keys.

### Compatibility Consideration

Whichever way this gets fixed, existing workflows must keep their current output keys. On the affected channels the editor never exposed a separate field name, but stored workflow JSON can still contain one (imports, API-created workflows, AI-generated workflows). A fix that starts preferring the stored field name unconditionally would silently rename output keys for those workflows. Any solution should either gate the new behavior behind an explicit user choice or a node version bump.

### Operating System

Linux (reproduces regardless of OS)

### n8n Version

2.36.0 (master)

### Node.js Version

24.x

### Database

SQLite

### Execution Mode

main

### Hosting

self hosted

### Proposed Fix

A draft implementation is open for reference: #36959 (adds an explicit Field Naming option to the Custom Form response type).

### Bug Description

Same (1:1) as in closed https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/issues/21262 

Workflows execute successfully and complete normally in the UI
However, the database record remains with finished = false and status = 'running'
These "zombie" executions accumulate in the database indefinitely
The issue occurs regardless of workflow complexity (even simple 3-node workflows)
100% reproducible across different workflow typ

### To Reproduce

1)Create any simple workflow
2) Set setting Save successful production executions to "Do not Save"
3) Execute workflow
4) check database table execution_entity -- Finish is set to False (should be True), stoppedAt is empty. 


### Expected behavior

Even when "Save execution data" options are disabled, N8N should still update the execution's finished flag and status to properly close the execution record. The "Don't Save" option should only skip saving execution logs/outputs (to save disk space), but should NOT skip the critical execution closure update.

Workspace: immvrsive (immvrsive.app.n8n.cloud), Starter plan, now on n8n@2.36.7 (upgraded from 2.35.4 today).

Symptom: manual executions never return to the editor. Clicking "Execute step" or "Execute workflow" spins indefinitely; the node output pane never populates.

Diagnosis from the browser: POST /rest/workflows/<id>/run returns 200 — the backend accepts the run. No result is ever pushed back. The frontend instead begins polling GET /healthz continuously, which is the pushConnection store's lost-connection behaviour. No /rest/push connection is established.

Ruled out: browser profile and extensions (reproduced in a second clean browser window), stale session (logged out and back in), stale frontend (fresh tabs), instance state (version change + restart today).

Not affected: production executions run fine — 20 successful this month.

Please check the push/WebSocket layer for this workspace.
