body_text:
### Problem

With `foldexpr=v:lua.vim.treesitter.foldexpr()`, a fold that starts above the edited lines and becomes foldable because of the edit never gets created. I hit it in Markdown. A note has only `# Title`, I type a blank line and some text under it, and the heading still has no fold. `foldlevel(1)` stays `0` and `zc` on it gives `E490: No fold found`. The wrong level carries down too: a `## Section` typed later gets level 1 instead of 2.

`zx` does not fix it. `:e` or `:setlocal foldminlines=1` does, since both trigger a full recompute.

The cause seems to be in `runtime/lua/vim/treesitter/_fold.lua`. After an edit, `on_bytes` ([L376-L377](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/v0.12.6/runtime/lua/vim/treesitter/_fold.lua#L376-L377)) and `on_changedtree` ([L306-L307](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/v0.12.6/runtime/lua/vim/treesitter/_fold.lua#L306-L307)) recompute from `srow - foldminlines`. `compute_folds_levels()` takes the base level from the cache ([L145](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/v0.12.6/runtime/lua/vim/treesitter/_fold.lua#L145)) and writes `>N` only from `srow + 1` ([L149](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/v0.12.6/runtime/lua/vim/treesitter/_fold.lua#L149)). Line 1 is outside that range, so it keeps `0`. Setting `srow = 0` in both places makes the fold appear. Master (9b7ec59) has the same logic.

Probably not the same as #38356, #28692 or #32759. Those are about the initial compute or folds getting closed, while here the folds are right on open and go wrong after an edit.

### Steps to reproduce

```sh
printf '# Title\n' > t.md
nvim --clean --cmd 'set foldmethod=expr foldexpr=v:lua.vim.treesitter.foldexpr() foldlevel=99' t.md
```

Type one key at a time, do not paste:

1. `o<CR>foo<CR>bar<Esc>`
2. `:echo foldlevel(1)` prints `0`
3. `ggzc` gives `E490: No fold found`
4. `:w`, `:e`, then `:echo foldlevel(1)` prints `1` and `ggzc` closes lines 1-4

### Expected behavior

After step 1, line 1 starts a fold over lines 1-4, same as after `:e` in step 4.

### Nvim version (nvim -v)

NVIM v0.12.6, Build type: Release, LuaJIT 2.1.1791988261
Also reproduces on nightly NVIM v0.13.0-dev-1868+gbe5167e21c.

### Vim (not Nvim) behaves the same?

N/A, this is `vim.treesitter.foldexpr()`

### Operating system/version

macOS 15.5 (24F74), arm64

### Terminal name/version

Ghostty 1.3.1. The steps above also reproduce in tmux 3.8.

### $TERM environment variable

xterm-ghostty (tmux-256color inside tmux)

### Installation

Homebrew

Homebrew

body_text:
Hello and thanks for this great editor!

### Problem

On Windows, opening a file through a full path with `..` in it can create a second buffer for a file that's already open. Then I have two buffers with different edits for the same file, and saving one overwrites the other.

I hit this with the quickfix list. A tool prints error locations like `C:/proj/build/../src/foo.txt`, and jumping to an error opens a new buffer instead of using the one I already have open.

It only happens after a `:w`. Two things seem to go wrong together:

1. On Windows the `..` isn't removed from full paths, so the buffer names don't match.
2. Then it falls back to comparing file ids. But `:w` gives the file a new id and the old buffer keeps its old one, so that check fails too.

<details>
<summary>Code I think is involved</summary>

`fix_fname` sees the `..` but calls `FullName_save` with `force = false`, even though its doc says it resolves things like `dir/../subdir`:

https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/9b7ec59580fddf671f7bf922f66ef114a59a51ee/src/nvim/path.c#L1795-L1820

With `force = false`, `path_to_absolute` skips paths that are already absolute, so the `..` stays:

https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/9b7ec59580fddf671f7bf922f66ef114a59a51ee/src/nvim/path.c#L2309-L2314

The file id fallback only refreshes the buffer's id when the ids already match, so an outdated id never gets fixed here:

https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/9b7ec59580fddf671f7bf922f66ef114a59a51ee/src/nvim/buffer.c#L3287-L3301

</details>

### Steps to reproduce

    mkdir test\src test\build
    echo hello > test\src\foo.txt
    cd test
    nvim --clean src\foo.txt
    :w
    :exe 'edit' getcwd() .. '/build/../src/foo.txt'
    :ls

### Expected behavior

One buffer. Instead `:ls` shows two:

    1 #h   "src\foo.txt"                    line 1
    2 %a   "~\test/build/../src/foo.txt"    line 1

Without the `:w` it works fine. `:set backupcopy=yes` also avoids it.

### Nvim version (nvim -v)

NVIM v0.12.0. The code above is the same on master.

### Vim (not Nvim) behaves the same?

Didn't test

### Operating system/version

Windows 10 Pro 19045

### Terminal name/version

Neovide, also happens with `--headless`

### $TERM environment variable

not set

### Installation

winget

Thank you for your support!

body_text:
### Problem

On exit, `vim.lsp`'s exit handler stops only the clients that `vim.lsp.get_clients()` returns. That call leaves out clients still waiting for the server's `initialize` answer, unless the caller passes the internal `_uninitialized = true` filter:

- the filter: [`runtime/lua/vim/lsp.lua#L1161`](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/0851e7dabed9fc9c019e22088029f36e9f3ec3e3/runtime/lua/vim/lsp.lua#L1161);
- the exit handler calls `lsp.get_clients()` with no filter: [`runtime/lua/vim/lsp.lua#L1172-L1180`](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/0851e7dabed9fc9c019e22088029f36e9f3ec3e3/runtime/lua/vim/lsp.lua#L1172-L1180).

So a server that is still starting when Nvim quits is never stopped. Nvim exits and closes its pipes, and from then on it depends on the server what happens. A server that doesn't exit when its stdin closes, or one that dies and leaves its own children behind, keeps running after Nvim is gone.

I hit this with tflint's language server (`tflint --langserver`). Quitting 100–120 ms after opening a `.tf` file left its `tflint --act-as-bundled-plugin` child running 6 times out of 6, still alive after 126 s; quitting earlier (before the client existed) or later (after `initialize` was answered) left nothing. In my config's CI, where a test opens a file and quits within half a second, it showed up as a leaked process.

I'm also seeing a process left behind after quitting with yamlls attached. I'm still investigating it and can't yet confirm it has the same cause; I'll add a comment here once I know.

Is leaving these clients out at exit intended? I couldn't tell from the code, so I'd like to check before assuming either way. Two things made me wonder:

- Other internal callers pass `_uninitialized = true`, at [L532](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/0851e7dabed9fc9c019e22088029f36e9f3ec3e3/runtime/lua/vim/lsp.lua#L532), [L953](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/0851e7dabed9fc9c019e22088029f36e9f3ec3e3/runtime/lua/vim/lsp.lua#L953), [L974](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/0851e7dabed9fc9c019e22088029f36e9f3ec3e3/runtime/lua/vim/lsp.lua#L974) and [L1059](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/0851e7dabed9fc9c019e22088029f36e9f3ec3e3/runtime/lua/vim/lsp.lua#L1059).
- `Client:stop()` already handles a client that is still starting: it terminates the server right away ([`runtime/lua/vim/lsp/client.lua#L928`](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/0851e7dabed9fc9c019e22088029f36e9f3ec3e3/runtime/lua/vim/lsp/client.lua#L928), `if force == true or not self.initialized or …`).

### Steps to reproduce

A "server" that never answers `initialize` is enough, so `sleep` stands in for one:

```sh
nvim --clean --headless \
  -c "lua vim.lsp.start({ name = 'never-initializes', cmd = { 'sh', '-c', 'echo \$\$ > /tmp/lsp.pid; exec sleep 60' } })" \
  -c 'sleep 200m' -c 'qa!'
sleep 1; ps -o pid,comm -p "$(cat /tmp/lsp.pid)"
```

The `sleep` process is still running after Nvim has exited (3 runs out of 3, on both versions below).

The same run with those clients included, applied here from a user autocmd, leaves nothing behind (3 out of 3, on both versions):

```sh
nvim --clean --headless \
  -c "lua vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd('VimLeavePre', { callback = function() for _, c in ipairs(vim.lsp.get_clients({ _uninitialized = true })) do c:stop(c.exit_timeout) end end })" \
  -c "lua vim.lsp.start({ name = 'never-initializes', cmd = { 'sh', '-c', 'echo \$\$ > /tmp/lsp.pid; exec sleep 60' } })" \
  -c 'sleep 200m' -c 'qa!'
sleep 1; ps -o pid,comm -p "$(cat /tmp/lsp.pid)"
```

For comparison, a client whose server did answer `initialize` (and, like the `sleep` above, ignores stdin closing) is stopped by the exit handler as expected when it has a numeric `exit_timeout`.

### Expected behavior

I expected quitting Nvim to stop a client that is still waiting for `initialize`, the same way it stops one that has finished starting. If that's not the intended behaviour, the change I tried above amounts to one line in the exit handler:

```lua
local active_clients = lsp.get_clients({ _uninitialized = true })
```

If the proposed fix looks okay, I'm happy to open a PR for it.

If it is intended, I'd be glad to know the reason, so I can handle it on my side instead.

### Nvim version (nvim -v)

Tested on both, with the same result:

- NVIM v0.13.0-dev-1868+gbe5167e21c
- NVIM v0.12.5

### Vim (not Nvim) behaves the same?

N/A (vim.lsp)

### Operating system/version

Linux 7.2.9 (CachyOS)

Related: #14428 (orphaned servers after exit, 2021, a different cause), #36783 (`Client:stop()` defaults to `exit_timeout`).

  -c "lua vim.lsp.start({ name = 'never-initializes', cmd = { 'sh', '-c', 'echo \$\$ > /tmp/lsp.pid; exec sleep 60' } })" \
  -c 'sleep 200m' -c 'qa!'
sleep 1; ps -o pid,comm -p "$(cat /tmp/lsp.pid)"
```

The `sleep` process is still running after Nvim has exited (3 runs out of 3, on both versions below).

The same run with those clients included, applied here from a user autocmd, leaves nothing behind (3 out of 3, on both versions):

```sh
nvim --clean --headless \
  -c "lua vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd('VimLeavePre', { callback = function() for _, c in ipairs(vim.lsp.get_clients({ _uninitialized = true })) do c:stop(c.exit_timeout) end end })" \
  -c "lua vim.lsp.start({ name = 'never-initializes', cmd = { 'sh', '-c', 'echo \$\$ > /tmp/lsp.pid; exec sleep 60' } })" \
  -c 'sleep 200m' -c 'qa!'
sleep 1; ps -o pid,comm -p "$(cat /tmp/lsp.pid)"
```

For comparison, a client whose server did answer `initialize` (and, like the `sleep` above, ignores stdin closing) is stopped by the exit handler as expected when it has a numeric `exit_timeout`.

### Expected behavior

I expected quitting Nvim to stop a client that is still waiting for `initialize`, the same way it stops one that has finished starting. If that's not the intended behaviour, the change I tried above amounts to one line in the exit handler:

```lua
local active_clients = lsp.get_clients({ _uninitialized = true })
```

If the proposed fix looks okay, I'm happy to open a PR for it.

If it is intended, I'd be glad to know the reason, so I can handle it on my side instead.

### Nvim version (nvim -v)

Tested on both, with the same result:

- NVIM v0.13.0-dev-1868+gbe5167e21c
- NVIM v0.12.5

### Vim (not Nvim) behaves the same?

N/A (vim.lsp)

### Operating system/version

Linux 7.2.9 (CachyOS)

Related: #14428 (orphaned servers after exit, 2021, a different cause), #36783 (`Client:stop()` defaults to `exit_timeout`).

### Problem

Currently, the way to quit a hover window displayed by for example LSP `K` is either to
- press `K` again to focus the hover window then press `q`, or
- move the cursor.

Pressing `<esc>` when focus is on the hover window has no effect, and pressing `<c-c>` shows `Type  :qa  and press <Enter> to exit Nvim`.

Related: https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/27288

### Expected behavior

I suggest the following when `<c-c>` or `<esc>` is pressed:
- If the hover window's buffer is modifiable, show `Press  q  to exit this hover window, or  :fclose!  to close all floating windows` on the command-line.
- Otherwise, just close it.

The modifiable case is mostly a corner case ("some plugins"), suggested by https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/27288#issuecomment-2336691578 . If we don't care about that case, a simpler solution is to close it either way.

`nvim_buf_set_lines()` on an unloaded buffer whose `BufReadCmd` autocmd deletes that buffer reads the freed `buf_T` (heap-use-after-free in `normalize_index`). A testing tool found this; it does not come from a real plugin or config.

```lua
local a=vim.api
local b=vim.fn.bufadd('cancelled.txt')
a.nvim_create_autocmd('BufReadCmd',{buffer=b,once=true,callback=function()
  a.nvim_buf_delete(b,{force=true})
end})
print(pcall(a.nvim_buf_set_lines,b,0,-1,true,{'replacement'}))
```

Save the script as `reduced.lua` and run, with an ASan build:

```
nvim --headless -u NONE -i NONE -n -l reduced.lua
```

Output:

```
Error in BufReadCmd Autocommands for "<buffer=2>":
E813: Cannot close autocmd window
E813: Cannot close autocmd window
==645==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: heap-use-after-free on address 0x527000003908
READ of size 4 at 0x527000003908 thread T0
    #0 in normalize_index src/nvim/api/private/helpers.c:452
    #1 in nvim_buf_set_lines src/nvim/api/buffer.c:339
    #2 in nlua_api_nvim_buf_set_lines build/src/nvim/auto/lua_api_c_bindings.generated.h:615
freed by thread T0 here:
    #2 in apply_autocmds_group src/nvim/autocmd.c:1823
    #4 in readfile src/nvim/fileio.c:314
    #5 in open_buffer src/nvim/buffer.c:334
    #6 in buf_ensure_loaded src/nvim/buffer.c:234
    #7 in api_buf_ensure_loaded src/nvim/api/buffer.c:60
```

I expected `nvim_buf_set_lines()` to fail with an error, as the release build does, rather than touch a buffer that no longer exists.

It reproduces at 0851e7dabed9 (latest upstream when checked). The ASan build aborts with the report above. The normal (release) build exits with rc 0, prints the E813 messages and `false Failed to insert line`, so nothing is visible without a sanitizer.

Looks like `buf_ensure_loaded` (buffer.c) returns success after `open_buffer` even though the autocmd wiped the buffer, and `api_buf_ensure_loaded` (api/buffer.c) then returns the dangling pointer; a `buf_valid()`/loaded re-check there might be enough. Open PR #37373 touches nearby code in api/buffer.c and may be related; I did not test it here.

I can send a patch if that helps.

Found with an LLM-based testing tool; I used Claude to reduce it and look for the cause.

body_text:
`nvim_parse_expression()` calls `abort()` instead of returning an error when the `l` (`:let` lvalue) flag is set and the input has an unterminated `{`.

```lua
vim.api.nvim_parse_expression('{', 'l', false)
```

Command, with the line above saved as `input.lua`:

```
nvim --headless -u NONE -i NONE -n -l input.lua
```

On an ASan build the process dies with SIGABRT (exit 1); a release build exits 134 with no message:

```
==1172==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: ABRT on unknown address ...
    #2 in abort
    #3 in viml_pexpr_parse src/nvim/viml/parser/expressions.c:2133
    #4 in nvim_parse_expression src/nvim/api/vimscript.c:470
    #5 in nlua_api_nvim_parse_expression build/src/nvim/auto/lua_api_c_bindings.generated.h:8290
SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: ABRT (/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6+0x969bc) in pthread_kill
```

I expected a dict with an `error` entry, not a process abort from a public API.

Reproduces on master at 0851e7dabed9 (ASan build: `ABRT` in `viml_pexpr_parse`; release build: exit 134, signal 6). The input came from generated tests, not from a real program.

Looks like `viml_pexpr_parse` in `expressions.c`: in lvalue mode `{` creates a `kExprNodeCurlyBracesIdentifier` that is still on the AST stack at end of input, and the switch after the main loop hits `abort()` instead of setting an E15 "Missing closing figure brace" error.

I can send a patch if that helps.

Found with an LLM-based testing tool; I used Claude to reduce it and look for the cause.

### Expected behavior

It would be nicer if for example `@lsp.type.formatSpecifier` was linked to `@string.special` by default.

It would resemble how in C printf syntax %d are identified as `cFormat` which links to `Special`.

body_text:
### Problem

When a count is typed before a register prefix, the commands that Normal mode translates into operator commands (x, X, D, C, s, S, `<Del>`) apply the count twice, i.e. the count is squared. For example, `2"_x` deletes 4 characters instead of 2, and `2"_D` deletes 4 lines instead of 2.

It happens with any register (`2"ax` too), not only the black hole register.
Not affected:
- count after the register: `"_2x` deletes 2 characters,
- the commands these translate to: `2"_dl` deletes 2 characters,
- Visual mode: `vl2"_x`.

Possibly a regression from 2514256d95 "refactor(input): exec stuffed keys eagerly". nv_optrans() now runs the stuffed translation (e.g. "2dl") at once via exec_stuffed(), before `cap->opcount = 0` runs, so it looks like the count that nv_regname() saved before '"' is multiplied in again. I have not bisected this.

### Steps to reproduce

```
nvim --clean
:call setline(1, 'abcdefgh')
2"_x
```
Line becomes "efgh".

### Expected behavior

`2"_x` deletes 2 characters, the same as `"_2x` and `2"_dl`, so the line becomes "cdefgh".

### Nvim version (nvim -v)

NVIM v0.13.0-dev+1915-c5641b2bfb

### Vim (not Nvim) behaves the same?

No, vim 9.2.1202 gives "cdefgh"

### Operating system/version

Fedora Linux 44, kernel 7.2.11-200.fc44.x86_64

### Terminal name/version

Konsole, but not terminal specific

### $TERM environment variable

xterm-256color

### Installation

Copr repo for neovim-nightly owned by agriffis

### Problem

Since 0977f70f4dd3 (#32549), `add_injection()` clips injection ranges to the parent's regions, but it checks for empty ranges before clipping. A range clipped away entirely becomes an empty region, which means "whole buffer", and the child then re-injects itself until it overflows the stack.

I hit this as a 100% CPU hang with multi-GB memory growth on a markdown file containing `<script>…</script>`, using the bundled markdown_inline query and nvim-treesitter's html/javascript queries.

Clipping first fixes it:

```diff
 local function add_injection(t, pattern, lang, combined, ranges, parent_ranges, result)
+  ranges = clip_regions(ranges, parent_ranges)
   if #ranges == 0 then
@@
-    table.insert(result[lang], clip_regions(ranges, parent_ranges))
+    table.insert(result[lang], ranges)
@@
-  for _, range in ipairs(clip_regions(ranges, parent_ranges)) do
+  for _, range in ipairs(ranges) do
```


### Steps to reproduce

`minimal.lua`:

```lua
vim.treesitter.query.set('markdown_inline', 'injections', [[
((code_span) @injection.content
  (#offset! @injection.content 0 1 0 -1)
  (#set! injection.language "lua")
  (#set! injection.combined))
]])
vim.treesitter.query.set('lua', 'injections', [[
((string content: (_) @injection.content)
  (#set! injection.language "lua"))
]])
```

`repro.md`:

```markdown
`[[` `]]`
```

`nvim --clean -u minimal.lua repro.md`

```
vim.schedule callback: .../runtime/lua/vim/treesitter/languagetree.lua:215: stack overflow
```

The two queries recreate the real-world case (markdown_inline's combined html injection, plus html injecting javascript into <script>) using only bundled parsers:

1. markdown_inline injects all code spans as a single combined Lua tree. For ``` `[[` `]]` ``` that tree only includes `[[` and `]]`.
2. Lua injects Lua into string contents. The long string's content lies between the two code spans, outside the parent's regions, so clipping leaves nothing.
3. The empty region is treated as "whole buffer". The child parses the entire line, finds the string again, and recurses until the stack overflows.

With `[[x]]` the content falls inside the code span and the nesting stops after one level.


### Expected behavior

No child tree for the clipped-away injection.

### Nvim version (nvim -v)

v0.13.0-dev-4c50814

### Vim (not Nvim) behaves the same?

N/A (tree-sitter)

### Operating system/version

macOS 27.0.1

### Terminal name/version

Rex 0.1.0 (1203)

### Problem

`vim.lsp.inline_completion` waits a fixed 200 ms before each request. With copilot-language-server's round trip on top, around 250-400 ms, a suggestion takes about half a second to appear after typing stops. copilot.lua defaults to 15 ms and lets you change it. In core the only way is to override the private `Completor:automatic_request`.

A way to set the delay, such as an option on `vim.lsp.inline_completion.enable()`.

### Problem

copilot-language-server prefetches the suggestion that follows the one on screen, but only once the client reports it as shown with `textDocument/didShowCompletion`. Core rightly doesn't send that, since it isn't in the spec, but there's also no public way to know when `vim.lsp.inline_completion` shows an item, so sending it means wrapping the private `Completor:select`. Without it, the suggestion after an accept is a fresh round trip, 222-286 ms here against 3-5 ms from the prefetch (copilot-language-server 1.554.0).

### Expected behavior

A public hook when an item is shown, like `get()`'s `on_accept`, either a callback or an autocmd, so a config or plugin can send the server's notification itself.

### Problem

I was trying to copy/yank multiple paragraphs from one buffer to another,
when I encountered this behavior, which is *"the cursors stayed at the original buffer"*

### Steps to reproduce

- Open any file that has at least two paragraphs [buffer A].
- Open a new buffer (split or whatever) [buffer B].
- Place a cursor at the beginning each paragraph from buffer A.
- Yank each paragraph.
- Now go to buffer B to paste the paragraphs.
- Only the primary cursor is moved, and it pastes what it yanked.

This also happens even when *follow* mode is activated via `q=`.

### Expected behavior

The expected behavior is to move all cursors into the new buffer and paste 
those paragraphs.

### Nvim version (nvim -v)

NVIM v0.13.0-dev-1929+g17f43325b1

### Vim (not Nvim) behaves the same?

no

### Operating system/version

Arch Linux x86_64

### Terminal name/version

foot 1.28.0

### $TERM environment variable

foot

AUR

### Problem

Reproducing mappings in Insert mode with present multicursor changes the value of `[count]`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create the following `init.lua`:

    ```lua
    local rhs = function() return (vim.v.count > 0 and vim.v.count or '') .. 'Hello' end
    vim.keymap.set('i', 'xx', rhs, { expr = true })
    -- For easier repro
    vim.api.nvim_buf_set_lines(0, 0, -1, false, { '', '' })
    ```

2. `nvim --clean -u init.lua`
3. `Qj` to initialize multicursor, `i` to start Insert mode.
4. `xx` - inserts `1Hello` at both cursors. Typing this without active multicursor correctly inserts just `Hello`.

### Expected behavior

Presence of multicursor has not effect on `[count]` value in any mode.

### Nvim version (nvim -v)

NVIM v0.13.0-dev-1929+g17f43325b1

### Vim (not Nvim) behaves the same?

No

### Operating system/version

EndeavourOS Linux x86_64, 7.2.11-arch1-1

### Terminal name/version

Ghostty 1.3.1-arch2

### $TERM environment variable

xterm-ghostty

body_text:
### Problem


`LspAttach` and `LspDetach` are too low-level to be used comfortably in user configs.

Most of the user-facing LSP API is server-agnostic. Take `vim.lsp.buf.definition()`: you don't tell it which server to ask. Neovim queries all attached servers that support `textDocument/definition` and decides what to do with the results. It's a high-level primitive.

However, [the recommended place](https://neovim.io/doc/user/lsp/#lsp-attach) to set up keymaps for these functions is the `LspAttach` autocommand, which is client-specific: it fires separately for **every** server that attaches to a buffer. A typical config that maps `gd` to `vim.lsp.buf.definition()` looks like this:

```lua
vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd('LspAttach', {
  callback = function(args)
    local bufnr = args.buf
    local client = vim.lsp.get_client_by_id(args.data.client_id)
    if client:supports_method('textDocument/definition', bufnr) then
      vim.keymap.set('n', 'gd', vim.lsp.buf.definition, { buf = bufnr })
    end
  end,
})
```

This approach has several problems:

1. **Redundant work.** `vim.keymap.set` runs every time a server that supports the method attaches. We only need to map `gd` once, because `vim.lsp.buf.definition()` doesn't care which server provides the result.

2. **It doesn't handle dynamic registration (`client/registerCapability`).** A server may register `textDocument/definition` after it has attached. In that case `supports_method()` returns `false` inside `LspAttach`, and the keymap is never created.

3. **Cleanup in `LspDetach` is unreasonably hard.** A user who wants to remove `gd` when the server goes away will naturally write:

```lua
   vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd('LspDetach', {
     callback = function(args)
       local bufnr = args.buf
       local client = vim.lsp.get_client_by_id(args.data.client_id)
       if client:supports_method('textDocument/definition', bufnr) then
         vim.keymap.del('n', 'gd', { buf = bufnr })
       end
     end,
   })
```

   This is wrong. Suppose two servers, `foo` and `bar`, are attached to the buffer and both support `textDocument/definition`. Running `:lsp disable foo` removes `gd`, even though `bar` is still attached and can still handle it.

   Doing this correctly requires tracking which attached clients support which methods per buffer (including dynamically registered ones), which is effectively a small framework. It can't be done in a few lines.

As a result, every user who wants a correct LSP setup has to carry the same boilerplate in their config. That boilerplate is hard to read and requires detailed knowledge of how Neovim and LSP servers interact under the hood.


### Expected behavior

Since `vim.lsp.buf` already provides server-agnostic functions that handle multiple servers internally, there should also be a server-agnostic event to go with them.

I propose a single `LspMethod` event that tracks whether a method is available in a buffer, regardless of which client provides it:

- it fires with `available = true` when the **first** client supporting the method becomes available in the buffer (via attach or `client/registerCapability`);
- it fires with `available = false` when the **last** client supporting the method stops providing it (via detach or `client/unregisterCapability`).

The autocmd pattern is the method name, and `args.data` contains `{ available: boolean }`:

```lua
vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd('LspMethod', {
  pattern = 'textDocument/definition',
  callback = function(args)
    if args.data.available then
      vim.keymap.set('n', 'gd', vim.lsp.buf.definition, { buf = args.buf })
    else
      vim.keymap.del('n', 'gd', { buf = args.buf })
    end
  end,
})
```

This fixes all three problems:

- the callback runs once per buffer and method, not once per client;
- dynamic registration is handled;
- cleanup is correct by construction.

In practice, configs rarely need the client object for anything except checking which methods it supports. With these events, buffer-local LSP setup could be expressed in terms of methods rather than clients, which matches how `vim.lsp.buf.*` already works.

networkx 3.7 and main (92f497e).

```python
import networkx as nx
G = nx.DiGraph()
G.add_node(0, demand=1)
G.add_node(1, demand=-1)
G.add_edge(1, 0, capacity=0, weight=1)

nx.network_simplex(G)   # raises NetworkXUnfeasible (correct)
nx.min_cost_flow(G)     # raises NetworkXUnfeasible (correct)
nx.capacity_scaling(G)  # returns (0, {0: {}, 1: {0: 0}}), no exception
```

The returned flow does not meet the demands (net flow 0 at both nodes vs demands 1 and -1). The graph is weakly connected and the demands sum to zero. The docstring says NetworkXUnfeasible is raised when "There is no flow satisfying all demand" (capacityscaling.py:228). A graph with the same two demands and no edges at all behaves the same way.

Cause: the "Residual network has no edges" early return (capacityscaling.py:297-300) fires before the excess check at capacityscaling.py:396-397, so the infeasibility is never detected.

(Found with the help of an AI code-auditing agent; I reran the reproducer above on 3.7.)

When hashing a directed graph using `weisfeiler_lehman_graph_hash` with an `edge_attr` supplied, the function silently drops the `s_` (successor) and `p_` (predecessor) prefixes on the edge labels

as a result, mathematically distinct directed graphs (such as an inward-pointing star and an outward-pointing star) incorrectly generate the exact same hash.

### Reproducer
```python
import networkx as nx

a = nx.DiGraph([(0, 1), (0, 2)]) # Outward star
b = nx.DiGraph([(1, 0), (2, 0)]) # Inward star

for graph in [a, b]:
    nx.set_edge_attributes(graph, "e", "label")

hash_a = nx.weisfeiler_lehman_graph_hash(a, edge_attr="label")
hash_b = nx.weisfeiler_lehman_graph_hash(b, edge_attr="label")

print("Hashes equal:", hash_a == hash_b)

body_text:
### Current Behavior

Calling `nx.percolation_centrality` on graphs with $n \le 2$ nodes (such as `nx.path_graph(2)`) crashes with an unhandled `ZeroDivisionError: division by zero`.

```text
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
  File "networkx/algorithms/centrality/percolation.py", line 112, in percolation_centrality
    percolation[v] *= 1 / (n - 2)
                      
ZeroDivisionError: division by zero

```

### Expected Behavior

For a graph with $n \le 2$ nodes, there can be no intermediary nodes on any shortest path between distinct pairs ($s \neq t \neq v$). Consistent with other centrality measures such as `nx.betweenness_centrality`, it should cleanly return `{0: 0.0, 1: 0.0}` (or `{}` for empty graphs) instead of raising `ZeroDivisionError`.

### Steps to Reproduce

```python
import networkx as nx

G = nx.path_graph(2)
nx.percolation_centrality(G)

```

### Environment

* Python version: 3.14.2
* NetworkX version: 3.7.1rc0.dev0 (main branch)
* OS: Windows 11

### Additional context

In `networkx/algorithms/centrality/percolation.py`:

The goal is to be able to browse these sites directly within NocoDB without having to leave the application. Describe alternatives you've considered I’ve tried resizing the current dashboard grid, but the widgets remain too small. I also tried various links, but many of them simply fail to display, making the dashboard less useful as a "single pane of glass" for my workflow. ### Additional context The goal is to use NocoDB Dashboards as a primary workstation where I can monitor both my data and external information sources (news, documentation, blogs) in one place, with a clear, full-sized view.

### Please confirm that the feature request does ***not*** already exist

- [x] I confirm there is no existing issue for this feature request.

### Use case

Currently the expanded record simply shows list of fields one after another.


### Suggested solution

It would be great if we can set the layout in the expanded record, like Twenty CRM or Nocobase:
- Two/three columns of fields (to easily see First Name, Last Name side by side and not one below another)
- Group certain fields in a collapsible widget like Twenty CRM (to hold similar or related fields together, can easily collapse and expand the widget)
- Widget to show the records of Associated Table (like Twenty CRM) if the table has LTAR (to view related Emails, Tasks, Notes, etc in the Expanded view of a record)
- And overall, customisable Tabs to store such columns, groups, widgets in the Expanded view

### Additional context

This would make Nocodb more versatile, and also currently Expanded Record view lacks customizations. You may add it in Business or Plus plan, that's okay. But it is definitely needed.

### Steps to reproduce

On a clean checkout of the `2026.09.0` release tag, following the repository's own bootstrap script:

```bash
git clone --depth 1 --branch 2026.09.0 https://github.com/nocodb/nocodb.git
cd nocodb
pnpm run bootstrap        # completes, exit 0
cd packages/nocodb
npx nest build            # exit 1
```

`bootstrap` succeeds. `nest build` fails with five errors, none of them in modified code:

```

### Please confirm that the feature request does ***not*** already exist

- [x] I confirm there is no existing issue for this feature request.

### Use case

In NocoDB dashboards, the "Number" widget displays a single aggregated value (count, sum, average, etc.) computed from one table/view. However, it is currently not possible to combine values coming from **different tables** into a single figure.

In many real-world setups, similar data is split across several tables (e.g. one table per country, per year, per business unit or per data source). To get a consolidated view at the dashboard level, we need to add these values together — and today this can only be done outside NocoDB (manually or via external tools), or by restructuring the data model, which is not always possible or desirable.

**Example:** a company operating in several West African countries, with one table per country:
- `Sales_Senegal`: SUM of `Amount` = 120,000 XOF
- `Sales_Cote_dIvoire`: SUM of `Amount` = 85,000 XOF
- `Sales_Mali`: SUM of `Amount` = 45,000 XOF
- `Sales_Burkina_Faso`: SUM of `Amount` = 30,000 XOF

Desired dashboard widgets:
1. **Addition of two numbers:** Senegal + Côte d'Ivoire = **205,000 XOF**
2. **Total of multiple numbers:** Senegal + Côte d'Ivoire + Mali + Burkina Faso = **280,000 XOF**

### Suggested solution

Add the ability to create a **"computed" Number widget** that combines the results of several aggregations, possibly from different tables. Two use cases should be covered:

1. **Addition of two Number values**
   A simple way to sum two sources, e.g. `{Widget A} + {Widget B}`, useful for quick comparisons or sub-totals (e.g. two countries, two periods, two product lines).

2. **Total of multiple Number values**
   A "Total" option where the user can select **any number of sources** (N tables / N widgets) and get their overall sum, useful for full consolidation (e.g. all countries of a region).

Possible implementation ideas:
- A new widget type (e.g. "Formula" or "Combined Number") where the user adds as many sources as needed, each with its own table, field, aggregation and filters.
- Optionally, allow referencing existing Number widgets on the same dashboard so users don't have to redefine each source.
- Supporting other basic operations (subtraction, multiplication, division, e.g. to compute ratios or a country's share of the total) would be a great bonus.

Filters applied at the dashboard level should ideally propagate to each underlying source when relevant.


### Additional context

This would make dashboards much more useful for **consolidated reporting** (multi-country, multi-period or multi-source KPIs) without requiring changes to the underlying schema or external BI tools.

Add the ability to create a **"computed" Number widget** that combines the results of several aggregations, possibly from different tables. Two use cases should be covered:

1. **Addition of two Number values**
   A simple way to sum two sources, e.g. `{Widget A} + {Widget B}`, useful for quick comparisons or sub-totals (e.g. two countries, two periods, two product lines).

2. **Total of multiple Number values**
   A "Total" option where the user can select **any number of sources** (N tables / N widgets) and get their overall sum, useful for full consolidation (e.g. all countries of a region).

Possible implementation ideas:
- A new widget type (e.g. "Formula" or "Combined Number") where the user adds as many sources as needed, each with its own table, field, aggregation and filters.
- Optionally, allow referencing existing Number widgets on the same dashboard so users don't have to redefine each source.
- Supporting other basic operations (subtraction, multiplication, division, e.g. to compute ratios or a country's share of the total) would be a great bonus.

Filters applied at the dashboard level should ideally propagate to each underlying source when relevant.


### Additional context

This would make dashboards much more useful for **consolidated reporting** (multi-country, multi-period or multi-source KPIs) without requiring changes to the underlying schema or external BI tools.

### Please confirm that the feature request does ***not*** already exist

- [x] I confirm there is no existing issue for this feature request.

### Use case

An operations table receives a staff identity through the records API as `Jane Example <person@example.com>`. We need to preserve both the known name and address and make the email clickable in NocoDB, without copying the address or rewriting the stored value as rich-text markup.

The current value is stored in a SingleLineText field. Retyping it as Email is not an equivalent solution: current Email rendering validates the complete string as a bare address, so the display-name form is not a clickable valid Email value.

### Suggested solution

Provide a supported named-email rendering mode that preserves the visible name/address, parses one mailbox from `Name <person@example.com>`, and preserves both the name and address in the composed recipient.

[RFC 6068](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6068) permits percent-encoded header values in a mailto URI. For example, the named recipient `Jane Example <person@example.com>` can be expressed through a `to` parameter:

```text
mailto:?to=Jane%20Example%20%3Cperson%40example.com%3E
```

The recipient directly after `mailto:` uses bare-address syntax; do not simply concatenate an unescaped display name there. Verify named-recipient handling across supported mail clients rather than assuming interoperability.

- Keep ordinary bare-address Email behavior unchanged.
- Preserve the supplied display name and stored value through editing, copy/paste, API reads/writes and export.
- Preserve the name and address in the composed To recipient; test names with Unicode, quotes, commas and URI-reserved characters using correct mailbox syntax and UTF-8 percent-encoding.
- Reject carriage returns/newlines and prevent header or query-parameter injection; do not add arbitrary recipients or message headers from cell content.
- Treat malformed, ambiguous or multi-mailbox strings conservatively; do not create arbitrary HTML or unsafe URI links.
- Apply the same behavior to normal and canvas-grid rendering, read-only/public surfaces as appropriate, and expanded cells.
- Document the supported syntax and column/rendering mode instead of silently weakening every Email validation rule.

### Additional context

#### Version/source evidence

The affected self-hosted deployment reports 2026.05.1 and offers 2026.09.1. Static comparison found the relevant Email renderer unchanged between those releases:

- [2026.05.1 Email renderer](https://github.com/nocodb/nocodb/blob/2026.05.1/packages/nc-gui/components/cell/Email/index.vue).
- [2026.09.1 Email renderer](https://github.com/nocodb/nocodb/blob/2026.09.1/packages/nc-gui/components/cell/Email/index.vue).
- [2026.09.1 Email validator](https://github.com/nocodb/nocodb/blob/2026.09.1/packages/nocodb-sdk/src/lib/columnHelper/utils/validation.ts).

The renderer creates a mailto link only when the whole value passes the bare-address validator. Paste extraction with Email validation enabled can extract only the address, which loses the display name rather than meeting this use case. Inspected canvas Email source follows the same whole-string contract.

#### Related changes and issues

A review of the past year's email/link-related release notes did not identify this feature. [2026.08.2 clickable lookup URLs](https://github.com/nocodb/nocodb/releases/tag/2026.08.2), [2026.09.0 rich-text workflow emails](https://github.com/nocodb/nocodb/releases/tag/2026.09.0), and [2026.09.1 variables in workflow email links](https://github.com/nocodb/nocodb/releases/tag/2026.09.1) concern other contracts.

Related #14450 and #12681 concern URL/formula lookup rendering, not a display-name mailbox. No exact duplicate was found in the bounded named-email/mailto/clickable search.

An explicit rich-text Markdown link is a different storage contract, not automatic named-email support. No schema change, upgrade or browser reproduction was performed; this request is based on the use case and tagged-source inspection.

### Use case

An operations table receives a staff identity through the records API as `Jane Example <person@example.com>`. We need to preserve both the known name and address and make the email clickable in NocoDB, without copying the address or rewriting the stored value as rich-text markup.

The current value is stored in a SingleLineText field. Retyping it as Email is not an equivalent solution: current Email rendering validates the complete string as a bare address, so the display-name form is not a clickable valid Email value.

### Suggested solution

Provide a supported named-email rendering mode that preserves the visible name/address, parses one mailbox from `Name <person@example.com>`, and preserves both the name and address in the composed recipient.

[RFC 6068](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6068) permits percent-encoded header values in a mailto URI. For example, the named recipient `Jane Example <person@example.com>` can be expressed through a `to` parameter:

```

The recipient directly after `mailto:` uses bare-address syntax; do not simply concatenate an unescaped display name there. Verify named-recipient handling across supported mail clients rather than assuming interoperability.

- Preserve the supplied display name and stored value through editing, copy/paste, API reads/writes and export.
- Preserve the name and address in the composed To recipient; test names with Unicode, quotes, commas and URI-reserved characters using correct mailbox syntax and UTF-8 percent-encoding.
- Reject carriage returns/newlines and prevent header or query-parameter injection; do not add arbitrary recipients or message headers from cell content.
- Treat malformed, ambiguous or multi-mailbox strings conservatively; do not create arbitrary HTML or unsafe URI links.

- [2026.09.1 Email renderer](https://github.com/nocodb/nocodb/blob/2026.09.1/packages/nc-gui/components/cell/Email/index.vue).
- [2026.09.1 Email validator](https://github.com/nocodb/nocodb/blob/2026.09.1/packages/nocodb-sdk/src/lib/columnHelper/utils/validation.ts).

### Please confirm that the feature request does ***not*** already exist

- [x] I confirm there is no existing issue for this feature request.

### Use case

Currently, NocoDB's Rich Text editor for Long Text fields does not support inserting or editing tables.

Tables are very useful for organizing structured information within a single record, such as research notes, comparisons, documentation, and other content that combines text with tabular data.

Since NocoDocs already supports tables, it would be great to have similar functionality in Rich Text fields as well, especially for users who primarily work with database records rather than standalone documents.

### Suggested solution

Add table support to the existing Rich Text editor for Long Text fields, ideally reusing the table functionality already available in NocoDocs where possible.

The expected functionality would include:

- Insert tables directly from the Rich Text toolbar.
- Edit table cells and add or remove rows and columns.
- Support pasting and rendering Markdown tables.
- Preserve table content when saving and reopening records.
- Render tables correctly in both Expanded Record and Expanded Cell views.

Since NocoDB already uses Tiptap-based editing functionality, it may be possible to reuse existing table extensions and components rather than implementing everything from scratch.

### Additional context

### Please confirm that the bug report does ***not*** already exist

- [x] I confirm there is no existing issue for this bug.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run self-hosted NocoDB `2026.09.1`.
2. Add an Anthropic AI integration and set the model to `claude-sonnet-5-5`.
3. Open AI chat and ask for something that goes to the builder specialist, e.g. "Create a table for tracking invoices".
4. NocoDB shows **"No output generated"**.

`claude-haiku-5-5` should avoid it, since it still accepts forced tool use.

**Why it happens**

Anthropic's newest models (`claude-opus-5-5`, `claude-sonnet-5-5`, `claude-fable-5-1`) reject forced tool use. A request with `tool_choice` set to `any` or `tool` gets a 400 straight away. The model never runs, so there is nothing to return.

NocoDB's structured output goes through the Vercel AI SDK. `generateObject()` in `packages/noco-integrations/core/src/ai/types.ts` calls `generateText` with `Output.object(...)`. When the provider doesn't know a model supports native structured output, it falls back to its `jsonTool` mode. That mode forces a tool call.

The lockfile pins `@ai-sdk/anthropic@3.0.9` (January 2026), both in the `2026.09.1` tag and on `develop`. That version predates these models.

The fix already exists upstream:

- `3.0.124` adds Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1 support. Forced tool choices fall back to `auto`, and `jsonTool` falls back to native structured outputs.
- `3.0.125` does the same for Sonnet 5.5.

Latest is `3.0.135`.

I couldn't check the chat agent code itself, since the specialist agents aren't in the public repo. If the builder sets `toolChoice` on its own, the SDK bump still stops the 400. It rewrites the call to `auto` and emits a warning. The agent should then verify that the tool was actually called.

### Desired Behavior

AI chat, including the builder specialist, works with `claude-sonnet-5-5`, `claude-opus-5-5` and `claude-fable-5-1`.

Suggested fix:

1. Bump `@ai-sdk/anthropic` to `>=3.0.125` (ideally latest) and refresh the lockfile.
2. Anywhere NocoDB forces a tool (`toolChoice: 'required'` or a named tool), switch to `auto` for these models. Use native structured outputs or strict tools when the output has to match a schema. Anthropic's docs recommend exactly that.

### Project Details

```
NocoDB version : 2026.09.1 (self-hosted)
AI integration : Anthropic (direct API key), model claude-sonnet-5-5
```

### What is the problem this feature will solve?

Would allow to dynamically create glob patterns from arbitrary paths.

Example:

```js
const pattern = `${path.escapeGlob(import.meta.dirname)}/*`;
```

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

Something similar in functionality to this:

```js
// Wraps symbols which open groups `{`, `[`, `(`, and
// those with semantics independent of groups `*`, `?`
path.escapeGlob = (x = "") => x.replace(/[*{[(?]/g, "[$&]");
```

And this:

```js
// inverse path.escapeGlob
path.unescapeGlob = (x = "") => x.replace(/\[.\]/g, "$&");
```

I was using #58988 as a reference for special chars.

### What alternatives have you considered?

Using a user land package everywhere dynamic glob creation is required, or even for everything glob related to keep things consistent.

Edit: Shortened regex replacement from `(...) -> $1` to `... -> $&`.

### Version

v24.13.0

### Platform

```text
Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0 x64
```

### Subsystem

_No response_

### What steps will reproduce the bug?

1. Run `node -e "for await (const c of process.stdin) console.log(c)"`
2. [f] [o] [o] [Enter]
3. [Ctrl] + [Z] or [Ctrl] + [D] (= EOF)
4. [Enter]




### How often does it reproduce? Is there a required condition?

Always

### What is the expected behavior? Why is that the expected behavior?

 In Ubuntu and Alma Node successfully stop reading by Ctrl + D:

```
$ node -e "for await (const c of process.stdin) console.log(c)"
foo
<Buffer 66 6f 6f 0a>
```

### What do you see instead?

Node will never stop reading in spite of [Ctrl] + [Z] or [Ctrl] + [D]:

```
PS> node -e "for await (const c of process.stdin) console.log(c)"
foo
<Buffer 66 6f 6f 0d 0a>
^Z
<Buffer 1a 0d 0a>
^D
<Buffer 04 0d 0a>
```

I had to end up with killing the process by Ctrl + C.

### Additional information

I usually use [Proto](https://moonrepo.dev/docs/proto/install) to manage Node versions, but it was able to be reproduced in the portable version in the official zipball:

```
PS> .\Downloads\node-v24.13.0-win-x64\node -e "for await (const c of process.stdin) console.log(c)"
foo
<Buffer 66 6f 6f 0d 0a>
^Z
<Buffer 1a 0d 0a>
^D
<Buffer 04 0d 0a>

PS> echo $?
False
```

(ended up with Ctrl + C)

Workaround: insert `if ((c[0] === 4 || c[0] === 0x1a) && c.length === 1 + EOL.length && c.toString("latin1", c.length - EOL.length) === EOL) break;` (`import { EOL } from "node:os"`)

If this bug did not exist, you would be able to retrieve the entire multiline text from stdin by  `(await Array.fromAsync(process.stdin)).join("")` in all platforms.

### Version

24.13.0

### Platform

```text
Have tried on these:
> Linux [hostname] 6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2 #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Thu Jun  5 18:30:46 UTC 2025 x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux
> Linux [hostname] 6.12.64-87.122.amzn2023.aarch64 #1 SMP Mon Jan 12 22:17:48 UTC 2026 aarch64 aarch64 aarch64 GNU/Linux
```

### Subsystem

tls

### What steps will reproduce the bug?

This is reproducible against mail.smtp2go.com on port 465.

Save the following as test.js and run with `node test.js`. After `socket.end()` is called, the process terminates due to an unhandled `'error'` event emitted by TLSSocket during TLS teardown.
```
const tls = require('tls');

const socket = tls.connect(465, 'mail.smtp2go.com', () => {
  console.log('TLS connected');

  socket.on('data', d => console.log('DATA:', d.toString()));
  socket.on('end', () => console.log('end'));
  socket.on('finish', () => console.log('finish'));

  setTimeout(() => {
    socket.end();
    console.log('socket.end() called');
  }, 3000);
});

setInterval(() => console.log('alive'), 1000);
```

### How often does it reproduce? Is there a required condition?

Every time, when the peer sends invalid (non‑TLS) after (or during?) TLS teardown.

### What is the expected behavior? Why is that the expected behavior?

After `tls.connect()` completes and `socket.end()` is called, I expected the process to continue running. Instead, the process exited with an "Unhandled 'error' event".

I am not certain whether this behavior is intentional, especially in light of the recent Node 24.13.0 security release, or an edge case in the TLS socket lifecycle.

### What do you see instead?

```
$ node test.js
TLS connected
DATA: 220 mail.smtp2go.com ESMTP Exim 4.99.1-S2G Sat, 07 Feb 2026 05:41:32 +0000

alive

socket.end() called
finish

      ^

    at TLSSocket._emitTLSError (node:_tls_wrap:1050:10)
    at TLSWrap.onerror (node:_tls_wrap:491:11) {
  library: 'SSL routines',
  reason: 'bad record type',
  code: 'ERR_SSL_BAD_RECORD_TYPE'
}

Node.js v24.13.0
```

### Additional information

To better understand the peer behavior involved, I verified the server interaction using OpenSSL.

Running the command `openssl s_client -connect mail.smtp2go.com:465 -quiet` followed by "QUIT" produced:
```
...
220 mail.smtp2go.com ESMTP Exim 4.99.1-S2G Sat, 07 Feb 2026 04:38:41 +0000
QUIT
221 mail.smtp2go.com closing connection
```

I also tested against a different SMTP server on port 465, which did not exhibit this behavior and it did not trigger the unhandled 'error' event in Node.

### What is the problem this feature will solve?

node.js supports running a subset of typescript nativly, but for _reasons_ doesn't allow this feature for files in node_modules.

A positive caveat is that node wants to support npm workspaces, where local sub packages are required thru node_modules. To do so it checks the real path of the file, and will type strip it if it's not within node_modules.

This also works in pnpm workspaces, but breaks in `pnpm deploy`. [This repo demonstrates that behavior.](https://github.com/everett1992/pnpm-node-type-stripping)

Read or run `repro.sh` steps to reproduce.

This difference between workspace and deploy structure
```
bin/node_modules/lib -> ../../lib
out/node_modules/lib -> .pnpm/lib@file++++lib/node_modules/lib
```

cause this error in out/index.ts, but not bin/index.ts

```
Error [ERR_UNSUPPORTED_NODE_MODULES_TYPE_STRIPPING]: Stripping types is currently unsupported for files under node_modules, for "file:///out/node_modules/.pnpm/lib@file++++lib/node_modules/lib/index.ts"
```

This would also break in npm, pnpm and other dependency managers that use `install-links` or other steps that indirect the workspace dependencies into node_modules.


### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

Either remove the node_modules restriction, add more detection's for 'local node_modules' cases - such as private: true or a new marker, or establish export conditions for type stripping.

I am okay with emitting `.js` and using it in my deployed app, but I want to use `.ts` in development, and I don't want dev tools to require possibly stale `.js` files.

I think a reasonable solution is an export condition for 'type stripping not supported' that node would use to fallback to .js instead of erroring.

```
"exports": {
  "unsupportedTypeStripping": "out/index.js",
  "default": "src/index.ts",
}
```
  

### What alternatives have you considered?

## Summary
Cross-building Node.js for `--dest-cpu=arm` (32-bit ARM / armhf) from an x64 Linux host fails in V8 host object compilation due to a host/target architecture guard in `deps/v8/include/v8config.h`.

## Environment
- Host: Ubuntu 24.04 x86_64
- Target: Raspberry Pi 3, 32-bit Raspbian Buster (armhf)
- Cross toolchain: `arm-linux-gnueabihf-*`

## Repro
From x64 host:

```bash
./configure \
  --dest-os=linux \
  --dest-cpu=arm \
  --cross-compiling \
  --with-arm-float-abi=hard \
  --with-arm-fpu=neon \
  --without-node-snapshot
make -j1
```

## Failure
Host V8 compilation fails with:

```text
#error Target architecture arm is only supported on arm and ia32 host
```

Coming from `deps/v8/include/v8config.h`:

```c
#if (V8_TARGET_ARCH_ARM && !(V8_HOST_ARCH_IA32 || V8_HOST_ARCH_ARM))
#error Target architecture arm is only supported on arm and ia32 host
#endif
```

In generated host makefiles (for example `out/tools/v8_gypfiles/v8_libplatform.host.mk`), host objects are compiled with `-DV8_TARGET_ARCH_ARM`, which triggers this guard on x64 hosts.

## Notes
- `--without-node-snapshot` does not avoid this, as host V8 objects are still built with ARM target macros.
- A local workaround changing the guard to include x64 host allows compilation to proceed:

```diff
-#if (V8_TARGET_ARCH_ARM && !(V8_HOST_ARCH_IA32 || V8_HOST_ARCH_ARM))
+#if (V8_TARGET_ARCH_ARM && !(V8_HOST_ARCH_IA32 || V8_HOST_ARCH_ARM || V8_HOST_ARCH_X64))
```

## Request
What is the intended/supported path for x64-host -> arm-target cross-builds in current Node/V8?

If this should be supported, could build generation be adjusted so host-side V8 tools/objects do not fail this guard (or guard logic updated in a supported way)?

### Version

v25.6.1

### Subsystem

node:test

### What steps will reproduce the bug?

Add the `todo`, `skip` or `testFailure` option to a test, setting it to an empty string. The result will be the same as if you set it to `true` or a non-empty string.

### What is the expected behavior? Why is that the expected behavior?

Unsure whether the bug is in the code or in the API docs.

The code clearly does not treat these options as truthy:
https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/2de34822cc9a19621a663e3f22b00b9a01697635/lib/internal/test_runner/test.js#L639-L641

But the docs specifically state they should be:

https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/2de34822cc9a19621a663e3f22b00b9a01697635/doc/api/test.md?plain=1#L1691-L1696

### Additional information

Previous discussions:
- Three years ago: https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/47537#pullrequestreview-1383887199 @ljharb 
- More recently as part of `expectFailure` development: https://github.com/nodejs/test-runner/pull/10#discussion_r2739831598 @JakobJingleheimer

_No response_

### What steps will reproduce the bug?

### Context

Hi, I have small TS loader for Node.js:
https://github.com/krutoo/ts-loader

I use it like:

```
npm i ts-loader@npm:@krutoo/ts-loader
node --import ts-loader ./test.ts
```

You can see real example with issue here:
https://github.com/krutoo/utils/pull/212

Under the hood loader just runs http server in first process and registers hooks by `module.register`

Hooks uses `fetch` to request server to complie modules

### Problem

After upgrade to Node.js 24.12.0 server don't answer any requests, even from browser, there is tab that waits for response

I don't have skills to figure out the cause myself.

Tried log some steps, seems the server isn't accepting any incoming requests at all.

Even though the server itself has definitely been created, has taken over the port, and is accepting messages. 

Can someone help to understand cause of this behavior?

### How often does it reproduce? Is there a required condition?

Clone this repo and branch:
https://github.com/krutoo/utils/tree/tsimp-replaced


Then:

```sh
nvm install 24.12.0

npm use 24.12.0

npm i

npm run test
```

### What is the expected behavior? Why is that the expected behavior?

Don't have enough skills to understand it is a bug or new behavior of async loader hooks

### What do you see instead?

Tests freezes

## What happened?

Node.js processes crash with exit code `-1073740791` (`0xC0000409` / `STATUS_STACK_BUFFER_OVERRUN`) within 20-70 seconds of startup when running a non-trivial application (WebSocket server with HTTP, Telegram bot polling, and plugin system) on Windows 11 Insider (Canary channel).

The crash is caused by V8's **Maglev** JIT compiler tier. Workaround: `--no-maglev` flag eliminates the crash entirely.

## Reproduction

**Environment:**
- Node.js: v25.8.0
- V8: 14.1.146.11-node.20
- OS: Windows 11 Pro for Workstations, Insider Canary build **10.0.26200.0**
- Arch: x64

**Steps:**
1. Run a long-lived Node.js application that uses `fetch()`, WebSocket, and timers on Windows 11 Insider build 26200
2. Process crashes with exit code `-1073740791` (0xC0000409) within 20-70 seconds
3. No JavaScript stack trace — the crash is in native JIT-compiled code via `__fastfail`

**Flags tested:**

| Flag | Crash? | `fetch()` works? |
|------|--------|------------------|
| (none) | **Yes** — crashes in 20-70s | Yes |
| `--jitless` | No | **No** — undici fetch broken |
| **`--no-maglev`** | **No** | **Yes** |
| `--no-turbofan` | No | Yes |

`--no-maglev` is the minimal workaround — disabling only the Maglev tier prevents the crash while keeping TurboFan and fetch() functional.

**Additional context:**
- A bare Node.js HTTP server (`http.createServer`) does NOT crash — the issue requires enough code to trigger Maglev optimization
- Crash bypasses Windows Error Reporting (`__fastfail` / SEH)
- Windows Event Viewer shows the Insider build has kernel-level instability (BlueScreen events, VIDEO_ENGINE_TIMEOUT_DETECTED), suggesting stricter CFG enforcement
- The same application runs without issues on Windows Server 2019 and stable Windows builds

## Expected behavior

Node.js should not crash with STATUS_STACK_BUFFER_OVERRUN. Maglev-compiled code should respect Windows CFG/CET enforcement on Insider builds.

## Workaround

Pass `--no-maglev` as a command-line flag (cannot be set via `NODE_OPTIONS`):

```
node --no-maglev app.js
```

body_text:
### What is the problem this feature will solve?

We currently have a significant number of users of Alpine Linux (Linux using musl as its libc implementation).  For the direct tarballs from the unofficial builds server there are approximately 1000 downloads per hour for x64 plus about 25 per hour for arm.  We do not currently have the figures for the container images on dockerhub but I would expect it to be quite high too.

Given the number of people using this build, I feel there is some justification for releasing this through the normal processes so it is made available in the same timescales as the other tier 1/2 platforms.  This would allow security updates to be made available in a timely manner, and also help to reduce any lag visible to customers caused by delays to the release of the container images in the docker-node project which is currently gated by availability of alpine builds (I will also note that there is a [proposal to decouple Alpine](https://github.com/nodejs/docker-node/pull/2348), but that would not solve the problem of potentially having a delay in getting updates into the hands of our Alpine users)

We should also bear in mind  that it is quite likely that many users are not aware that Alpine is in experimental status and do not understand the implications of using this platform in production.  While it may be clear to
someone pulling it form the unofficial-builds server - the clue being in the hostname - when viewed on dockerhub it [does not look any different to the other platforms](https://github.com/nodejs/docker-node/issues/2011#issuecomment-3813471009) which shipped as "official" container images.

Superficially I would hope that it would be a low risk to add Alpine as the Linux/glibc on x64/aarch64 platforms are well-supported and any likely risk would be around its use of musl instead of the GNU libc. I'm not sure if we've ever hit any problems so far because of that difference but I don't recall anything.

Noting that Alpine/x64 is already part of the regular CI testing and therefore failures on that platform will get noticed, but as an experimental platform any CI failures would not currently block a release cycle.

While I'm not considering it as part of this proposal, I will state for background information that we have previously had Alpine/ppc64le and Alpine/s390x container images published by the docker-node project.  Alpine/ppc64le was discontinued in the node 22 time frame and I am proposing [doing the same for
Alpine/s390x](https://github.com/nodejs/docker-node/pull/2462).


### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

Promote the Alpine builds from Experimental to Tier 2 so that it is a formal part of the release cycle.  This would be at least for the x64 architecture as a minimum, but possibly also arm64.

**For this we would want to have some commitment from at least one contributor willing to actively keep up to date with any problems on the platform so in part this is a call for volunteers to be able to handle any failures and ensure that new features can be enabled successfully on the platform.**  Typically we have found that when problems show up they do get looked at fairly quickly if people spot that the unofficial builds for Alpine are not generated properly.  This change would also mean that the environment used in the CI for testing and the build environment would be consistent (Unofficial build environments are not automatically kept in sync with the  systems for the equivalent platform in the CI and in fact the compilers used are currently not the same)

We have some Alpine/x64 systems in the CI but would need to evaluate capacity and also add extra systems for arm64 if we chose to promote that Alpine architecture out of experimental status too.

_Regardless of whether we choose to promote Alpine, should we perhaps have a github platform team created of interested parties that can be tagged if any issues show up?_


### What alternatives have you considered?

- Leave it as-is - an experimental platform with no formal support.

- Put more disclaimers on the existing experimental builds which are shipped as "official" container images to dockerhub (either have it more obvious on the dockerhub UI, or build it in such a way that it puts some notice to the console on startup)

- As far as options we also have the choice to do this for just x64 or also arm.  I believe Alpine is now quite popular on the desktop for the many developers now using arm Mac desktop systems so this can also be discussed in this issue.  I will also note that if we included arm64 we would likely add native arm64 machines in, as opposed to the current cross-compiled one on the unofficial-builds server however I will point out that we do not currently test Alpine/arm in the CI.

FYI @nodejs/build @targos @mcollina and maybe @RafaelGSS who has seen the impacts of Alpine being an experimental platform when the docker images don't always get published quickly.

The current list of platforms and their support category is listed in https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/main/BUILDING.md#platform-list

A couple of previous discussions on the topic of platform tiers:
- https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/8265 (Note: From 2016 but referenced the original addition of Alpine to the docker-node project!)
- https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/43457 (Mostly ref: Smartos)

### What is the problem this feature will solve?

The process title can only be set via [`proccess.title`](https://nodejs.org/api/process.html#processtitle). Problems with it:

- Setter APIs like it are weird and legacy, it's a side-effect that may look like a code smell
- Doesn't work with destructuring, setter is not triggered:
  ```ts
  import {title} from "node:process";
  title = "title";
  ```

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

```ts
import {setTitle} from "node:process";
setTitle("title");
```

### What alternatives have you considered?

None available

### Version

v24.15.0 (also v25 per anthropics/claude-code#53660 measurements)

### Platform

Darwin (macOS 26.4.1, Apple Silicon Mac16,12). Reproduces on macOS Sonoma/Sequoia per the linked downstream reports.

### Subsystem

tls, crypto

### What steps will reproduce the bug?

On a Mac with any active network-flow filter (corporate NetworkExtension, content filter, or even a userland VPN-style daemon like ZeroTier), and a moderately-sized login keychain:

```bash
$ node -e 'const t0=process.hrtime.bigint();
           const c = require("tls").getCACertificates("system");
           console.log(`returned=${c.length} elapsed=${(Number(process.hrtime.bigint()-t0)/1e6).toFixed(0)}ms`)'
returned=34 elapsed=5287ms
```

The same call against `"bundled"` returns in ~0.1ms. HTTPS request times via `--use-system-ca` are ~100× slower than `--use-bundled-ca` (5093ms vs 103ms to `api.github.com`).

The bug is in `node::crypto::ReadMacOSKeychainCertificates` (`src/crypto/crypto_x509.cc` / wherever the macOS branch lives). It calls `SecTrustEvaluateWithError` with a revocation-enabled policy when *collecting trust anchors*, which causes `trustd` to attempt AIA/OCSP/CRL fetches for every cert. When a NetworkExtension content filter is present, each flow goes through per-flow cryptographic signing (~1-2ms × hundreds of certs = 5-10 seconds total) before being denied. Without a flow filter the cost is smaller but still present.

### How often does it reproduce?

Every invocation. Stable across reboots and Node versions in the v24.x / v25 line.

### What is the expected behavior? Why is that the expected behavior?

`tls.getCACertificates("system")` should be fast (single-digit milliseconds for a typical keychain) because it's collecting trust anchors, not validating a server chain. Revocation checks are pointless during anchor collection — a trust anchor's revocation status is determined by user/admin trust settings, not by an OCSP responder.

### What do you see instead?

5-10+ seconds of latency, predominantly in synchronous XPC round-trips to `trustd`. Effectively blocks Node CLI startup any time the CLI's CA loader touches the system store. Several Node-based CLIs are affected in practice:

- **anthropics/claude-code#53660** — comprehensive root-cause analysis. Their measurement on a corporate Mac: 9.7s for 18 certs (530ms/cert), vs 0.3ms/cert for direct C calls using `SecPolicyCreateBasicX509`. They shipped a `CLAUDE_CODE_CERT_STORE=bundled` env var workaround.
- **github/copilot-cli#3330** *(filing concurrently)* — same call costs 5+ seconds on every `copilot` invocation. The CLI's code explicitly asks for `"system"` certs in addition to `"bundled"`.
- **github/copilot-cli#1250** — Windows variant of the same call (different failure mode, same offending line).

### Additional information

#### Proposed fix

Per the anthropics/claude-code#53660 analysis, the call should use `SecPolicyCreateBasicX509()` (no revocation) when enumerating system CAs to use as trust anchors. Alternatively, the function could skip trust evaluation entirely and call `SecTrustSettingsCopyCertificates(kSecTrustSettingsDomainAdmin/System)` to collect anchors without validation. Either approach removes revocation from the hot startup path.

#### Reproducer kit

```bash
# Standalone measurement
node -e 'const t0=process.hrtime.bigint();
         require("tls").getCACertificates("system");
         console.log(`${(Number(process.hrtime.bigint()-t0)/1e6).toFixed(0)}ms`)'

# HTTPS A/B
node --use-bundled-ca -e 'require("https").get("https://api.github.com/zen",r=>r.on("data",()=>{}).on("end",()=>{}))'   # ~100ms
node --use-system-ca  -e 'require("https").get("https://api.github.com/zen",r=>r.on("data",()=>{}).on("end",()=>{}))'   # ~5s

# Sample to confirm the syscall pattern
node --use-system-ca -e 'require("tls").getCACertificates("system")' &
PID=$!; sleep 0.1; sample $PID 3 -mayDie
```

Sample output during the wait deterministically shows:
```
node::crypto::ReadMacOSKeychainCertificates
  → node::crypto::IsCertificateTrustedForPolicy
    → SecTrustEvaluateWithError
      → securityd_send_sync_and_do (XPC to trustd)
```

#### Why this matters beyond corporate networks

Anthropic's analysis (and the original v24 design assumption) treats this as a "corporate Macs only" problem. In practice, **any userland flow-handling daemon** — ZeroTier, Tailscale, Cloudflare WARP, certain VPN clients — places similar code in the path. The fix doesn't depend on detecting the filter; it's simply correct to skip revocation when enumerating trust anchors.

#### Related Node-side tracking

- #58990 — tracking issue for custom CA support; lists "Load system CA certificates off thread" as done, but off-thread loading doesn't fix the cost, only moves it. The root cause is the revocation policy.
- #57163 — `--use-system-ca` intermediate-cert issues on Windows.
- #58346 — request for env-var alternative to `--use-system-ca`.

The bug is in `node::crypto::ReadMacOSKeychainCertificates` (`src/crypto/crypto_x509.cc` / wherever the macOS branch lives). It calls `SecTrustEvaluateWithError` with a revocation-enabled policy when *collecting trust anchors*, which causes `trustd` to attempt AIA/OCSP/CRL fetches for every cert. When a NetworkExtension content filter is present, each flow goes through per-flow cryptographic signing (~1-2ms × hundreds of certs = 5-10 seconds total) before being denied. Without a flow filter the cost is smaller but still present.

### How often does it reproduce?

Every invocation. Stable across reboots and Node versions in the v24.x / v25 line.

### What is the expected behavior? Why is that the expected behavior?

`tls.getCACertificates("system")` should be fast (single-digit milliseconds for a typical keychain) because it's collecting trust anchors, not validating a server chain. Revocation checks are pointless during anchor collection — a trust anchor's revocation status is determined by user/admin trust settings, not by an OCSP responder.

### What do you see instead?

5-10+ seconds of latency, predominantly in synchronous XPC round-trips to `trustd`. Effectively blocks Node CLI startup any time the CLI's CA loader touches the system store. Several Node-based CLIs are affected in practice:

- **anthropics/claude-code#53660** — comprehensive root-cause analysis. Their measurement on a corporate Mac: 9.7s for 18 certs (530ms/cert), vs 0.3ms/cert for direct C calls using `SecPolicyCreateBasicX509`. They shipped a `CLAUDE_CODE_CERT_STORE=bundled` env var workaround.
- **github/copilot-cli#3330** *(filing concurrently)* — same call costs 5+ seconds on every `copilot` invocation. The CLI's code explicitly asks for `"system"` certs in addition to `"bundled"`.
- **github/copilot-cli#1250** — Windows variant of the same call (different failure mode, same offending line).

### Additional information

#### Proposed fix

Per the anthropics/claude-code#53660 analysis, the call should use `SecPolicyCreateBasicX509()` (no revocation) when enumerating system CAs to use as trust anchors. Alternatively, the function could skip trust evaluation entirely and call `SecTrustSettingsCopyCertificates(kSecTrustSettingsDomainAdmin/System)` to collect anchors without validation. Either approach removes revocation from the hot startup path.

#### Reproducer kit

```bash
# Standalone measurement
node -e 'const t0=process.hrtime.bigint();
         require("tls").getCACertificates("system");
         console.log(`${(Number(process.hrtime.bigint()-t0)/1e6).toFixed(0)}ms`)'

# HTTPS A/B
node --use-bundled-ca -e 'require("https").get("https://api.github.com/zen",r=>r.on("data",()=>{}).on("end",()=>{}))'   # ~100ms
node --use-system-ca  -e 'require("https").get("https://api.github.com/zen",r=>r.on("data",()=>{}).on("end",()=>{}))'   # ~5s

# Sample to confirm the syscall pattern
node --use-system-ca -e 'require("tls").getCACertificates("system")' &
PID=$!; sleep 0.1; sample $PID 3 -mayDie
```

Sample output during the wait deterministically shows:
```
node::crypto::ReadMacOSKeychainCertificates
  → node::crypto::IsCertificateTrustedForPolicy
    → SecTrustEvaluateWithError
      → securityd_send_sync_and_do (XPC to trustd)
```

#### Why this matters beyond corporate networks

Anthropic's analysis (and the original v24 design assumption) treats this as a "corporate Macs only" problem. In practice, **any userland flow-handling daemon** — ZeroTier, Tailscale, Cloudflare WARP, certain VPN clients — places similar code in the path. The fix doesn't depend on detecting the filter; it's simply correct to skip revocation when enumerating trust anchors.

#### Related Node-side tracking

- #58990 — tracking issue for custom CA support; lists "Load system CA certificates off thread" as done, but off-thread loading doesn't fix the cost, only moves it. The root cause is the revocation policy.
- #57163 — `--use-system-ca` intermediate-cert issues on Windows.
- #58346 — request for env-var alternative to `--use-system-ca`.

```text

```

### Subsystem

sqlite

### What steps will reproduce the bug?

node:sqlite's `backup()` checks that its first argument is an object, then unwraps it. Passing anything other than a `DatabaseSync` results in a crash:

```js
const { backup } = require('node:sqlite');
backup({}, '/tmp/c1a.db');
```

Similarly, the `DatabaseSync` constructor treats any object as a `URL` if it has a string `href`. If that `href` doesn't parse, it crashes:

```js
const { DatabaseSync } = require('node:sqlite');
new DatabaseSync({ href: 'zzz' });
```

### How often does it reproduce? Is there a required condition?

It's consistent.

### What is the expected behavior? Why is that the expected behavior?

Both should raise a `TypeError`.

### What do you see instead?

A segfault.

### Version
v26.7.0

### Platform
Linux x64

### Subsystem
fs / src/node_file.cc

### What steps will reproduce the bug?

```js
const fs = require('node:fs');
fs.mkdirSync('a/b', { recursive: true });
try {
  fs.rmSync('a/.', { recursive: true, force: true });
} catch (err) {
  console.log('code   :', JSON.stringify(err.code));
  console.log('errno  :', err.errno);
  console.log('syscall:', err.syscall);
  console.log('message:', err.message);
}
```

Output:

```
code   : ""
errno  : -4094
syscall: "rm"
message: , Unknown error: Invalid argument 'a/.'
```

### What is the expected behavior? Why is that the expected behavior?

`err.code` should be `'EINVAL'` and `err.errno` should be `-22`. The underlying
failure is a plain `EINVAL` from `rmdir(2)`, which POSIX requires for a path whose
final component is `.`.

Every other `fs` error carries a usable `code`, and `err.code === 'EINVAL'` is the
documented way to branch on `fs` failures, so an empty string breaks ordinary error
handling. The message is also malformed: it begins with `, ` because the empty code
is interpolated into it.

### What do you see instead?

`errno` is `-4094` (`UV_UNKNOWN`) and `code` is the empty string.

### Additional information

This is not specific to `EINVAL`. `RmSync()` in `src/node_file.cc` translates the
`std::error_code` from `std::filesystem::remove_all()` with a hardcoded chain that
covers four values:

* `operation_not_permitted` -> `EPERM`
* `directory_not_empty` -> `ENOTEMPTY`
* `not_a_directory` -> `ENOTDIR`
* `permission_denied` -> `EACCES` (`EPERM` on Windows)

Anything else falls through to the tail of the function:

```c++
std::string message = "Unknown error: " + error.message();
return env->ThrowErrnoException(
    UV_UNKNOWN, "rm", message.c_str(), path_c_str);
```

So the mapping is an allowlist rather than a translation, and any errno outside
those four surfaces as `UV_UNKNOWN` with an empty `code`. `EINVAL` is simply the
one that is easiest to trigger from user code.

The async form is unaffected, because `fs.rm()` and `fsPromises.rm()` use the JS
`rimraf` and report `EINVAL` correctly.

Noting for context that the dot segment handling in #61958 is being addressed
separately at the JS layer. That change stops `a/.` from reaching this code path,
but it does not fix the mapping, which stays reachable for other errnos.

### Version

### Platform

```text
Linux aarch64-unknown-linux-musl 7.2.3-gentoo-dist-hardened #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Sat Sep  5 05:15:30 CEST 2026 aarch64 GNU/Linux

llvm stack (clang, libcxx, compiler-rt, libunwind)
```

### Subsystem

_No response_

### What steps will reproduce the bug?

```
$ ./configure
$ make
```

### How often does it reproduce? Is there a required condition?

always

### What is the expected behavior? Why is that the expected behavior?

build succeeds

### What do you see instead?

```bash
ld.lld: error: unable to find library -latomic
clang++: error: linker command failed with exit code 1 (use -v to see invocation)
make[1]: *** [node_js2c.target.mk:144: /home/pepper/dev/ghrepos/node/out/Release/node_js2c] Error 1
make: *** [Makefile:145: node] Error 2
```

### Additional information



This [comment in tools/v8_gypfiles/v8.gyp](https://github.com/peppergrayxyz/node/blob/b949c28b7957f913bfbf042e6b07a22af59f1f3f/tools/v8_gypfiles/v8.gyp#L1404-L1407) suggests, that `-latomic` was added to facilitate the use of atomic operations as described in the linked clang docs:
```gyp
# Platforms that don't have Compare-And-Swap (CAS) support need to link atomic library
# to implement atomic memory access.
# Clang needs it for some atomic operations (https://clang.llvm.org/docs/Toolchain.html#atomics-library).
 ['(OS=="linux" and clang==1) or (v8_current_cpu in ["mips64", "mips64el", "arm", "riscv64", "loong64"])', {
```

But the docs also state that `compiler-rt` (LLVM) **or** `libatomic` (GNU) may be used. `-latomic` requests `libatomic` while atomics from `compiler-rt` can be used without linker settings.

**Current behaviour** 
The builds adds `-latomic` which unconditionally requests to link `libatomic` even in cases when it is not needed or desired.

**Desired behaviour**
Check if `-latomic` is needed e.g. like mesa [meson.build](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/-/blob/main/meson.build?ref_type=heads#L1639), which checks if atomics compile successfully without link settings (which is the case with  `compiler-rt`). Then append them conditionally only when needed.
